Course Descriptions Introductory Notes

1. The Accounting Group is expert encing tremendous demand for its courses beyond available resources. Thus, accessibility to Accounting courses cannot be guaranteed to all students. Accounting courses

. numbered 300 and higher are normally restricted to students who require these courses as part of their undergraduate program. if space permits, students in good standing in an Honours program may be admitted, subject to prerequisite requiremenis.
Courses. Descriptions Accounting —
2. Courses or sections with the suffix A (e.g. ACC 341A) are restricted to students in the Honours Accounting program.
3. The minimum grade required to Satisfy a prerequisite for courses labelleci ACC is C-.
4. Students may only repeat courses labelled ACC in which they have a grade of D+ or less.

courses.label: ACC 101
courses.title: Introductory Accounting 1
paras: An introduction to the principles and practices underlying the historical-cost income determination model. Restricted to students required by their program to take ACC 101, or to students registered in ECON 107 and ACC 131. a

courses.label: ACC 121
courses.title: Understanding and Using Financial Accounting Information
paras: This course is designed for nonaccounting majors to help them understand and analyze financial statements.

courses.label: ACC 122
courses.title: Understanding and Using Managerial
paras: Accounting information This course is designed for nonaccounting majors. The use of accounting information to assist in planning, control and managerial decisionmaking will be examined.
Prereq: ACC 121

courses.label: ACC 131
courses.title: Management 1/2
paras: The functional areas of business: finance, personne! administration,’ Production, marketing and accounting are examined within differing organizational structures, Coverage also includes study of the principles of effective management and the financial system in Canada as a source of corporate capital.
Prereq: ACC 131 is a prerequisite for "ACC 132

courses.label: ACC 231
courses.title: Business Law
paras: Particular attention is given to the law relating to contracts and business organizations. Other areas of study include sources of law, the judicial process, real and personal property, torts, agency, credit, and negotiable instruments.

courses.label: ACC 281
courses.title: Introductory Managerial Accounting
paras: An introdliction to the principles and Practices of managerial accounting. Prereq: ACC 101

courses.label: ACC 291
courses.title: Financial Accounting 1
paras: A first course in intermediate financial
accounting dealing with the theory and
Practice of financial statement prepara-
tion and reporting. The emphasis will be
on asset valuation and the related
impact on income measurement. Prereq: ACC 261

courses.label: ACC 341
courses.title: Computer Applications in Business
paras: An introduction to the operation of mainframe and microcomputer systems. Emphasis will be placed on software packages that have particular application to accounting transaction processing and financial planning. Prereq: Registration in Year 3 of any Faculty of Arts Accounting program

courses.label: ACC 351
courses.title: Auditing 1
paras: An examination of the standards developed by the accounting profession which guide professional accountants in performing the attest function. Elements of effective control structures and the concept of audit evidence are examined.
Prereq: ACC 291

courses.label: ACC 371
courses.title: Managerial Finance 1
paras: Analytic techniques for financial decision-making will be considered within a conceptual framework. Emphasis is placed upon the long-term investment, capital structure and distribution decisions. Developments in capital asset pricing, and efficient markets will be examined.
Prereq: ECON 101 or 102, 221 and ACC 291 or registration in AP1

courses.label: ACC 372
courses.title: Managerial Finance 2
paras: The theoretical concepts examined in Accounting 371 will be apptied within the context of the Canadian economy. Topics examined will include interest rate determination, capital markets, and tisk/return characteristics of financing alternatives.
Prereq: ACC 371

courses.label: ACC 381
courses.title: Managerial Accounting 1
paras: The development and use of accounting information in performing the managerial functions of planning, controlling, decision making and performance evaiuation. Emphasis is on analysis of costs rather than procedural aspects of costing systems.
Prereq: ACC 291 and a course in Statistics

courses.label: ACC 382
courses.title: Managerial Accounting 2
paras: Consideration of more complex topics in management planning and control. Emphasis is on cost accumulation systems, control models and applications of quantitative methods to management accounting.
Prereq: ACC 381

courses.label: ACC 392
courses.title: Financial Accounting
paras: This course completes the coverage of intermediate financial accounting. It deals with problems related to the measurement of liabilities, accounting for income taxes and the reporting and measuring of corporate equities.
Prereq: ACC 291

courses.label: ACC 401
courses.title: Accounting Theory
paras: A review of accounting theory as a background for applying underlying concepts to current accounting problems. Emphasis is on current literature, with a major term paper required. Prereq: ACC 292 and 371

courses.label: ACC 402
courses.title: Research
paras: An introduction to research methodology
and current research in accounting. Prereq: Registration in AP3 and ACC -
ACC 4144/B WS 0.0/0.5 Special Topics °
Prereq: Admission by consent of instructor.

courses.label: ACC 415
courses.title: Special Topics
paras: Admission by consent of instructor.

courses.label: ACC 431
courses.title: Management Decisions
paras: A case course that examines the accountant's participation in such functional areas as marketing and production. Students are involved in policy and strategy formulation, in evaluation of the impact of government regulation and policy.
Prereq: Registration in AP3

courses.label: ACC 441
courses.title: Accounting Information Systems
paras: Investigates the concepts and principles of management information systems. Concentration is on the role of accounting information in the pianning/ decision-making process and the design and implementation of accounting information systems.
Prereq: ACC 381 1

courses.label: ACC 443
courses.title: Models for Decision Making
paras: This course deals with modelling as an approach to problem solving and decision making. Problems of credibility, verification and implementation of models are considered and illustrated by application to problems encountered in management and accounting.
Prereq: Registration in AP3

courses.label: ACC 451
courses.title: Auditing 2
paras: An examination of the elements involved in the determination of the extent of audit testing. Quantitative models will be employed in developing and evaluating examination samples.
Prereq: Registration in AP3

courses.label: ACC 452
courses.title: Auditing 3
paras: An examination of current topics affecting public accounting practice. Topics will also include legal, ethical and statutory guidelines.
Prereq: Registration in AP3 and ACC 451 .

courses.label: ACC 453
courses.title: Computer Control and Audit
paras: The evaiuation of controls in a comput-
erized environment, the impact of the
computer on the audit approach and
the utilization of the computer in
conducting audit testing are considered. Prereq: Registration in AP3 and ACC

courses.label: ACC 454
courses.title: Operational Auditing
paras: An extension of the basic audit to
include the appraisal and establishment
of administrative and operational
controls; and the evaluation of the effi-
ciency of individual business functions. Prereq: Registration in AP3

courses.label: ACC 461
courses.title: Taxation 1
paras: A course in the interpretation in application of the major provisions of the Income Tax Act through an analysis of court decisions, Revenue Canada’s publications, and practical problem situations.
Prereq: ACC 292 or registration in AP!

courses.label: ACC 462
courses.title: Taxation 2
paras: A continuation of ACC 461. Prereq: ACC 461

courses.label: ACC 463
courses.title: Taxation 3
paras: A course which integrates the topics covered in ACC 461 and 462 for individual and corporate tax planning through a study of trusts, partnerships, corporate reorganizations and estate planning. i
Prereq: ACC 462 and registration in AP3

courses.label: ACC 464
courses.title: Taxation: Business and Property
paras: income .
An in-depth study of the computation of business and property income with an
_ emphasis on the case law that has
developed in this area. Prereq: Registration in AP3 and ACC 463

courses.label: ACC 465
courses.title: Taxation: Corporate Reorganizations
paras: An in-depth study of the provisions of the Income Tax Act relating to corporate reorganizations including share exchanges, amalgamations, and winding up a corporation.
Prereq: Registration AP3 and ACC 463

courses.label: ACC 466
courses.title: Taxation: Partnerships and Trusts
paras: An examination of tax legislation pertaining to the taxation of partnerships and their members, and trusts and their beneficiaries.
Prereq: Registration in AP3 and ACC 463

courses.label: ACC 467
courses.title: International Taxation
paras: An examination of topics including shareholders of non-resident corporations and tax on Canadian income of non-residents. The course will also examine the effects on.Canadian residents of the United States’ tax legislation.
Prereq: Registration in AP3 and ACC 463

paras: A comprehensive review of Canadian income tax legislation with a focus on techniques and consequences of estate planning.
Prereq: Registration in AP3 and ACC 463

courses.label: ACC 471
courses.title: Investments
paras: The objective of this course is to introduce the student to concepts of investment selection, purchase and management. The student should obtain a knowledge of security markets and the risk/return characteristics of forms of investment.
Prereq: ACC 371

courses.label: ACC 481
courses.title: Controllership
paras: A comprehensive insight into the problems facing top management accounting executives. Course includes a number of cases designed to expose students to real world situations requiring qualitative and quantitative analysis.
Prereq: ACC 382

courses.label: ACC 482
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Managerial Accounting
paras: An extension of basic managerial accounting concepts. Course includes the assignment of a broad range of articles designed to expose the student to theoretical and practical applications of managerial and cost accounting. Prereq: Registration in AP3 and ACC 382

marriage of computers and decision-

interest to accountants. Emphasis is on
the implications of DSS to managers
and the building of prototype DSS. Prereq: Registration in AP3

courses.title: Financial Accounting 3
paras: An advanced accounting course considering specific problems of accounting for the corporate entity, such as business combinations, intercorporate investments, consolidated financial statements, accounting for foreign operations and foreign currency transactions, segment reporting.
Prereq: ACC 292

courses.label: ACC 494
courses.title: External Reporting
paras: A case course integrating accounting, taxation, corporate and securities law, and report formulation.
Prereq: Registration in AP3 and ACC 491

courses.label: ANTH 101
courses.title: (Human and Cultural Evolution
paras: An overview of Physical Anthropology and Archaeology. Lectures on living and fossil primates, the fossil evidence for the origins and development of man, modern races, and archaeological evidence for the origins and development of culture.

courses.label: ANTH 102A
courses.title: Introduction to Social and Cultural
paras: Anthropology : The dynamic nature of socio-cultural systems is examined. Topics include language, technology, social organization, economics, politics, and religion. Data are drawn from a broad ethnographic base, including both “primitive” cultures and modern, developed societies.
A student may not take both ANTH 102A and ANTH 102B for credit.

courses.label: ANTH 102B
courses.title: Anthropology Through Science Fiction
paras: Basic anthropological concepts, such as biological and cultural evolution, culture, human adaptability, and culture contact will be explored through examples from science fiction and related anthropolgicai studies. ‘

courses.label: ANTH 103
courses.title: The Nature of Language
paras: A general introduction to the scientific study of language. Lectures on the nature of human language as compared with animal communication, some of the basic methods of historical and descriptive linguistics, and the importance of language in culture and society.

courses.label: ANTH 201
courses.title: Principles of Archaeology
paras: An introduction to the working assumptions, analytic approaches, and integrative and descriptive methods of archaeological anthropology.

courses.label: ANTH 202
courses.title: Principles of Soclal Organization
paras: An introduction to basic concepts used by social anthropologists for the analysis of social, economic, political and ideational systems.
Prereq: ANTH 102A or ANTH 102B or permission of the instructor

courses.label: ANTH 203
courses.title: Prehistoric Man in North America
paras: This is a general introduction to North
American Archaeology. The traditional
cultural ecological approach is used. 4

courses.label: ANTH 222
courses.title: Prehistoric Man In the Great Lakee
paras: Area - A Survey ; A general survey of the archaeological evidence of prehistoric man in the Great Lakes area from his arrival ca. 11,000 years ago to the coming of the Europeans. Cultural ecology and cultural evolution will be stressed.
Honours Anthropology students should take ANTH 322.

courses.label: ANTH 223
paras: Archaeology of Foodways: Gatherers and Hunters The technology, social organization and ideology of prehistoric and historic peoples who subsist without domesticated plants or animals. Archaeological and ethnographic evidence conceming human adaptations over the past 3 million years are considered.
Prereq: ANTH 101

courses.label: ANTH 230
courses.title: Indians of Canada The cultures of Canadian Indians are
paras: described as they existed when initially contacted by Europeans. Consideration is given to economic adaptation, social organization, political structure, material culture, ritual, and mythology.
Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: ANTH 233
courses.title: Inult and Eskimo Cultures An examination of Inuit and Eskimo cultures of Alaska, Canada, and Green-
paras: land from their prehistoric origins to the present. Administrative systems imposed upon the Inuit and Eskimo will be analyzed and compared, a8 will the contemporary problems these communities face.
Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: ANTH 241
courses.title: The Contemporary Cansdian Indian
paras: Scene ; ; An analysis of present-day Canadian Indian politics, economics, social organization, and education. The emergence of pan-indianism and large-scale Indian organizations will be examined as responses to the Federal Government's policy of withdrawing and decentralizing administrative services for native people.

courses.label: ANTH 258
courses.title: Anthropology and the Future of Man
paras: Anthropological theories pertaining lo culture change and cultural evclution are examined in the context of the modern world. Long and short term trends in technology are examined using data from Archaeology, Ethnography, History, Technology and Science.
Prereq: ANTH 101 or 102 or permission of the instructor

courses.label: ANTH 260
courses.title: Human Evolution
paras: Data, methods, and theory in the study of the origin and evolution of humans are surveyed. Topics will include ostedlogy, growth and development, the fossil record, and genetics.
Praraq: ANTH 101 or permission of the instructor

courses.label: ANTH 261
courses.title: Primate Behaviour
paras: An introduction to the behaviour of non-human primates and its relevance to human development. Topics will include social organization, role of behaviour, and communication patterns, as weil as the history of primate studies.

courses.label: ANTH 270
courses.title: Archaeological Method and
paras: Techniques: Survey of archaeplogical approaches to data focusing on field observation and recording. Some attention is given to the contribution of other disciplines to archaeology.
Prereq: ANTH 201

courses.label: ANTH 271
courses.title: Archaeological Field Methods
paras: Data gatnéring techniques will be studied and applied in field work on archaeological sites in the Waterloo area, Materials and transportation fee. Enrolment is limited, and instructor's - permission must be obtained. Offered concurrently with ANTH 372. This course will meet one half day, five days a week, for one month.

courses.label: ANTH 300
courses.title: Design of Anthropological Inquiry
paras: This course systematically examines research design and methodology in anthropology.
Prereq: ANTH 101, ANTH 102A or ANTH 1028

courses.label: ANTH 322
courses.title: Prehistoric Man in the Great Lakes
paras: Area : An in-depth study of the archaeological evidence of prehistoric man in the Great Lakes area from his arrivai ca. 11,000 years ago to the coming of Europeans. Cultural ecology and cultural evolution will be stressed
Prereq: ANTH 203 or consent of the instructor

courses.label: ANTH 330
courses.title: Cultura! Ecology
paras: An examination of the relationships among environment. technology, society. and culture. The increasing levels of complexity will be considered in the context of hunting and foraging bands, horticultural tribes and chiefdoms, pastoral tribes and agricultural peasantry.
Prereq: Fulf credit in Anthropology or consent of the instructor

courses.label: ANTH 345
courses.title: Special Topics in Anthropology
paras: Directed independent research Prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.label: ANTH 351
courses.title: Comparative Policies on Native Minorities
paras: A comparative survey of government policies on native minorities with emphasis on recent attempts to involve native groups in the policy-making processes. The course will compare policy approaches to Canadian Indians and Metis, Australian Aboriginals, New Zealand Maoris and Scandinavian Samis (Lapps).
Prereq: One of ANTH 102A or 1028, or P SCI 101 or 102M, or SOC 101

courses.label: ANTH 365
courses.title: Fossil Man
paras: A detailed examination of the fossil evidence for human evolution with particular emphasis on interpretation and reconstruction
Prereq: ANTH 260 or permission of the instructor

courses.label: ANTH 372
courses.title: Archaeological Research
paras: Supervised research in field or laboratory studies and analysis in archaeology. Prereq: ANTH 270. Offered concurrently with ANTH 271

courses.label: ARCH 192
courses.title: Design Fundamentals and Workshop Design Studio
paras: Development of the means to appreciate art and science of building; introduction to a history of architecture; introduction to the study of theories of architecture; development of skilis in graphic communication; introduction to a study of building structure, construction, and materials; promotion and encouragement of the theory and practice of design. Field trip (1 week).
Prereq: Architecture students only

courses.label: ARCH 193
courses.title: Design Fundamentals and Studio
paras: Reinforcement and development of the ARCH 192 program, but with emphasis upon the application of design method and practice to specific architectural problems.
Prereq: ARCH 192

courses.label: ARCH 194
courses.title: Visual Interdieciplinary Language
paras: Theory and practice of visual form. based on formative processes and hierarchial structures. Propositions: form follows process, rotation is a universal form-generating process, symmetric form is a result of an asymmetric. process and freedom is the single organizing principle. , Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 213
courses.title: Computer Generated Design 1 (Architectural Design 1)
paras: An overview of design logic and computer system requirement currently used for architectural design.
Prereq: CS. 116 or equivalent, or consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 224
courses.title: An Introduction to Landscape
paras: Design . An introduction to the design of landscape with emphasis upon the architectural attributes of plants and landforms.
Prereq: ARCH 192, 193, 292 or
consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 244
courses.title: History of Gardens of Europe and Western Asia
paras: The study of gardens as works of art reconciling man with his world. Gardens of Europe and Westem Asia are studied as responses to specific human needs, the stress and aspirations of an age, and to the climate and landscape of the land in which they were created. Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 245
courses.title: Survey of Contemporary
paras: Architecture. . Beginning with the formative years of modern architecture, the course will analyse buildings and theories of representative architects and designers, documenting the development of architectural ideas in Europe and elsewhere. Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 246
courses.title: Foundations of Europe: Sense of Periods and Styles
paras: Recognition of patterns of life and concepts of order and conduct, models of the universe and other, moving metaphors and myths by means of study of
- the thoughts, acts, art, architecture.
technology, literature, music and town design of the West from the break-up of the Roman Empire until the Renaissance. Field trips to museums, concerts in Toronto, Detroit or Buffalo.
Prereq: ARCH 143 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 247
courses.title: Renaissance to Revolution: Sense of Periods and Styles
paras: Analysis of the various styles emerging out of provincial and international Gothic, especially Italian use of classical models, the spread of this “renaissance” mode, leading to consideration of the Mannerist, the Baroque, the Rococo, the Neoclassical; investigation of the course of men’s attitudes from humanism, nationalism, and Reformation through the Enlightenment until the French Revolution and Hume’s dethronement of Reason. Field trips to museums, concerts in Toronto, Quebec, Detroit or Buffalo; Stratford Festival.
Prereq: ARCH 246 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 252
courses.title: Creative Problem Solving
paras: Development of creative skills through group behaviour in problem solving sessions by: developing a clear understanding of each participant's own creative thought processes; increasing his/her ability to consciously and deliberately make use of his/her own creative potential; engendering an awareness of the capacity to use himself/herself and the people he/she works with to produce better solutions to the problems identified by the group.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 262
courses.title: Strength of Materials
paras: Concept of simple stress and strain; statically indeterminate axially loaded members; thermal stresses, torsion; shear and bending moments in simple beam; shear and moment diagrams, qualitative deflected shapes, flexural and shearing stresses, deflection calculations; combined stresses, beams of different materials, compression members, Euler’s formula.
Prereq: ARCH 163
Course Descriptions Architecture

courses.label: ARCH 263
courses.title: Theory of Structure 1
paras: Study of foading conditions as per building code; stability of structural systems; geometric instability; analysis of statically determinate structures, beams, arches, cables, trusses, frames; approximate analysis of rigid frames; influence lines; deflections by conjugate beams; introduction to indeterminate structures.
Prereq: ARCH 262

courses.label: ARCH 265
courses.title: Structural Morphogenesis
paras: Exploration of new structural forms. Basic physical principles and laws governing these forms. Study of membrane surfaces. Arrangements of forms for structural efficiency. Minimum surfaces and modular developments (close packing and hierarchies). Use of modular symmetry to create optinum structural systems.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 272
courses.title: Survey and Soils
paras: Surveying types, instruments and measurements. Plotting of areas and contours; layout of buildings and underground systems. Types of soils, their identification and investigation; mechanics of strength, suitability of soils for various types of foundations.

courses.label: ARCH 293
courses.title: Design Concepts and Studio
paras: Design involving problems of human perception and dimension in complex or large spaces, and to develop in each student the ability to generate solutions to architectural problems on a scale which involves “privacy and community.” Emphasis is placed on programming, analysis and solution evaluation. Problems of construction, servicing, and siting will be further explored. Field trip to a major Urban Area (1 week).
Prereq: ARCH 292

“ARCH 345 W 2C,iS 05 Architectural Theory 1850-1940 Beginning with the introduction of . important theories of architecture in vogue prior to 1850, the course will examine texts, movements, buildings, projects, and urban proposals of the period in order to understand the structure of contemporary architectural theory.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 346
paras: Romanticism and 20th Century: Sense of Periods and Styles Depiction of "modem” culture as one in which the notion of environmental order as the fulfilling of natural law is replaced by a notion of order as the creation of autonomous human wills. Selected works in philosophy, literature, art and architecture will be studied.
Prereq: ARCH 247 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 347
courses.title: Fhe Roots of Civilization
paras: The course attempts to establish a basis for the understanding of the functions of myth, ceremony and ritual, the structures. of primitive and ancient built environments, man’s attitude towards nature, and his use of the resource environment, the development of classical culture, and beginnings of science. Prereq: ARCH 346 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 348
courses.title: Kalian Renaissance Architecture
paras: Architecture and urban design from the early 15th to the early 17th century in central and northern Italy. Special atten-_ tion is paid to the development of theory and its relation to architectural practice. in addition to the works of the major figures of the period, typical reiationships between buildings and their urban and natural contexts are considered. Prereq: Registration in ARCH 492 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 349
courses.title: Topics in Cultural History
paras: Research into various topics including architectural history, theory, practice, and pedagogy but exploring the means of study (the human mind, the precepters, the tools of searching, ordering of findings, ways of presentation of the results of reflection). Guest lecturers, field trips, and private consultants will diversify the common studies. Because the topics will shift, it is possible to enrol in the course more than once.
Prereq: Consent of instructor after an interview and inventory

courses.label: ARCH 362
courses.title: Structural Synthesis 1: Steel and Concrete Design
paras: Design and behaviour of structural steel systems, application of current building specifications, proportioning structural elements based on pertinent design considerations, bolted and welded; criteria for choosing steel systems; introduction to plastic design.
Prereq: ARCH 263

courses.label: ARCH 363
courses.title: Structural Synthesis 2: Concrete and Timber Designs
paras: Design and behaviour of structural concrete systems, application of building specifications; analysis and design of concrete elements using ultimate strength principle; criteria for choosing structural concrete systems; introduction to prestressed concrete. Behaviour and design of modern wood structures fasteners, ring connectors and their significance in timber construction; proportioning and design of sawn and laminated timber members. Prereq: ARCH 362

courses.label: ARCH 371
courses.title: Designing and Building with Soler Energy
paras: Instruction in the basics of solar technology, including principles of climatic design, solar basics, efficient building layout design, solar systems design, heat loss/gain calculations, and simple computer simulation of the. designed systems.
Prereq: Consent of instructor (ability to figure heat calculations, basic knowt edge of solar building).

courses.label: ARCH 372
courses.title: Mechanical Systems 1
paras: Plumbing and drainage; heating, venti- Jating and air-conditioning systems; electrical distribution for power and light illumination, acoustics, geometrics and materials; vertical transportation systems..
Prereq: ARCH 293, or consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 373
courses.title: Mechanical Systems 2
paras: Advanced topics and integrative investigations in heating, ventilating and airconditioning systems for buildings; plumbing and drainage; electrical distribution for power and. light in buildings; illumination; acoustics, geometrics and. materials; and vertical transportation systems.
Prereq: ARCH 372.

paras: Design
The application of critical thought will be —

exercised regularly through oral and written assignments on a wide range of designed human experience; secondarily, there will be reading assignments to facilitate the practice of criticism through a broadening knowledge of critical theory and its relationship to culture. Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 446
courses.title: Hatlan Urban History
paras: The course provides a survey of the history of settlement and urban form on the ttalian penninsula from antiquity to the present day. In it the influences upon the structure. of public and private space are outlined for each historical period. These include the constants such as geography and climate, but more especially the factors that induce and manifest change: politics, warfare, economics, social structure, the arts and theory.
Prereq: Registration in ARCH 492 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 448
courses.title: Rome and the Campagna
paras: History of settlement and building in Rome and the surrounding area from antiquity to the present. Acts of design in architecture, urban form and landscape related to political, cultural and spiritual authority of Rome. Comparison drawn between the image of the city, represented in literature and art, and the material facts of the place. Field trips, lecture.
Prereq: Registration in ARCH 492 or consent of instructor

Courses not offered in the current academic year are listed at the end of this section.
Introductory Notes

1. Courses designated " Arts”, those listed below, usually cover some topics and themes of general interest to several disciplines. and their presentation is often made with this interdisciplinary perspective in view. '
2. Arts courses are elective courses in General and Honours programs and do not satisfy either the Group A or Group 8 requirements.

courses.label: ARTS 100A
courses.title: Introduction to the Humanities A and
paras: 8B

An interdisciplinary introduction to the arts, literatures, philosophies and religions of Western Civilization, enabling the student to experience and discuss important representative works and ideas from selected periods, and to become acquainted with the humanistic disciplines. 100A focuses on selected periods from Classical Antiquity to toughly 1750. 100B focuses on selected periods from roughly 1750 to the present.

courses.label: ARTS 122
courses.title: Quest for Meaning in the 20th Century
paras: This course invites students to a quest for personal and corporate meaning in the context of a century in which traditional meaning definitions have been challenged by world wars, nuclear threat and rapidly shifting sexual, social, economic and religious values. Offered by Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: ARTS 198
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Technology
paras: A general introduction to the fundamental ideas of computers. Topics treated will include the use of an interactive computing system, word processing, and the beginnings of program writing. The course will examine the history of computing, and will consider the social and economic impact of the use of computers. No previous knowledge of computing is assumed.

courses.label: ARTS 202P
courses.title: Psychology of Religion in Historical Perspective ‘
paras: A study of the Psychology of Religion in its historical perspective from the nineteenth century to the present day. Methods, techniques and practices of research that are applicable to the examination of religious experience will also be introduced.

courses.label: ARTS 211
courses.title: Computing Techniques In Language and Literature
paras: An introduction to non-mathematical computer programming, with special emphasis on the manipulation of language data. The programming language used will be PL/1. ARTS 211 will concentrate on gaining skill in computer programming. ARTS 212 will stress file management, advanced text formatting and the use of system program utilities. Applications will include word indexes, text concordances, methods of computer-aided text comparison..
Prereq: ARTS 211 presupposes ARTS 198 or equivalent; 212 presupposes 211 or permission of the instructor
ARTS 2154/8
Man in Crisis (Literary Views)

A critical study of such themes as freedom vs. happiness, nihilism, collectivism vs. individualism, old tablets vs. - utopias, alienation, earthbound fragmentation vs. the transcendental in the artistic writings of Kafka, Brecht, Hesse, Nietzsche, Solzhenitsyn, Dostoevsky, Zamiatin, Camus, and others. Taught in English

courses.label: ARTS 215A
courses.title: Man in Crisis 1 (Literary Views)
paras: A critical study of Dostoevsky’s The Grand Inquisitor, Nietzsche's Thus Spake Zarathustra, Tolstoy's What Men Live By, and works by Aldous Huxley, Zamiatin, Turgenev, and Andres. The 2 major themes are Utopia, the yearning for and the shape of perfectibility, and Nihilism, the denial and/or destruction of "Old Tablets” or "God is Dead.”

courses.label: ARTS 215B
courses.title: Man in Crisis 2 (Literary Views)
paras: A critical study of Brecht’s The Caucasian Chalk Circle, Katka's The Metamor- Phosis, and’ works by Ibsen, Hesse, Dostoevsky, Tolstoy, and Sdizhenitsyn. The 2 major themes are Nihilism (see above) and Alienation, the divided self in exile, or the inability to give and to accept love.

courses.label: ARTS 225
courses.title: Mennonite Authors and Artists
paras: An examination of Mennonite cultural expression in literature (fiction, poetry, drama, children’s literature) and the. visual arts (especially painting and film) during the past century.
Offered by Conrad Grebel College.

ARTS 250) J 1.0 Introductory Topics in Family Life Education: Marriage and the Family This course will study marriage and the family from psychological, sociological, Philosophical and theological perspectives. Methods for incorporating significant knowledge about marriage and the family into family life programs will also be given attention.
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

paras: An in-depth analysis of selected topics in marriage and family life, especially their emotional aspects, including an evaluation of family life education in school and community.
Prereq: ARTS 250J

Course Descriptions

courses.label: BIOL 111
courses.title: Introductory Biology 1
paras: An introduction to basic concepts in biology, including aspects of genetics, evolution and plant biology.
Open to students other than those intending to major in Biology or to enter the School of Optometry.

courses.label: BIOL 112
courses.title: Introductory Biology 2
paras: An introduction to the basic principles of zoology and ecology with reference to man as a biological organism.
Open to students other than those intending to major in Biology or to enter the School of Optometry.

courses.label: BIOL 201
courses.title: Human: Anatomy
paras: Basic anatomical features of the skeletal, muscular, nervous and cardiovascular systems of the human.
Open to students other than those intending to major in Biology.
BIOL 201 cannot be counted for credit toward a BSc (Kinesiology) degree.

courses.label: BIOL 202
courses.title: Embryology and Histology
paras: Fundamental developmental processes in vertebrates, including man; the development of the early embryo; morphogenesis of tissues and the major organ systems. Structure of human cells and tissues at the light-microscope level; epithelia, connective, muscular and nervous tissues and the major organ systems.
Open to students other than those intending to major in Biology.

courses.label: BIOL 210
courses.title: Introductory invertebrate Zoology
paras: A study of the functional morphology of selected invertebrate types with special emphasis: on the various grades of organization and development in the different phyla.

courses.label: BIOL 211
courses.title: Introductory Vertebrate Zoology
paras: An introduction to the structure, evolution and development of vertebrate organ systems.
Offered during the Spring term in odd-numbered years.

courses.label: BIOL 220
courses.title: Plant Biology 1 - The Living Plant
paras: An introduction to the structure, function and physiology of plants with emphasis on flowering plants.

and life histories of the. different kinds of

courses.label: BIOL 222
courses.title: Non-Vascular Plants
paras: An introductory course which will survey the evolution, morphology, ecology and importance to man of the fungi, algae, and bryophytes.
By correspondence only for 1985-86.

courses.label: BIOL 230
courses.title: Introductory Cell Biology
paras: An introduction to the concepts of cell biology with emphasis on (1) the structural organization of the cell and its constituent organelles and (2) the function of critical molecular processes that are characteristic of living organisms. | When taking this course, the lab must be designated separately. The lab is compulsory, but does not have any credit weight.

courses.label: BIOL 233
courses.title: Human Physiology
paras: The physiology of the major organ systems including the nervous, muscular, circulatory, respiratory, urinary, digestive, endocrine and reproductive systems.
Antireq: SCI 351-362
When taking this course, the lab must be designated separately. The lab is compulsory, but does not have any credit weight.
Offered during the Spring term in even-numbered years. .

courses.label: BIOL 239
courses.title: Genetics
paras: The Mendelian basis of genetic analysis. Chromosomal mechanisms in mitosis and meiosis. The origin, inheritance and adaptive significance of chromosomal changes. Nucieic acids as the carriers of genetic information. Natural selection and the evolution of genetic systems. Offered during the Spring term in even-numbered years.

courses.label: BIOL 240
courses.title: Fundamentals of Microbiology
paras: Introduction to fundamental theories, principles and methods of microbiology. Structure, methods of cultivation, growth, effects of physical factors, and inhibition and killing of microorganisms will be studied.

courses.label: BIOL 241
courses.title: Introduction to the Microbial World
paras: Biological characterization of major
‘bacterial groups, microorganisms as
geochemical agents, utilization of microorganisms by man, and mechanisms of microbial pathogenicity.
Offered during the Spring term in odd-numbered years.

courses.label: BIOL 245
courses.title: General Microbiology 1
paras: History and scope of microbiology. Study of the characteristics of bacteria and other microorganisms.
Open to students other than those intending to major in Biology or to enter the School of Optometry.

courses.label: BIOL 246
courses.title: General Microbiology 2
paras: Relationships of microorganisms to man and his environment.
Prereq: BIOL 245
Open to students other than those intending te major in Biology or to enter the School of Optometry.

courses.label: BIOL 250
courses.title: Ecology
paras: An introduction to the study of the relationships of plants and animals to their environment. The nature of ecosystems, ecological energetics, biogeochemical , cycling, community ecology, introduction to population biology.

courses.label: BIOL 298
courses.title: Field Course 1
paras: A series of one-day field trips from campus, usually the-first six Saturdays of term, designed to introduce students to the flora, fauna, and major ecosystems of Southern Ontario. Written reports will be required for each trip. Coreq: BIOL 250 or equivalent Field trip fee: A small charge for bus fare.

courses.label: BIOL 301A
courses.title: Human Physiology
paras: The physiology of the major organ systems of the body. The topics discussed include circulation, respiration, digestion and nutrition, metabolism, muscle, nervous system, special senses, and the endocrine system.
No credit or grade:will be given for the first-term course whiasé the twoterm sequence is cormpiéted.
For Optometry students only.

courses.label: BIOL 311
courses.title: Vertebrate Zoology
paras: Major topics in vertebrafe zoology as
exemplified by both living and fossil
members of the subphydum Craniata. Prereq: BIOL 2198

courses.label: BIOL 315
courses.title: Invertebrate Zoology
paras: A survey of the major invertebrate phyla ather than the arthropods, with emphasis on their functional anatomy, classification and ways. of life.
Prereq: BIOL 210

courses.label: BIOL 316
courses.title: Arthropod Zoology ‘
paras: A survey of the phylum: Arthropoda, including the insects, with emphasis on their classification, interrelationships and ways of life.
Prereq: BIOL 210
Offered during the Spring term in even-numbered years.

courses.label: BIOL 323
courses.title: Plant Anatomy and Morphogenesis
paras: Plant structure in relation to function and development with particular reference to the vascular plants. Cell, tissue and organ differentiation.
Prereq: BIOL 220 and 230
Offered during the Spring term in odd-numbered years.

courses.label: BIOL 324
courses.title: The Flowering Plants
paras: A study of floral morphology in relation to classification and evolution. An introduction to taxonomy and nomenclature. History of taxonomy. Systems of classification. Mechanisms of pollination and dispersal.
Students entering this course are required to make a flowering plant collection. instructions should be obtained from the Herbarium prior to the summer break.

courses.label: BIOL 327
courses.title: Mycology 1
paras: Fungal taxonomy and ecology; medical
mycology; plant pathology; industrial
applications; food and food processing.
toxins and hallucinogens; biological
control; fungi as coprophiles, predators.
and symbionts with plants and animals. Prereq: BIOL 221

courses.label: BIOL 330
courses.title: Molecular Biology
paras: Molecular biological aspects of chromosome replication, expression of genetic information, functional translation of specific eukaryotic proteins, cell division, gamete formation, embryogenesis, hormone action, cellular interactions and cell differentiation.

courses.label: BIOL 331
courses.title: Cell Physiology
paras: The functional organization of cells with particular reference to cell-cell interaction, the structure, function and development of organelles and the biological roles of cellular membranes.
Prereq: BIOL 230

courses.label: BIOL 333
courses.title: Histology and Cytology
paras: The structure of mammalian cells.
tissues and organs interpreted in func-
tional terms. Cell reproduction and
differentiation, with some discussion of
the embryological origin of tissues and
the regulation of tissue growth. Light
and electron microscopy techniques. Prereq: BIOL 211 or 230 or 233

courses.label: BIOL 335
courses.title: Plant Physiology
paras: A study of the principal physiological mechanisms that govern the water economy, mineral nutrition, transport processes and metabolism of plants.

courses.label: BIOL 336
courses.title: Embryology
paras: Fundamental processes and concepts in embryonic development including the acquisition of multicellularity, organization of the early embryo, morphogenesis of tissues, major organ systems, fetal membranes, growth, differentiation and analysis of common developmental defects.

courses.label: BIOL 337
courses.title: Comparative Animal Physiology 1
paras: The comparative physiology of animals with particular emphasis on homeostatic principles as demonstrated by water balance, excretion, nutrition, digestion and the endocrine system.

courses.label: BIOL 338
courses.title: Comparative Animal Physiology 2
paras: A comparative study of the cardiovascular, nervous, muscular, respiratory and reproductive systems.
Prereq: BIOL 233

BIOL 42 FS 2C3al 05 Microbial Biotechnology The role of microorganisms in biotechnology. Topics examined will include the isolation, selection, and development of microorganisms important in biotechnology, and specialized techniques for their cultivation and maintenance. ~ Processes studied will include biomass conversions, fermentations, bioproduction of compounds, nitrogen fixation, treatment and utilization of wastes and mineral leaching.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241 or permission of instructor

courses.label: BIOL 344
courses.title: Microorganisms in Foods
paras: Food preservation, spoilage, poisoning and modern concepts in quality assurance programs are studied. The aim is to understand factors governing microbial changes in foods. Problem solving in the food industry is emphasized. Laboratory work will reflect current practices in quality control and testing. Prereq: BIOL 240-241 or permission of instructor

courses.label: BIOL 350
courses.title: Environmental Toxicology 1
paras: An introduction to the basic theories, principles and techniques of environ- , mental toxicology. A comparative study of the effects of specific groups of toxicants on ecosystems; biodegradation and cycling.

courses.label: BIOL 356
courses.title: Population Ecology 1
paras: The ecology of populations. Topics include: demographic parameters and their estimation; population growth and regulation; competitive and predatorprey interactions; population genetics and evolution; applied population biology. Prereq: BIOL 250 and STAT 202

courses.label: BIOL 416
courses.title: Entomology
paras: Introduction to morphology, systematics and biology of insects.
Brief field trips will be made to collect insects from different local habitats.

courses.label: BIOL 420
courses.title: The Flora of Canada
paras: The composition and history of the Canadian flora. Major plant communities in Canada; their floristic composition and ecology. Endangered species and the conservation of our flora.

courses.label: BIOL 424
courses.title: Ferns, Gymnosperms and Fern
paras: Allies: an evolutionary survey A detailed survey of the non-flowering vascular plants with emphasis on the extant members of each major group in Ontario. The phylogeny of the plants will be explored through a study of fossil ancestors in each line of evolution. Prereq: BIOL 220 and 221 or permission of the instructor Offered in even-numbered years.

courses.label: BIOL 426
courses.title: Phycology
paras: The taxonomy and ecology of freshwater and marine algae. Algal cytology, morphology, and life histories; biology of planktonic and attached algae; culturing of algae; experimental phycology; economic aspects of algae.
Prereq: BIOL 220 or 221

courses.label: BIOL 427
courses.title: Mycology 2
paras: The growth of mycological knowledge will be traced and current developments analyzed. Extensive literature surveys, active class participation, and a lab project, will be required.
Prereq: BIOL 327

courses.label: BIOL 490
courses.title: Comparative Animal Physiology 3
paras: A comparative study of physiological processes in animals; emphasis will be placed on the neuroendocrine system and anima! models that are useful for understanding basic physiological processes

courses.label: BIOL 481
courses.title: Mammalian Reproductive Physiology
paras: A study of the endocrine and reproductive systems of mammals. Major topics include methods of hormone assay, chemistry of the hormones, regulation of secretion, mechanisms of hormone action, neurosecretion, reproductive cycles, gametogenesis and fertilization. Prereq: BIOL 233 recommended

courses.label: BIOL 482
courses.title: Piant Growth and Development
paras: A study of the plant hormones and the mechanisms that control growth, dormancy and development.

courses.label: BIOL 433
courses.title: Stress Physiology and Aging In
paras: * Plants A study of stress tolerance and aging in plants. Mechanisms of adjustment to temperature, moisture, salt and chemical stress will be emphasized.

courses.label: BIOL 434
courses.title: Advanced Genetics
paras: A detailed examination of the recent advances in molecular genetics with emphasis on the regulation of gene action in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Current research literature will be reviewed.
Offered every other year. Alternates with BIOL 438.
BIOL 4385 F 203L 05 Developmental Biology
Analysis of embryonic development of selected organisms with emphasis on growth and the processes: of subcellular, cellular and organ differentiation stressing recent experimental methodology.

courses.label: BIOL 438
courses.title: Advanced Molecular Biology
paras: An examination of the current major issues in molecular biology with emphasis on the technical and conceptual advances. Current research literature will be reviewed.
Prereq: BIOL 330
Offered every other year. Alternates with BIOL. 434.

courses.label: BIOL 439
courses.title: Blochemistry of Natural Products
paras: The chemistry, functions and distribution of natural products including alkaloids, isoprenoids, amines, phenolics, cyanogenic glycosides and other important compounds in plants and other biological systems.
Prereq: At least one full-year course or equivalent in organic chemistry plus a one-term course in biochemistry that includes the essentials of carbohydrate and fat metabolism.

courses.label: BIOL 444
courses.title: Immunology
paras: Physical and biological properties of immunological agents that protect against disease, the procedures for their identification and their practical applications.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241

courses.label: BIOL 442
courses.title: Virology
paras: The nature of viruses and their interaction with their plant, microbial and animal hosts.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241

courses.label: BIOL 443
paras: Microorganisms of industrial Importance A study of the role of microorganisms in industrial processes of biosynthesis and degradation.
Prereq: BIOL 344

courses.label: BIOL 444
courses.title: Microorganisms and Disease
paras: A study of the microorganisms involved in pathogenesis, their mode of infection, symptoms and prevention.
Prereq: BIOL 240, 241, 447

courses.label: BIOL 446
courses.title: Microbial Ecology
paras: A study of the ecological roles of microorganisms. Examples from freshwater, terrestrial, marine and other ecosystems will be used to illustrate the activities and importance of microorganisms in these habitats.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241, or permission of instructor

courses.label: BIOL 447
courses.title: Environmental Microbiology
paras: A study of the environmental impact of microorganisms. Aspects of pollution, - waste treatment, biodegradation of environmental contaminants, and nutrient cycling will be examined. Prereq: BIOL 240-241, 446, or permis sion of instructor

courses.label: BIOL 448
courses.title: Microbial Physiology 1
paras: A study of the physiology of microorganisms including multiphasic and synchronous growth, cell permeation, nutrition, physical and chemical environmental factors and metabolic mechanisms as elucidated by radioactively labelled tracers.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241, or permission of instructor

courses.label: BIOL 449
courses.title: Microbial Physiology 2
paras: A study of the physiology of microorganisms with emphasis on synthetic and assembly processes. Mechanisms underlying the biosynthesis of DNA, protein, stable RNA, peptidoglycan, phospholipids, lipopolysaccharides and polysaccharides as well as assembly of the cell envelope, the nucleoid and polysomes will be discussed.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241 or permission of instructor

courses.label: BIOL 450
courses.title: Marine Biology
paras: An examination of coastal and offshore marine environments. Physical and chemical oceanography, plankton, benthos and fish are discussed. Prereq: BIOL 210; a marine field course Antireq: SCI 453

courses.label: BIOL 451
courses.title: Limnology
paras: A study of the geomorphology, physical and chemical processes, and biology of lakes and streams. Ecology of zooplankton, zoobenthos, and fishes is emphasized.
Prereq: BIOL 210, 250
Antireq: SCI 454

courses.label: BIOL 452
courses.title: Fisheries Biology
paras: The practices of fisheries biology; life history; age and growth, fecundity, production, harvest and management of fisheries resources.

courses.label: BIOL 455
courses.title: Environmental Toxicology 2
paras: Cellular, developmental and physiological effects of toxicants on multicellular organisms. .
Prereq: BIOL 350

courses.label: BIOL 456
courses.title: Population Ecology 2
paras: The analysis of the structure and dynamics of plant and animal populations, Theoretical, mathematical and experimental approaches to the study of population ecology. Evolutionary processes in population biology.
Prereq: BIOL 356

courses.label: BIOL 457
courses.title: Analysis of Communities
paras: A study of the organization, structure and development of communities with emphasis on vegetation change. Topics include: sampling procedures; diversity; stability; succession; niche; multivariate analysis.
Prereq: BIOL 250 and STAT 202

courses.label: BIOL 458
courses.title: Quaternary Ecology
paras: A consideration of the Quaternary environment. Pollen, plant macrofossil and faunal remains as indicators of past environments. Relationship of fossil assemblages.to modern ecosystems. Pollen analysis and the interpretation of fossil deposits. _
Prereq: an introductory course in biology or geology, dr permission of the instructor

courses.label: BIOL 460
courses.title: Statistical Procedures for Biologists 1
paras: An introduction to biometrical analysis. Measures of central tendency, dispersion and variability; the normal distribution; one-sample hypotheses; parametric and non-parametric two-sample and paired-sample hypotheses; correlation; goodness-of-fit tests; chi-square and G-tests for contingency tables; the Poisson and Binomia! distributions. Throughout, the emphasis is on biological examples.

courses.label: BIOL 461
courses.title: Statistical Procedures for
paras: Biologists 2

Design and analysis of experiments with an emphasis on the application of Statistics to research problems in Biology. Topics will include: analysis of variance; experimental designs; factorial experiments; models; missing data.
transformations; a priori and a posteriori -
comparisons among means; regression analysis; analysis of covariance.

courses.label: BIOL 473
courses.title: Biosystematics and Evolution
paras: A study of the processes of evolution; the differentiation of populations and the origin of new forms of life.
Prereq: BIOL 239

courses.label: BIOL 480
courses.title: Biotechnology 1
paras: Genetic engineering entails the directed alteration of the hereditary apparatus of cells. How genetic material is manipulated {i.e., recombinant DNA technology) will be examined including the use of restriction endonucleases, cloning vehicles, transformation procedures, screening methods and expression of cloned genes. _
Prereq: BIOL 240-241 and CHEM 237 or permission of the instructor

courses.label: BIOL 481
courses.title: Biotechnology 2
paras: Biotechnology involves the harnessing of biological processes for large-scale industrial applications. Topics examined will include industrial enzymology, and animal and plant cell culture.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241 and CHEM 237 or permission of the instructor

courses.label: BIOL 490
courses.title: Field Course in Marine Biology
paras: A 2-week study of marine environments ‘and biota. Emphasis on: the flora and fauna of rocky shores, mud flats, and the sub-tidal benthos. Grade based on a field notebook and a research project. This course will normally be held at Huntsman Marine Lab, New Brunswick each September. Courses sponsored by Ontario Universities at other times of the year may also qualify. Prereq: BIOL 210, 250 or equivalent Field trip tee: $400-$500

courses.label: BIOL 491
courses.title: Field Course in Terrestrial and Aquatic Biology
paras: A 2-week study of the flora and fauna of terrestrial! environments, lakes and streams. Emphasis on biosystematics, distribution and dynamics of organisms. Both population and community approaches are stressed. This course will normally be held in Algonquin Park, Ontario each September. Courses sponsored by Ontario Universities at other times.of the year may also qualify. Prereq: BIOL 250 or equivalent Field trip fee: $100-$300

courses.label: BIOL 498
courses.title: Field Course 2
paras: A general interest field course usually of one week duration. Requirement is met by attending the first week only of a 2-week trip arranged or approved by the Department (e.g. BIOL 490 or 491). Courses sponsored by Ontario Universities at other times of the year may also qualify.
Coreq: BIOL 250 or equivalent
Field trip fee: $100-$300

courses.title: Senior Honours Project
paras: A senior-year research project. Normally, only students attaining a 70% cumulative major average will be accepted into this course. Students are referred to the co-ordinator for BIOL 499 for further details.

Course Descriptions
Introductory Note

The core courses for each year of the Program constitute an interdisciplinary study of Canadian problems, and are offered either in a lecture/tutorial format or a seminar format (depending on the number of students registered). These courses are given by faculty members of the participating departments of the University and by eminent scholars from other parts of Canada who visit the University for brief or extended periods during the year.

courses.label: CDNST 101
courses.title: Landforms and Mindscapes
paras: An introduction to the Canadian landscape and its early impact upon the creative imagination of Canadians. The course sets out to provide a basis for dealing with contemporary Canadian culture.

courses.label: CDNST 201
courses.title: Secial Regionalism
paras: Lecturers in Geography, Political
Science, Sociology and History discuss . the roles which economic disparities.
social elites, federal/provincial relations
and political parties play in defining
Canadian regionalism. Particular atten-
tion is paid to Quebec’s desire for
separate status.

courses.label: CDNST 202
courses.title: Cultural Regionalism
paras: Lecturers discuss the contribution made by literature, film, drama, and fine arts in defining distinctive regional identities in Canada. Particular attention is paid to the emergence of a distinctive Ontario culture.

courses.label: CDNST 301
courses.title: Regionalism: West
paras: This course continues the exploration ot Canadian regionalism by applying knowledge gained in CDN ST 201/202 to distinctive problems of the Canadian west and northwest. The focus of the seminar will vary according to the interests of the faculty and students. Prereq: CDN ST 101, 201 or 202 or permission of the instructor

courses.label: CDNST 302
courses.title: Regionalism: East
paras: This course continues the exploration of Canadian regicnalism by applying knowledge gained in CDN ST 201/202 to distinctive problems of Atlantic Canada. The focus of the seminar will vary according to the interests of the faculty and students.
Prereq: CDN ST 101, 202 or 202 or permission of instructor

courses.label: CDNST 400A
courses.title: Research Essay
paras: An extensive senior research essay, supervised by a committee composed of faculty members from 2 or more of the participating departments, which deals with a specific aspect of Canada utilizing material and methods from several different disciplines.
A grade for CDN ST 400A will be submitted only after the completion of CON ST 4008.

Course Descriptions Introductory Note
Prerequisite: For all courses in the.
registration in the Department or permission of the Associate Chairman (Undergraduate Studies) is a requirement.

courses.label: CHE 100
courses.title: Weeks 0.75
paras: Chemical Engineering Concepts 1 An introduction to the basic methods and principles used by engineers in the analysis and design of physical processes: units, dimensions, and measurements, mass balances, behaviour of fluids. Laboratory on visual communication is included.

courses.label: CHE 101
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Concepts 2
paras: An extension of the topics covered in CH E 100. Energy balances. Laboratory experiments illustrate the physical principles discussed. ~

courses.label: CHE 102
courses.title: Chemistry for Engineers
paras: Chemical principles with applications in engineering. Stoichiometric calculations, properties of gases, properties of liquids and solutions, gas phase chemical equilibrium, ionic equilibrium in aqueous solution, oxidation-reduction reactions, chemical kinetics.

courses.label: CHE 210
courses.title: Transport Processes 1 (Equilibrium Stage Operations)
paras: Equilibrium between phases; the equilibrium-stage concept. Cascades of Stages with and without reflux; examples of their analysis when used to separate components by distillation, extraction, absorption and leaching. Introduction to computer methods for multicomponent mixtures.

courses.label: CHE 213
courses.title: Transport Processes 2 (Fluid Mechanics)
paras: Fundamentals of fluid flow; conservation laws for mass, momentum and mechanical energy; flow of fluid in conduits; flow past immersed bodies. Description, collection and separation of particulate systems.

courses.label: CHE 220
courses.title: Applied Mathematics 1
paras: Basic concepts of probability and their relevance to engineering decisions. Statistical frequency distributions, tests of significance, correlations, curve fitting, sampling theory, applications, errors, design of experiments.

courses.label: CHE 230
courses.title: Physical Chemistry 1
paras: Introduction to physical chemistry. Ideal and real gases, the kinetic theory of gases, first law of thermodynamics, thermochemistry, heats of reaction, second law, chemical equilibria in simple systems, phase equilibria in simple systems, third law.

courses.label: CHE 231
courses.title: Physical Chemistry 2
paras: Thermodynamics of systems of variable composition; properties of solutions, ideal solutions, colligative properties of solutions, phase equilibria in complex systems, non-ideal solutions. Surface phenomena. Chemical kinetics; empirical laws and mechanisms.
Prereq: CH E 230
" Course Destriptions Chemical Engineering
CHE 2322 WF X 05
Inorganic Chemistry 1

Wave mechanics, atomic structure and the periodic table, chemical bonding, structural chemistry of elements and compounds, introductory transition metal chemistry, some thermodynamic aspects of inorganic chemistry.

courses.label: CHE 233
courses.title: Physical Chemistry Laboratory
paras: Experiments on viscosity of gases and liquids, chemical Kinetics, absorption, homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis, thermochemistry, phase equilibria, diffusion, determination of molecular weight of polymers, training in technical report writing.

courses.label: CHE 314
courses.title: Transport Processes 3 (Heat Transfer)
paras: Introduction to heat transfer, momentum-heat transfer analogies and dimensional analysis, steady and transient heat conduction, convection and applications to engineering problems, radiant heat transfer and heat transfer with change of phase.
Prereq: CH E 213

courses.label: CHE 317
courses.title: Transport Processes 4 (Mass
paras: Transfer) . Mass transfer by molecular and turbulent motion, heat-mass transfer analogies, mass transfer models and application to separations such as distillation, absorption, adsorption, extraction, etc.; simultaneous heat and mass transfer in gas-liquid contacting and solids drying; introduction to mass transfer with chemical reaction.
Prereq: CH E 314

courses.label: CHE 320
courses.title: Applied Mathematics 2
paras: Gamma-Beta-and error-functions; sinecosine-, exponential- and ellipticintegrals, linear differential equations, Wronskian, Green function; initial and boundary value problems; Bessel func: tions; Fourier series, integrals and transforms, orthogonal functions; Laplace
transforms; applications.

courses.label: CHE 321
courses.title: Process Dynamics and Contro! 1
paras: Block and signal flow diagrams, proportional-integral-derivative control lers, frequency response techniques, analytical and graphical stability criteria. introduction to modem control theory. Computer tab includes simulation and control strategy design.
Prereq: MATH 216, CH E 314, CHE

courses.label: CHE 330
courses.title: Chemical Engineering
paras: Thermodynamics of flow processes, vapour power plants, intema! combustion anginas, liquefaction of gases, refrigeration and evaporation, chemical equilibria in chemical reactions, thermal pollution, the energy crisis, efficient energy utilization and thermodynamics. Prereq: CH E 231

courses.label: CHE 331
courses.title: Chemical Reaction Engineering
paras: Homogeneous reactors; batch, CSTR, tubular flow systems, ideal models, residence time distributions in ideal reactors, temperature effects, steady states, semi-batch systems, nonideal behaviour. Heterogeneous catalysis; mass transfer effects; catalytic rate equations, fixed and fluidized bed reactors.
Prereq: CH E 231

CHE 32 WS 3C 05 Inorganic Chemistry 2 Introductory electrochemistry; electrotysis, electrolytic conductance and transport, reversible, electrode processes, irreversible electrode processes and electrode kinetics, electrochemical measurements and their analytical applications, chemistry of corrosion.
Prereq: CH E 232

courses.label: CHE 333
courses.title: Instrumental Methods of Chemical Analysis
paras: An introduction to modern analysis including optical, electrochemical, radiochemical, chromatographic and spectroscopic methods.

courses.label: CHE 382
courses.title: Engineering Economics and Process Design 1
paras: Mathematics of finance, time value of money, taxes and depreciation, profitability, estimation of capital and production costs. Linear programming. Study of piping, valves, pumps, compressors, and fans. Materials of construction.

courses.label: CHE 410
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Laboratory
paras: Experimental applications of physical and chemical principles using pilot scale equipment, experiments ittustrating major unit operations (distillation, absorption, extraction, drying, humidification). Prereq: CH E 314

courses.label: CHE 484
courses.title: Engineering Economics and Process Design 2”
paras: The business cycle and financial state ments, cost accounting, optimization. Study of pressure vesseis and equipment for heat and mass transfer.

courses.label: CHE 486
courses.title: Technical Seminar
paras: Each student will be expected to Prepare and deliver a seminar on material from the recent literature or industrial experience, as well as an impromptu talk on a variety of topics. This course is graded CR or NCR, and CR must be obtained as a requirement for graduation.

courses.label: CHE 501
courses.title: The Engineer as Entrepreneur
paras: A survey course covering the place of smail business in Canadian manufacturing. The role of innovation in organizing @ successful new business. Topics important to business startup; patents, business pians, financing new ventures, bookkeeping, marketing, government assistance, taxation, and bankruptcy.

courses.label: CHE 502
courses.title: Fundamentals of Petroleum Production
paras: Background for understanding the physical principles involved and the terminology used in petroleum production. Fundamentals of surface chemistry (capillarity), characterization of and fluid flow through porous media. Principles of production performance, water flooding and enhanced recovery techniques.

courses.label: CHE 510
courses.title: Prediction of Physico-chemical Properties
paras: Methads of estimating physico-chemical properties of gases and liquids in cases where experimental values are absent. Prediction is usually based on correlations of a form suggested in part by theory, with empirical constants based on experimental data.

courses.label: CHE 515
courses.title: Two-Phase Flow Operations
paras: Introductory theory of one-dimensional two-phase flow; conventions, definitions, homogeneous theory, separated flow (Lockhart-Martinelli), particulate characterization and behaviour, applications; two-phase flow in pipes, boiling and evaporation, filtration.

courses.label: CHE 520
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Analysis
paras: Application of advanced mathematical techniques to the analysis of chemical engineering processes.

courses.label: CHE 521
courses.title: Process Dynamics and Control 2
paras: Computer control, state space methods.
control of complex chemical systems. Prereq: CH E 321

courses.label: CHE 523
courses.title: Process Control Laboratory
paras: Experiments on process dynamics, control and analog simulation of chemical processes. Time constant, step and frequency response, controller settings, cascade control of thermal, liquid tevel, and reaction systems.
Prereq: CH EF 321

courses.label: CHE 540
courses.title: Introduction to Polymer Science
paras: Basic definitions and polymer nomenclature, molecular weight averages and distributions, constitutional and configurational isomerism, rubber elasticity, step-growth and free radical chain growth polymerizations, emulsion polymerization.
Prereq: CH E 231, CHEM 254 or equivalent
Antireq: CHEM 353

courses.label: CHE 541
courses.title: Physical Chemistry of Polymers
paras: Polymer solutions, molecular characterization of polymers, molecular weight distributions, morphology and crystallinity in polymers. Reaction kinetics and mechanism of addition and condensation polymerization.
Prereq: CH E 540

courses.label: CHE 543
courses.title: Polymer Laboratory
paras: Experimental studies of polymerization and physical properties of polymers: condensation and addition polymerization, copolymerization, molecular weight, extrusion rheology.
Coreq: CH E 541

courses.label: CHE 550
courses.title: Introduction to Extractive Metallurgy
paras: Physical and chernical nature of ores ard intermediates, introductory pyrometallurgy, hydrometallurgy and electrometallurgy, survey of extraction processes, application of the principles of thermodynamics and kinetics to metallurgical processes.

courses.label: CHE 551
courses.title: Metallurgical Chemistry
paras: lonic equilibria, thermodynamics and kinetics of reactions in solution, bonding, stability and stereochemistry of co-ordination compounds and mecheanisms of their reaction, introductory hydrometallurgy, corrosion and homogeneous catalysis.

courses.label: CHE 583
courses.title: Principles of High Temperature Extractive Metallurgy
paras: in-depth discussion of several processes of importance in Canada; blast-furnace smelting (iron, lead, zinc), steel making and other specialized refining processes, pyrometailurgical treatment of sulfide ores, and fused salt electrolysis. The emphasis is on the interplay of the underlying thermodynamic, kinetic, transport, and processengineering considerations.

courses.label: CHE 560
courses.title: Introduction to Biochemical Engineering
paras: Aspects of the life sciences of interest to the biochemical industries and to environmental pollution. Classification and growth characteristics of microorganisms. Physico-chemical properties of biological compounds. Metabolism and biochemical kinetics. Course includes some lab work.

courses.label: CHE 561
courses.title: Fermentation Operations
paras: Application of process engineering principles to the design and operation of . fermentation reactors which are widely used in the pharmaceutical, food, brewing, and waste treatment industries. Aspects of mass transfer, heat transfer, mixing, and rheology with biochemical and biological constraints. Course includes some lab work.
Prereq: CH E 560 or permission of instructor

courses.label: CHE 563
courses.title: Food Processing
paras: Applications of unsteady and steady heat and/or mass transfer operations to processing natural and texturized foods. Design and analysis of sterilization, low temperature preservation, concentration, separation and purification processes. Effects of formulation, additives, and Processing on organoleptic and nutritional quality.
Prereq: CH E 560 or permission of instructor

courses.label: CHE 570
courses.title: Air Pollution
paras: Treatment of gaseous waste products from representative Canadian industries. Characterization and toxicity of filtration, scrubbing, cycloning, electrostatic précipitation, and other chemical treatment. Legal, socio-political, economic and engineering aspects.

courses.label: CHE 571
courses.title: Water Pollution
paras: Treatment of waste water from metals processing industries; waste characterization; toxicity; recycling; treatment by electro-oxidation/reduction, ion exchange, solvent extraction, absorption, electrodialysis, reverse osmosis, etc. Economics, regulations, moral, legal, social and political implications.

courses.label: CHE 580
courses.title: Research-Design Project 1
paras: individually supervised research and/or design project on any Chemical Engineering subject chosen by the studentprofessor group. Written report required.

courses.label: CHE 581
courses.title: Research-Design Project 2 Continuation of CH E 580. Equivalent to
paras: 2 one-term courses. A written report, meeting minimum technical report standards, and a public oral presentation will be required.

courses.label: CHE 583
courses.title: Process Systems Design
paras: The undergraduate curriculum is brought together to accomplish, by team effort, the basic objective of the process engineer: the design of an integrated process. A written report, meeting minimum technical report standards, and a public oral presentation will be + required.
Course Descriptions Chemical Engineering

courses.label: CHE 585
courses.title: Technical Elective Project
paras: An individually supervised research or design project, based on 1 of the technical elective courses taken in the 4A term. A written report meeting minimum technical report standards, and a public oral presentation will be required.

Course Descriptions
Some courses are regularly given every other year, and are listed in their regular places.
Introductory Note

In all cases, it is the student's respons? bility to determine eligibility to enter a course. it is advisable to obtain special consents in writing before registration period to avoid delays and complications.
Most 300- and 400-level courses are listed as 2 lecture hours. An additional hour may be scheduled at the discretion of the lecturer, usually for a tutorial.
COURSES CARRYING NO UNIVERSITY CREDIT

courses.label: CHE 204
courses.title: Mechanics of Solids 1
paras: Stress-strain-temperature relationships. Axial tension, Thin-walled pressure vessels. Torsion of shafts.’ Bending of beams. Analysis of stresses in beams.

courses.label: CHE 222
courses.title: Differential Equations
paras: An introduction to linear and partial differential equations. Standard methods . of solution, applications to physical and engineering problems, linear equations with constant coefficients, systems of differential equations, solution by series, numerical methods, partial differential equations. Applications from Dynamics and Vibrating Systems

courses.label: CHE 265
courses.title: Structure and Properties of Materials
paras: A basic course in structure, behaviour and application of engineering materials. Bonding forces. Crystalline and amorphous structures. Structural defects. Phase transformations and equilibria. Structures and responses of metals, ceramics and polymers. Corrosion. Modes of deformation and failure.
4 lab sessions

courses.label: CHE 292
courses.title: Engineering Economics
paras: An introductory course on the principles of engineering economy. Basic concepts; capital; interest formulas and derivations; annual worth comparisons; present worth; return on investment; benefit-cost ratio depreciation effect of taxes.
CVE 24 FS 2C2T 05
Thermal Sciences

An introductory course in thermal science. Provides an understanding of thermodynamic principles as well as engineering aspects of heat transfer including applications to practical engineering problems. ’

courses.label: CHE 381
courses.title: Hydrology/Hydraulics 1
paras: Basic hydrologic principles. Elementary hydrologic design. Open channel flow. Principles of reservoir design. Dams, spillways, gates and culverts. Pumps and turbines. Hydroelectric development.

courses.label: CHE 473
courses.title: Contaminant Transport
paras: Mathematical modelling of transport phenomena in rivers, estuaries and lakes. Data collection and analysis. Thermal pollution. Non-point source contributions to pollution. Management problems. Ecological modelling.

courses.label: CHEM 517
courses.title: Performance of Separation
paras: Processes . ; : Introduction, patterns of change and Computational approaches, group _ methods, limited flows and stage requirements, capacity and efficiency of contacting devices, energy requirements, seiection, optimal design and Operation, mass transfer with chemical reaction..

courses.label: CHEM 001
courses.title: Pre-University Chemistry
paras: The course covers the material considered essential preparation for first year chemistry courses. Included are formulae, nomenclature, stoichiometry, an introduction to thermochemistry, solution chemistry, chemical equilibria, acids, bases, oxidation-reduction reactions, kinetics and bonding.
Successful completion of this course fulfills the University Admission requirements where high school chemistry is necessary. No University credit. Offered by correspondence only.
CHEM 10 F,W,S 1C 0

General Chemistry Seminar _ Required for all Chemistry students beyond Year 1, this seminar brings together students from all years to receive information conceming the activities of the Chemistry Department and the Chemical Institute of Canada, and to hear invited speakers.

courses.label: CHEM 123
courses.title: Chemica! Reactions, Equilibria and Kinetics
paras: The stoichiometry of compounds and chemical reactions; principles of equilibria, solubility and acid-base equilibria; electrochemistry; chemical kinetics. Prereq: Grade 13 Chemistry, Mathematics (Calculus) Coreq: (for Scienge students) CHEM 123L toon.

Prereq: Grade 13 Chemistry, Mathematics (Calculus)
CHEM 123 strongly recommended

courses.label: CHEM 311
courses.title: Radiochemistry

Prereq: Grade 13 Chemistry, completion of Year 1 in good standing or permission of instructor
