courses.label: CIVE 126
courses.title: Civil Engineering Concepts
paras: A continuation of GEN E 115 with applications of graphics, measurement and
other analytic principles to introductory -

problems in the various disciplines of Civil Engineering; an introduction to engineering design methods as applied to Civil Engineering and including specification development, informationgathering, concept formulation, feasibility analysis and report writing.

courses.label: CIVE 203
courses.title: Statics
paras: Equilibrium of rigid and deformable bodies. Analysis of internal forces in structures; beams, cables, arches, trusses.

courses.label: CIVE 205
courses.title: Mechanics of Solids 2
paras: Buckling and Stability. Failure hypotheses. Virtual work. Displacement analysis. Introduction to influence lines.

courses.label: CIVE 221

paras: A review of Year 1 Calculus. Hyperbolic Functions. Partial derivatives. Multiple integration with applications. Vector analysis, theorems of Green and Gauss, line integrals. Elements of Fourier series.

10 weeks only.

courses.label: CIVE 224
courses.title: Probability and Statistics
paras: Role of Probability in engineering and decision-making under uncertainty. Data analysis. Basic probability concepts. Probability distributions. Functions of random variables. Estimation theory. Empiricat determination of distrioution models. Regression analysis.

courses.label: CIVE 253
courses.title: Geology for Engineers —
paras: A study of earth processes and earth materials from an engineering point of view. Topics include: mineral and rock identification, the rock cycle, structural geology, geology of Canada, effects of water, ice and wind. Description of aggregates used in engineering works. Field trip.

paras: An introductory course in fluid
mechanics. Fluid properties, fluid statics.
Bernoulli equation; the momentum equa-
tion and applications; laminar and turbu-
lent flow; closed conduit flow; pipe
network analysis; Dimensional Analysis
and Similitude; unsteady flow in pipes. 4 lab sessions.

duction to surveying, length measure-
ments, levelling, transit surveys. Approximate cost to each student

courses.title: Seminar
paras: The engineer in society. Principles, methods and practice of Civil Engi neering. Informal lectures.

courses.title: Civil Engineering Project 1
paras: The development of problem-solving skills utilizing the systems approach to the solution of civil engineering problems. Knowledge from previous courses and the practical application of the digital computer are integrated in a team/project-oriented environment. A written report and a verbal presentation are requirements.

courses.label: CIVE 303B
courses.title: Structural Analysis 1
paras: Beams, frames, arches, trusses, cables. Statically determinate structures. Staticaily indeterminate structures. Computer applications.

The nature of intercity transport, estimating transport demands, highway transport, rail transport, air transport, pipelines.

paras: Natural systems behaviour; Man’s impacts on ecosystems; Current environmental issues in Canada; Canadian urban system; Trends in resource consumption and waste production; Population forecasting; Economic forecasting; Uroan spatial structure; Regional water management, Sources of
‘water supply; Spatial aspects of network
design; impacts of urbanization on hydrological regimes; interactions with natural systems. Not for Civil Engineering students. Cross-listed as PLAN 436.

courses.title: Geotechnical Engineering 1

6 lab sessions.

7 lab sessions.

The students are encouraged to independently identify and resolve a problem within the scope of their chosen area of specialization utilizing knowledge gained from their academic and employment experiences. A written report and a verbal presentation are requirements.

ability, structural idealizations. Building ©

courses.label: CCIV 202
courses.title: Ancient Roman Society
paras: A survey of the civilization of the Roman Republic and Empire, featuring such topics as the individual (male and female), political institutions, art, religion, philosophy, literature, socia! life and leisure activities.
Students are advised to pre-register early for this course as enrolment is limited.

courses.label: CCIV 251
courses.title: Greek History
paras: A survey of ancient Greece, emphasizing its political, military, social and economic aspects.
This course is acceptable for credit by the History Department.
CCN 252 W 3C 05
Roman History
A military, political, social and economic survey of Rome from earliest times to the Empire’s fall.
This course is acceptable for credit by the History Department.
Classical Studies accepts HIST 238 for Classical Civilization credit, but a student may not take both HIST 238 and C CW 282.
CCW 265 F 3C 05
Medieval Civilization 1
A study of medieval literature, art, architecture, music and other expressive forms. The period from late antiquity to A.D. 1200 will be studied.
CCW 265 F 3X 05
Ancient Epic in Transiation

This course examines ancient epic through the diad and Odyssey of Homer, the Argonautica of Apollonius Rhodius and the Aeneid of Vergil. The evolution of the epic genre is traced in lectures and discussions. No knowledge of Greek or Latin is needed.

CCIW 22 WS 3C 05 Social Problems in Antiquity A study of selected social problems in ancient Greece and Rome. Each year, 2 of the following will be examined: women in society, slavery and the labour force, the aged and infirm, human sexuality and sexual mores, children and education, minority groups and racial prejudice, war and conflict. Prereq: C CIV 201 or 202 or instruc tors permission
CCW 301 F 3C 05
Ancient Myth and Religion 1
A study of Greek and Roman myth, including the birth of the gods, creation, the Olympians, Prometheus and the fall, the flood, the ages of man.
CCN 3X2 WX OS
Ancient Myth and Religion 2
A study of Greek and Roman legend, including the cycles of Troy, Mycenae, Thebes; the Argonauts, the heroes, Odysseus; and the mystery religions (with their relation to Christianity).
CCN 361 F 3C 05
Greek Art and Architecture
A survey of the art and architecture of
the ancient Greek wortd from the
Minoan to the Hellenistic periods. Cross-listed as FINE 310.

courses.title: Roman Art and Architecture
paras: A survey of the art and architecture of the Roman world from Etruscan. to imperial Times.

courses.title: History of Ancient Philosophy 1
paras: From the beginnings to Plato. Cross-listed as PHIL 380.
CCN 42 W 3 05 History of Ancient Philosophy 2 From Aristotle to the close of classical antiquity.
Cross-listed as PHIL 381.

CCN 36 F X O05 Ancient Lyric and Satire in Translation Lyric poetry of Greece and Rome, including Sappho, Pindar, Catuilus, Horace and others; classical satire, including Horace, Petronius, Juvenai, Lucian. No knowledge of Greek or Latin is needed.
Prereq: C CIV 265 or 266 or an appropriate course in literature, or instructor's permission

courses.label: CCIV 371
courses.title: Christianity and the Roman
paras: Empire 1

The relationship between Christianity and the Roman Empire from the beginning to 200.A.D., including the trial of Christ, the trials of Paul, the buming of Rome in 64 A.D., and the subsequent outlawing of Christianity.
CCW 372 W X O05 Christianity and the Roman Empire 2
A continuation of C CIV 371. Topics included are the persecutions by the
Emperors Decius and Valerian, the
Great Persecution and the triumph of Christianity under the Emperor Constantine.

Course Descriptions Introductory Notes
1. EARTH 121-122 is normally regarded as a prerequisite for any Major program in Earth Sciences.

2. Second, third and fourth year courses may involve field trips in the fall. All those enrolled in Honours Earth Sciences programs are ‘required to take a two-week field camp at the end of the third year (EARTH 390). The cost will range from $50-$100 per student.
3. Regular Earth Sciences students are encouraged to seek geological employment in the summers.

courses.label: EARTH 121
courses.title: Introductory Geology 1
paras: An introduction to rocks and minerals and the processes of their formation. The structure of the earth, plate tectonics and its relationship to deformation, metamorphism and formation of magmas. Earth resources.

courses.label: EARTH 122
courses.title: Introductory Geology 2
paras: An introduction to processes that shape the earth’s landscapes. Consideration of the time concept in geology. Introduction to fossils, their occurrence and uses in earth sciences. The geologicat history of North America.

courses.label: EARTH 221
courses.title: Geochemistry 1
paras: Origin, abundance and geochemistry of elements. Introduction to stable isotope geology and radiometric dating. Basic aqueous geochemistry. Chemical characteristics of crystalline and sedimentary rocks.
Prereq: EARTH 231 or permission of instructor

courses.label: EARTH 231
courses.title: Mineratogy
paras: Introduction to systematic mineralogy. Bases of mineral classification. Interrelationships of chemical, structural and physical properties. Occurrence of major groups of rock-forming minerals. Introduction to optical properties of minerals and the use of the petrographic microscope as a tool in identifying minerals and interpreting their genetic history. Piereq: EARTH 121 ‘

courses.label: EARTH 232
courses.title: Petrography
paras: The study of rocks in thin section. The classification and identitication of sedimentary, igneous, and metamorphic rocks.
Prereq: EARTH 231

courses.label: EARTH 235
courses.title: Stratigraphy
paras: An introduction to the nature, origin and interpretation of. stratified earth materials. Emphasis on principles and approaches. Stratigraphy in earth history and economic deposits. Prereq: EARTH 121-122

courses.label: EARTH 236
courses.title: Principles of Paleontology
paras: The principles of paleontology with particular stress on the species concept and evolution; examples will be drawn Primarily from the fossil record of plants and vertebrates. Laboratory work will . include projects related to lecture topics.
Prereq: EARTH 121-122

courses.label: EARTH 238
courses.title: Introductory Structural Geology
paras: Major structural features of the earth. Concepts of stress and strain; elementary rock mechanics. The deformation of earth materials, continuous and discontinuous structures. Introduction to regional tectonics.
Prereq: EARTH 121-122

courses.label: EARTH 260
courses.title: Applied Geophysics 1
paras: An introduction to seismic, gravity, elec-
tric, electromagnetic and magnetic
methods of exploration geophysics. Preraq: PHYS 111-112 or consent of
instructor

courses.label: EARTH 331
courses.title: Igneous Petrology
paras: The principles and theories of igneous frock genesis. Silicate phase equilibria in magmatic systems. Magmatic differentiation; distribution and occurrence of magma types.
Prereq: EARTH 231, 232

courses.label: EARTH 332
courses.title: Metamorphic Petrology
paras: Principles and theories of metamorphic tock genesis. Static, dynamic and polyphasal crystalloblastic growth. Processes of solid-state crystallization in metamorphic environments. Zonal and facies classifications; facies series and the place of metamorphism in global tectonics. introduction to metasomatism.
Prereq: EARTH 232
For Honours Earth Sciences and Geological Engineering students only.

courses.label: EARTH 333
courses.title: Introductory Sedimentology
paras: The origin, transport and deposition of sediments. Size analysis and sedimentary structures. Recent sedimentary environments as a key to the interpretation of ancient sediments. Sedimentary petrology.
Prereq: EARTH 232

courses.label: EARTH 336
courses.title: Paleontology
paras: Advanced paleontology emphasizing morphology, classification, evolution, paleoecology and stratigraphic value of fossil invertebrates. Laboratory study of fossil collections.
Prereq: EARTH 236 '

courses.label: EARTH 342
courses.title: Geomorphology
paras: The process of landscape evolution and the classification of landforms. Geomorphic effects of glacial, fluvial, marine and slope processes. Physical and chemical weathering, soil formation. Laboratory study of topographic maps and air photo interpretation. Field trips. Antireq: GEOG 302

courses.label: EARTH 345
courses.title: Historical Geology
paras: A systematic review of the geological
history of North America from the
Precambrian to. the Recent exemplified
by regional geology. Laboratory work will
include study of rocks and fossil
regional suites and geological maps. Prereq: EARTH 235

courses.label: EARTH 355
courses.title: Statistical Methods in Geology
paras: Introduction to the principtes of probability and statistics and their application in the earth sciences. Evaluation of quantitative data; statistical models.
Prereq: MATH 113a/b and an intro ductory course in computer programming

courses.label: EARTH 360A
courses.title: Global Geophysics
paras: Topics in the plate tectonics, heat flow.
gravity, seismology, magnetics, electro-
magnetics and dynamics of the planet. Prereq: PHYS 121-122, EARTH 260 Offered every other year alternating
with EARTH 460.

courses.label: EARTH 368
courses.title: Geophysics 1
paras: Introductory topics on the physics of the earth. Seismology and the earth's interior. Thermal history of the earth. Gravity and isostasy. Origin of the continents and continental drift.
Prereq: MATH 113a/b, PHYS 121-122 or equivalent
Cross-listed as PHYS 368.

courses.label: EARTH 369
courses.title: Geophysics 2
paras: The geology of the ocean basins. Topics in physical oceanography. Physical properties of ocean water, heat budget of the world oceans. Oceanic circulation, Coriolis effects. Some idealized current regimes. . Prereq: MATH 113a/b and PHY. 121-122 or equivalent Cross-listed as PHYS 369.

courses.label: EARTH 370
courses.title: Economic Geology
paras: The occurrence and geological setting of metallic, non-metallic minerals and construction materials. Energy resources. Special emphasis on Canada’s resource industries. The laboratory will involve sampling methods, ore calculation and property evaluation. Prereq: EARTH 231, 232

courses.label: EARTH 390
courses.title: Methods in Geological Mapping
paras: Ten day field camp at Whitefish Fails, held at beginning of spring term.

courses.label: EARTH 421
courses.title: Geochemistry 2
paras: The application of chemical thermodynamics to geochemical problems. Development of the 3 laws of Thermodynamics; Gibbs free energy and equilibria constants. Introduction to various topics in aqueous geochemistry such as mineral equilibria; ion exchange and redox equilibria. Various aspects of organic geochemistry and geochemical exploration will also be covered.
Prereq: First year chemistry, EARTH 221
Restricted to fourth year and grad uate students.

courses.title: Crustal Evolution
paras: An analytical critique of the plate tectonics theory. Tectonic syntheses - based on the theory in the light of world geology.
Normally restricted to fourth year Earth Sciences students.

courses.label: EARTH 432
courses.title: Precambrian Geology
paras: The geology, tectonics, stratigraphy and history of the Canadian Precambrian Shield. The early evolution of the earth’s crust. The Precambrian time scale and problems of geochronology. Life, climate and physical conditions in Precambrian time.

courses.label: EARTH 433
courses.title: Applied Sedimentology
paras: The source, migration and sedimentary environment of hydrocarbons, exploration, types of traps, extraction. Carbonate sedirnents and their diagenesis. The environmental impact and control of recent sedimentation.
Prereq: EARTH 333

courses.label: EARTH 434
courses.title: Biostratigraphy
paras: Methods of using paleontological data to solve stratigraphic problems. Faunal provinces in space and time. Effects of continental drift and climatic change on biogeography through the Phanerozoic. Prereq: EARTH 336

courses.label: EARTH 435
courses.title: Advanced Structural Geology
paras: The geometry, kinematics and dynamics of structural geology. The relationships of structures from the microscopic to the megascopic scale; statistical studies of structural elements.
Prereq: EARTH 260

courses.label: EARTH 436A
courses.title: Honours Thesis
paras: (A course for Honours Earth Sciences students only.) - Each student will work under the direction of a member of the Department on a short research project. The results of this will be presented in thesis form and will be critically examined by members of this and, where pertinent, other departments.

courses.label: EARTH 437
courses.title: Rock Mechanics
paras: Review of stress and strain. Mohr's circle, strength theories, laboratory tests, classification of rocks. Rock mechanics .considerations in the construction of shafts, drifts, tunnels, foundations and rock slopes. Laboratory exercises will deal with uniaxial, triaxial, flexure, hardness and tensile testing of rock. Problem sets will be assigned.
Prereq: A course in Statics and Mechanics of deformable materials, or - consent of instructor

courses.label: EARTH 438
courses.title: Engineering Geology
paras: Review of basic concepts in soil and rock mechanics. Field and laboratory methods used to define and characterize the properties of geological materials and their use in selected engineering geologic design and construction problems. Laboratory assignments will focus on the determination of physical properties and site assessment problems.

courses.label: EARTH 439
courses.title: Hydrogeology
paras: The location, exploitation, and conservation of groundwater. Groundwatersurface-water interactions, effect of man’s activities on ground water quality, hydrogeologic aspects of subsurface waste disposal.

courses.label: EARTH 440
courses.title: Quaternary Geology Stratigraphy and history of the Quater-
paras: nary Period with emphasis on glaciation. Laboratory studies on glacial deposits. Field trips. A previous course in geomorphology is recommended. Antireq: for students majoring in Earth Sciences: GEOG 300 and GEOG 401 Not to be taken by third year students.

courses.label: EARTH 456
courses.title: Numerical Methods in Geoscience
paras: Introduction to numerical methods and their use in geology and hydrogeology. Finite differences and finite elements. Solution of boundary value problems, mathematical modelling.
Prereq: MATH 113a/b and an introductory course in computer progranr ming

courses.label: EARTH 460
courses.title: Applied Geophysics 2
paras: A detailed examination of selected topics in exploration geophysics, with an emphasis on data processing and computer modelling of geophysical responses. Prereq: EARTH 260 and an introduc tory course in computer programming Offered every other year alternating with EARTH 360A

courses.label: EARTH 461
courses.title: Applied Geophysics 3
paras: Geophysical field methods for Engineering and Hydrogeology.
Prereq: Students must be enrolled in the Geophysics Option

courses.label: EARTH 470
courses.title: Metallic Mineral Deposits
paras: The petrology and genesis of metalliferous ore deposits. The description of classic deposits; the stability of ore Minerats; ore minerals i aqueous systems. The laboratory: will include instruction and practice in ore microscopy. ve Prereg: EARTH 370 ©

courses.label: EARTH 480
courses.title: S$ fidiab: 6.5 Fleld Study ae
paras: Depending on the demand and the availability of an instructor, a 6 week field course may be offered in an area of unusual geological interest during the spring or summer. This: course will consist of 2 weeks of classroom lectures and 1 month in the field location. Expenses are to be paid by the student. Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: EARTH 490
courses.title: Field Trip
paras: One or more regional geology field trips normally conducted at the beginning of the Fall term. These trips will emphasize the integration of the various subdisciplines within Geology to achieve an understanding and synthesis of a geologically complex region such as the central and western Appalachians of southern Quebec. Field exercises will be part of the trip. Enrolment will be limited to not more than 30 students per trip. Open to Honours Earth Sciences students only. .

courses.label: ECON 101
courses.title: Colossos - The Major Figures of Ancient Greece
paras: An introductory study of the achievement of ancient Greece through some of its most prominent figures. Each year 2 of the following will be featured: Theseus: The Minoan-Mycenaean Age of Bronze; Pericies and the Rise of Democracy; Socrates, Man and Martyr, Alexander the Great and The Age of Expansion. .
CCW 102 W 3X 05
Colossos - The Major Figures of Ancient Rome

An introductory study of the achievement of ancient Rome through some of its most prominent figures. Each year 2 of the following will be featured: Julius Caesar and the Collapse of the Republic; Augustus: The Empire Rises; Nero and the Corruption of Power; Hadrian and the imperial Machine.
CCW 21 FS 3X OS

Greece, featuring such topics as the
individual (male and female), political
institutions, art, religion, philosophy.
literature, social life and leisure activities. Students are advised to pre-register

courses.label: ECON 101
courses.title: Introduction to Microeconomics
paras: An introduction to the central economic problems of society, the functioning of a mixed enterprise system, the economic role government, the composition of and pricing of national output, pricing of productive factors, and income distribution.

courses.label: ECON 102
courses.title: Introduction to Macroeconomics
paras: Determination of national income; the
banking system; government fiscal and monetary policy; intemational trade and finance; and current economic problems.

courses.label: ECON 201
courses.title: Microeconomic Theory
paras: Theory of consumer demand; production theory; market structure; resource pricing and allocation under perfect and imperfect competition.
Prereq: ECON 101

courses.label: ECON 202
courses.title: Macroeconomic Theory
paras: Theory of the determination of the level of national income, employment and the price level, and macroeconomic policies to affect these determinates.
Prereq: ECON 102
Course Descriptions ; Economics

courses.label: ECON 211
courses.title: Mathematics of Economists
paras: Application of elementary mathematics to problems in economic theory. Topics include the graphing of functions, elementary exponential and logarithmic functions and differentiation-all developed within the context of economic theory.
Prereq: ECON 101, 102
Students who have not taken Grade 13 Algebra and Calculus are strongly advised to take MATH 104.

courses.label: ECON 221
courses.title: Statistics for Economists
paras: An introduction to the underlying logic of statistical procedures most commonly employed by economists. No mathematical training beyond high school algebra is presumed. Emphasis is given to solving problems as a way of learning statistical theory.
Prereq: ECON 101, 102

Students who have taken or are taking a course of similar content in another discipline should check with their Undergraduate Officer or the Arts Registrar's Office to determine if credit will be granted for both courses.

courses.label: ECON 231
courses.title: Introduction to International Economics
paras: Theory of comparative advantage and the gains from trade; tariff theary; concepts and measurement of balance of payments; exchange rate systems; reform of international monetary system. Prereq: ECON 101, 102

courses.label: ECON 241
courses.title: Cost-benefit Analysis and Project Evaluation
paras: Methods for evaluating private and public projects; decision rules, efficiency conditions and methods of conducting cost-benefit analysis. Application of the technique.
Prereq: ECON 201

courses.label: ECON 263
courses.title: Economic History of Canada
paras: A study of the economic development of Canada; export staple theory, industrial structure and national policies analyzed in a Classical-Marxian framework.
Prereq: ECON 101, 102

courses.label: ECON 301
courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
paras: Theory of modern welfare economics with some applications; the meaning and measurement of economic efficiency and equity and their relationship to economic welfare.
Prereq: ECON 201, 202
Economics

courses.label: ECON 302
courses.title: Monetary Theory and-Banking
paras: Monetary theory and banking in an open
economy; national policies for achieving
full employment, price stability, and
equilibrium in the balance of payments. Prereq: ECON 201, 202, 231

courses.label: ECON 303
courses.title: Economic Thought
paras: A critical survey of the development of
economic thought from the pre-
Socratics to the Post-Keynesians.
Emphasis on Classical Economics. Prereq: ECON 201, 202, 231

courses.label: ECON 311
courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical
paras: Economics
Mathematica! treatment of some micro-
and macro-partial and general.
equilibrium models; programming and
other techniques; simple growth models. Prereq: ECON 201, 202, 211 (or ~
MATH 130) .

courses.label: ECON 321
courses.title: Introduction to Econometrice
paras: Introductory level course in economet- - tics; includes economic model building and testing, regression and correlation analysis, and price indices. Prereq: ECON 221

courses.label: ECON 331
courses.title: {nternational Trade and Finance
paras: An examination of theories of international trade. and finance at an intermediate level. Topics include theories of trade structure (Ricardian, Heckscher- Ohlin, and product cycle), the effects of tariffs and multinational corporation behaviour, the balance of paymenis, - and the workings of the exchange market.
Prereq: ECON 231, 201

courses.label: ECON 333
courses.title: Interregional Economics
paras: Application of economic theory to analyses of structural characteristics, growth and development in interregional systems. Models examined include integration of regional economic analysis in view of Canadian policy, export-base, shiftshare, neo-classical, cumulative causation. .
Prereq: ECON 201, 231

courses.label: ECON 335
courses.title: Economic Development
paras: The nature of the problem of economic development; theories of economic development; major policy issues in economic development.
Prereq: ECON 201, 202, 231

courses.label: ECON 341
courses.title: Public Finance
paras: The economic rationale of governmental fiscal activity, cost-benefit analysis; the structure and economic effects of public expenditure and revenues, the analysis of income, consumption and weaith taxes; introduction to fiscal federalism. Prereq: ECON 102, 201

courses.label: ECON 343
courses.title: Urban Economics
paras: Application of economic analysis to location decisions of firms and households; discussion of policy problems, for example, urban renewal and housing. Prereq: ECON 107 (ECON 201 is recommended).

courses.label: ECON 344
courses.title: Consumer Theory
paras: The development of economic principles for consumer analysis. The course examines market responsiveness as well as conditions causing problems for public and private consumption. It also evaluates alternative economic policies for correcting such conditions.
Prereq: ECON 201

courses.label: ECON 345
courses.title: Industrial Organization
paras: An analysis of the characteristics of industrial structure, behaviour and performance with special reference to Canada. Competition and "rationalization” policy in Canada and other selected countries.
Prereq: ECON 201
ECON 3681 W 3C 05 Labour Economics Wage theory, training and mobility theory; economics of information in Canadian labour markets; other investments in human capital; manpower poiicies.
Prereq: ECON 201

courses.label: ECON 353
courses.title: Population Economics
paras: Population objectives; demographic
techniques; economic interrelationships
with fertility, mortality and migration.
determinants and consequences of
current world population changes. Prereq: ECON 201

courses.label: ECON 355
courses.title: Economics of Energy and Natural
paras: Resources : An analysis of the economics of conservation, especially the adequacy of the market mechanism as an allocator of resource use over time. Issues __ conceming the economig behaviour of Canada’s fishery, forest, fuel and nonfuel mineral industries will be considered.
Prereq: ECON 207
(ECON 241 is recommended.)

courses.label: ECON 363
courses.title: Contemporary Canadian Problems 1,2
paras: A “topic oriented’ seminar course. The class agrees to study a Canadian problem selected from 4 fist that includes poverty, unemployment, industrial policy, and so forth. The format assists the student in gaining analytical skill through work on the selected topics. — «
Prereq: ECON 201, 202

courses.label: ECON 365
courses.title: Economics Devetopment of Modem
paras: Europe 1780-1973" A survey of Europe’s economic development from the Industrial Revolution to 1973, Case studies of England, France, Germany, Russia and the Soviet Union. Emphasis on technology, economic institutions, capital formation, standards of living and the role of the State. Prereq: ECON 101, 102

courses.label: ECON 381
courses.title: Special Topics
paras: One or more special half courses will be offered at different times as announced by the Department.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ECON 401
courses.title: Advanced Microeconomic Theory
paras: This course concentrates upon Walra: sian general equilibrium analysis with special reference to Debreu’s formulation and temporary equilibrium theory; the micro-foundations of Keynesian economics and the Sraffian alternative to, and critique of, supply and demand theories.
Prereq: ECON 211, 301

courses.label: ECON 402
courses.title: Advanced Macroeconomic Theory
paras: Classical and Keynesian models and
recent contributions; theory of economic
policy; inflation and unemployment.
modem theories of economic growth. Prereq: ECON 211, 221, 901, 302

ECON. 4038 W 3C 05 Economic Analysis, Forecasting, and Public Policy : ‘ The course focuses on the problems of forecasting economic activity (as measured by the principal macroeconomic variables), and of designing and implementing policies to control those variables; topics covered include a critical review of current forecasting models, problems associated with lags of the impact of policies, and so forth.
Prereq: ECON 301, 302, 321

courses.label: ECON 421
courses.title: Econometrics 2
paras: Review of linear algebra and development of basic statistical inference; formulation, identification, estimation, and tests of single equation and simultaneous equation regression models of micro- and macro-economics; empirical models. ; Prereq: ECON 201, 202, 211, 221, 321

courses.label: ECON 431
courses.title: International Economic Policy
paras: Analysis of selected policy problems of open economies, such as optimum tariff and balance of payments stabilization, international capital flows, monetary and fiscal policy mix, multinational firms, international monetary reform and the new international economic order. Prereq: ECON 301, 302, 331

courses.label: ECON 441
courses.title: Economics of the Public Sector 1
paras: An overview of fiscal functions and institutions; the theory of social goods, expenditure and revenue structures; fiscal incidence.

courses.label: ECON 442
courses.title: Economics of Public Sector 2
paras: Fiscal stabilization, fiscal federalism, public pricing, international public finance, social security and other contemporary policy issues.
Prereq: ECON 441

courses.label: ECON 451
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Resource Economics
paras: Advanced analysis of selected topics in the area of energy, land, and labour resources.

courses.label: ECON 461
courses.title: Comparative Economic Systems
paras: This course concentrates upon the criteria which are relevant for comparing different economic systems, how well various forms of economic theory make comparisons, the development of capitalist and socialist economies, together
SCC RR eee Pert or
with the analysis of altemative types of price system and planning. . Prereq: ECON 201, 202

courses.label: ECON 463
courses.title: Political Economy of Capitalist
paras: Development ; A study of the main tools and models of modern political economy. Micro and macro tools and concepts are integrated in a Marxian framework based on the work of Robinson, Sraffa, Kaldor, Pasinetti, Rowthorn, Nell, Sweezy and others in what can be termed the "Classical Martian” tradition.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ECON 472
courses.title: Advanced Public Policy and Applied Economics
paras: An advanced discussion of selected topics in macroeconomic theory, policy and empirical research. Seminar topics include the role of stabilization policy, the usefulness of income policy and evaluation of Monetarism as practiced by the Bank of Canada.
Prereq: ECON 321, 402 (may be taken concurrently)

courses.label: ECON 482
courses.title: Special Studies - Keynes and Post Keynesian Economics
paras: This course is on the recently emerging Post Keynesian school of ‘economic theory, with roots in Keynes and, through Kalecki, in Marx. An alternative to the “neoclassical synthesis” is drawn from The General Theory and other sources, and used to describe and prescribe for such modern problems as stagflation, debt crises, high interest rates and lagging growth. Topics include micro foundations of macroeconomics and the role of finance in the modern economy.
Prereq: ECON 301, 302

Course Descriptions

courses.label: ELE 123
courses.title: Electrical Engineering Circuits
paras: Introduction to network variables; resistors; Kirchhoff’s laws; circuit simplification techniques; circuit analysis methods; operational amplifiers and their uses; resistor-capacitor circuits; resistorinductor circuits; sinusoids and phasors; impedance and admittance; circuit functions and analysis techniques. Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 126
courses.title: Electricity dnd Magnetism
paras: Electrostatics; electric flux and potential energy; dielectrics, capacitors and capacitance; flow of electric charge and resistance; Kirchhoff's Voltage and Current Laws; magnetism; magnetic materials and circuits; Faraday’s Law and inductance.
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 205
courses.title: Advanced Calculus for Electrical
paras: Engineers 1
Fourier Series; Ordinary differential
equations; Laplace transform; applica: _
tions to linear electrical systems. Cross-listed as MATH 211.

courses.label: ELE 206
courses.title: Advanced Calculus for Electrical Engineers 2
paras: Partial differentiation, relative maxima and minima, directional derivatives, — divergence and curl of vector fields with applications; multiple integrals, double and triple integrals; line and surface integrals, applications of divergence and Stokes theorems. Complex analysis: limits, analytic functions, complex line integral, Cauchy's integral formula, residues. Partial differential equations. Cross-listed as MATH 212.

courses.label: ELE 208
courses.title: Electronic Circuit Analysie
paras: This is an introductory course in electronic circuit analysis which follows the first circuits course EL E 123. The topics to be discussed are: Operational ampifier applications, diodes, rectifiers, introduction to MOS and bipolar transistors, basic amplifier circuits, frequency tesponse, elementary treatments of feedback, filters and oscillators. The student is introduced to computer-aided analysis techniques using WATAND. Prereq: EL E 123 or equivalent Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 222
courses.title: Digital Computers
paras: Brief introduction to switching algebra. Information representation and arithmetic in binary systems. Computer organization. Assembly language programming, basic programming techniques. Memory units, arithmetic logic units, control units, VO devices. Translation and loading. Computer case studies. Microcomputers. . Coreq: GEN E 121 or equivalent . TOpen

courses.label: ELE 224
courses.title: Numerical Methods
paras: Application of computers to engineering problems. Number systems, errors and error propagation. Roots of nontinear equations. Solution of systems of linear equations. interpolation and numerical integration. Solution of ordinary differential equations. A non-numeric algorithm (e.g., sorting). Emphasis will be placed on algorithm development and programming style.
Prereq: GEN E 121 or equivalent

courses.label: ELE 231
courses.title: Electronic Devices
paras: Review of band theory and doped semiconductors in thermal equilibrium, charge neutrality, mass action law, recombination and transport mechanisms, Boltzmann relations, derivation of P-n junction de and ac characteristics, charge storage effects. The bipolar transistor; derivation of de and ac terminal characteristics, equivalent circuits. The Junction Field Effect transistor (JFET) and Metal Oxide Semiconductor FET, derivation of de characteris: ties.
Prereq: PHYS 125 or equivalent
Alternate weeks.
ELE 2% S 3C,1T3L' 05 ; Microelectronic Circuits and Devices
The first of a two course sequence covering the following topics: theory of devices, theory of networks, analog circuits, digital circuits, operationat amplifiers. Prereq: EL E 123 Alternate weeks

courses.label: ELE 251
courses.title: Programming Languages and Translators
paras: Oata types and representations, operations, sequence control, data control, storage management, language syntax, compilers and interpreters.
Prereq: GEN E 121

courses.label: ELE 252
courses.title: Data Structures
paras: Introduction to data and data abstraction, fundamental data structures, implementing and manipulating data structures, basic file systems.
Prereq: El. E 251

courses.label: ELE 263
courses.title: Microprocessor Systems and interfacing
paras: Microprocessor system architecture, buses, memories, peripheral connections, parallel, serial, analog interfaces, magnetic storage media, data communications, testing and debugging. Prereq: EL E 222, Et E 251 Alternate weeks

courses.label: ELE 261
courses.title: Energy Sy and Comp ts 1
paras: Comparative and historical review of energy sources and systems. Operating, security and planning principles for the electric energy generation, transmission and distribution systems. Excitation and loss analysis of ac magnetic circuits. Principtes, circuit modelling, and performance of transformers.
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 262
courses.title: Energy Systems and Components 2
paras: Principles of electromechanical energy conversion. Rotating machines. DC motors. Induction motors. Synchronous machines.
Prereq: Ef-E 261
Alternate weeks.
- ELE 269 FW 3C2T3L' 05.

Electrical Engineering 2 | Review of ac circuits. Three-phase Circuits. Transformers. Industrial power networks. Principles and operating characteristics of dc and ac motors including speed. control. Power conditioning for supplying mechanical drives. Interface of electro-mechanical systems with control circuits ant transducers. Alternate weeks. For Mechanical Engineering students only.

courses.label: ELE 316
courses.title: Probability and Statistics
paras: Conditional probability and independence; Bayes’ Theorem; random variables: functions of random variables; distribution functions; applications to feliability and failure rates; marginal and conditional distributions; correlation and applications to regression and statistical testing.

courses.label: ELE 318
courses.title: Communications Systems
paras: Orthogonality and signal representation in continuous time. Fourier spectrum, Fourier transforms and applications to communications. Convolution. Transfer functions and filters. Power spectral density. Amplitude modulation and applications to techniques such as DSB, AM, SSB; etc. Angle modulation and the spectrum of frequency modulated signals. Techniques for the generation and demodulation of FM signals. introduction to noise and its effects in AM and FM systems. Noise figure and noise temperature. ; Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 323
courses.title: Digital Circuits and Systems
paras: Switching algebra. Simplification of Boolean functions. Combinational logic. MSI/LSI combinational circuits. Sequential logic. Algorithmic state machines, implementation with MSI circuits, timing considerations. Hardwired and microprogrammed controllers. Semiconductor memories. IC families.
Open.

courses.label: ELE 332
courses.title: Electronic Circuits
paras: Amplifier biasing networks, single and multi-stage smal+signal amplifiers, the hybrid-pi model; high and low frequency effects; negative feedback amplifiers; oscillators; noise in electronic circuits; introduction to large signal amplifiers; introduction to digital circuits.
Alternate weeks
ELE 32 WS 3C,1T 05
Electrical Networks 1

Elements and equations. Differential equations. Z-transforms, Digital systems, Recursion equations. Convolution. System Function. Frequency response simulation. Analog and digitial synthesis. Fourier series. Fourier integrals.

courses.label: ELE 371
courses.title: Transmission Lines and Basic Field Theory
paras: Transmission lines: transmission line equations, steady state (sinusoidal) solution, terminated lines, matching and the Smith Chart. Basic Field Theory: vector caiculus, electrostatic and magnetostatic fields, time-varying fields and Maxwell's equations, plane wave propagation, polarization, reflection, refraction, applied boundary value problems..
Prereq: EL E 126 or equivalent
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 380
courses.title: Systems and Control
paras: An introduction to control. Advantages of closed-loop feedback systems. The role of the system mathematical model. Block diagrams and signal flow graphs. The basic contro! system design problem, stability in control systems. Frequency response analysis techniques. Root-locus analysis. Elementary lead-lag compensation. Z-transforms. Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 411
courses.title: Digital Communications
paras: Review of sampling and pulse transmission. Signa! distortion, band-width for pulse ‘transmission. Digital multiplexing, line coding, pulse shaping, detection and error rates. ISI and equalisation. Pulse-code modulation, Delta modulation, quantization and detection errors. Random processes: stationary process, power spectral density, noise, low-pass and band-pass processes. Effect of noise on communication systems: noise in PCM systems, optimum threshold detection, matched filter. Carrier systems with coherent and non-coherent detection.
Prereq: EL E 318, EL E 316 or by Permission of instructor

courses.label: ELE 412
courses.title: Data Communication
paras: Representation of signals, gaussian processes, optimum receiver, equivalent signal sets, non-white channel noise, maximum likelihood and minimax receiver. Information and its measure, source encoding, error-free communication, channel capacity. Error-correcting codes: linear block codes, cyclic codes, convolution codes.
Prereq: EL E 411 or permission of instructor

courses.label: ELE 413
courses.title: Digital Signal Processing
paras: Discrete systems for-signal processing, in particular linear filtering, are rapidly replacing analog forms. This course serves a8 an introduction to the analysis and design of linear, time invariant discrete systems, with both software and hardware implementations.

courses.label: ELE 426
courses.title: Software Engineering
paras: Block structured languages, actual and formal parameters, recursion, formal description, relationship to machine code. Compilers. Data structures, arrays, lists, stacks, associative structures. Searching and sorting. Operating system organization, co-operating processes, process synchronization primitives. Structured software design, software testing and maintenance.
Prereq: EL E 222 or equivalent
"Project.

courses.label: ELE 427
courses.title: Digital Systems Engineering
paras: Complexity in digital systems and its control: microprogramming, multiprogramming, paging, segmentation, capabilities. Hardware-software homomorphism; evolution of microprocessor - , architectures. Performance estimation. Prereq: EL E 323 and either EL E 426 or CS 354 or equivalent Open.

courses.label: ELE 428
courses.title: Computer Communications Networks
paras: Use of computer networks. Network architecture. ISO reference model. Network topology, connectivity analysis, delay analysis, local access design. Physica! layer, data link layer, higher layer protocols. Routing, flow control, congestion control. Local area networks. Prereq: EL E 222, EL E 316, EL E 318

courses.label: ELE 435
courses.title: Semiconductor Devices Metal-Semiconductor junctions (Schottky
paras: barriers), heterojunctions, solar cell, light emitting diode, photodetector diode, . JFETs, MESFETs, MOSFETs, VLSI bipolar and MOS devices, CCDs, Power devices (SCRs, power switching transistors, PIN rectifier diodes). ‘

courses.label: ELE 436
courses.title: Design of Integrated Circults and Devices
paras: Design and process details of discrete bipolar, JFET and MOSFET devices. Design and implementation of VHSIC and VLSI digital and analog integrated circuits. Process, device and circuit CAD.
Project.

courses.label: ELE 437
courses.title: Integrated Electronic Systems
paras: Integrated system design; memary cells and systems; logic arrays; analog - system design; application: in digital signal processing; applications in data processing.
"Project.

courses.label: ELE 438
courses.title: Switching and Digital Circults
paras: Switching characteristics of semiconductor devices, non-sinusoidal wave generation and shaping, comparators, digital integrated circuits, including ECL, TAL, I7L, STL, MOS, CMOS.
"Project.

effect transistors. Analysis of operational
amplifiers. IC temperature compensation
and biasing. Differential, low noise and
power amplifiers, receiver front end
design, noise analysis. Modulators.
mixers, detectors. Power supplies. "Project.

courses.label: ELE 443
courses.title: Electrical Networks 2
paras: Topics from the following: two-port descriptions of ideal devices, including operational amplifiers; network functions, formulation and solution of network equations; sensitivity calculations in the frequency domain; active networks their analysis; simple filter design; time domain solutions; simulation; introduction to digital and switched capacitor networks; computer-aided analysis and design of networks. Prereq: EL E 342 or equivalent Project. -

courses.label: ELE 446
courses.title: Linear Systems
paras: Three types of linear multivariable systems are studied.
1. real time-continuous systems; 2. real time-discrete systems; and 3. modulo-two time-discrete systems.

The unifying approach of state equations is developed andthe importance of linear algebra is emphasized. Topics include: time domain analysis, transform analysis (Laplace- and Z-transforms), stability considerations, system equivalence, system decomposition, system realization. The necessary matrix and linear-aigebra theory is developed as required.

courses.label: ELE 459
courses.title: Sound, Noise and Electroacoustics
paras: An interdisciplinary study of acoustical physics, human response to sound and audio engineering. Main topics include the physics of sound, acoustical measurements, human hearing, environmental noise, electroacoustical systems and_ transducers.
Every third week.

courses.label: ELE 463
courses.title: Power Electronics
paras: Characteristics and ratings of power semi-conductor devices with emphasis on the thyristor. General methods of achieving design objectives. Performance and analysis. of power conversion circuits for both static and rotating loads.
Open.

courses.label: ELE 464
courses.title: High Voltage and insulation Engineering
paras: Nature and origin of high voltage surges encountered on power systems. Travelling waves on transmission systems; - insulation engineering, electrostatic fields in high voltage apparatus, insulation failure; corona; insulation testing; circuit breakers and surge protection devices; insulation coordination.
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 465
courses.title: Power Systems
paras: Introduction to system concepts; aspects of power system planning and operation. Energy sources; environmental and resource implications. Perunit and co-ordinate systems. Representation of equipment such as generators, transformers and transmisgion lines in system analysis. Analysis of imbalanced systams and faults. Voltage and reactive power control. Load/ frequency control. Power transfer and system stability. Introduction to load flow methods. High voltage de transmission.

courses.label: ELE 473
courses.title: Microwave Engineering
paras: Review of Maxwell’s equations, rectangular and circular waveguide, microwave Circuits, scattering matrix theory, microwave filters, simple waveguide discontinuities, klystrons and magnetroris. Prereq: EL E 371 or equivalent Every third week.

and of antenna and propagation engi-
neering; linear antennas, linear arrays.
aperture antennas, frequency indepe-
dent antennas, measurement theory. Prereq: EL E 371 or equivalent lEvery third week.

courses.label: ELE 475
courses.title: Guided Wave Engineering
paras: Conducting waveguiding structures; rectangular and circular waveguides, microstrip theory and applications, numerical field analysis on microstrip tines, microstrip components. Dielectric waveguidiing structures; dielectric slab waveguides, propagation theory for step-index fibres and graded-index fibres. Fibre measurements; loss measurments, time-domain and frequencydomain measurements, measurement of refractive index profiles. Fibre-optical telecommunication systems; system design considerations, fibre characteristics, source and detector characteristics. Project

courses.label: ELE 481
courses.title: Design of Analog and Digital Contro! Systems
paras: Review of performance specifications for design. Design of analog control systems using transform techniques. Analysis of discrete-time systems using the Z-transform. Sampled data systems. Design of digital control systems using transform techniques.
TAltermate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 482
courses.title: Multivariable Control Systems
paras: Review of multivariable state space methods with emphasis on control applications. Performance indices and optimal control. Continuous and discrete time state feedback control of linear systems. Systems with inaccessible states. Stability analysis. .
Prereq: EL E 446, EL E 481
Open lab.

courses.title: Computer Control Applications
paras: Realization of digital controllers: digitalanalog equivalences, sampling and quantization effects, fixed-point arithmetic realizations. Real-time computer interfacing: hardware and programming considerations. Modelling and simulation of processes for control design applications. Detailed study of an example application.
Prereq: EL E 426, EL E 481
Project.

GROUP ONE

Courses in this group count towards a degree as electives in any program in the University. Normally, none of them qualifies as a major credit for a General or Honours program in English (see Note 1). These courses are primarily designed to make students aware of the different functions of language in various contexts and to assist them to improve their writing.

courses.label: ENGL 109
courses.title: Introduction to Essay Writing 1
paras: The course teaches the construction of the expository essay, with attention to the structure of good paragraphs, to techniques of putting the essay together, and to the nature of the language. Ten to 12 short writing assignments are required. Also offered at St. Jerome's College. Students may receive credit for only 1 of ENGL 109 and ENGL 129R.

courses.label: ENGL 110
courses.title: Introduction to Essay Writing 2
paras: The course deals with the persuasive essay. Attention will be given to the elements of logical thinking and the techniques of persuasion. The demand. of the library research paper w. be considered.
Prereq: ENGL 109

courses.label: ENGL 129R
courses.title: Introduction to Written English
paras: Instruction provided in basic grammar, sentence and paragraph structure, elements of composition and essay writing including focus on theme, development of central idea, exposition and argumentation. Minimum of 4 hours of instruction each week with additional tutorial hours as required.
Prereq: Open only to students whose maternal language is not English and who lack language mastery sufficient for admission to other introductory English language courses

courses.label: ENGL 140R
courses.title: The Use of English 1
paras: The use and abuse of spoken and written English. The study and evaluation of language as it is used for various purposes (e.g., colloquial, scientific, legal, political, commercial, journalistic, literary) in order to increase critical awareness and to help students to write clearly and effectively.

courses.label: ENGL 141R
courses.title: The Use of English 2
paras: A continuation of ENGL 140R. The study
of factual, emotive, scientific and imagi-
native writing; relevance, context.
meaning, tone, feeling and intention. Prereq: ENGL 140R

courses.label: ENGL 150
courses.title: English as an Instrument of Thought and Communication 1
paras: The course is designed to improve the reading and writing of students from all disciplines. In order to develop clarity of thought and critical awareness, students will identify and study in several media the various ends that are served by language; objective reporting; persuasion; argument; and emotional, social and artistic expression. About 8 written exercises are assigned.

courses.label: ENGL 151
courses.title: English as an instrument of Thought
paras: and Communication 2
A continuation of ENGL 150. From a
basis of simple semantics and elemen-
tary logic, students will proceed to
examine more complex language in
fiction and other forms of literature.
About 6 written exercises are assigned. Prereq: ENGL 150

courses.label: ENGL 210
courses.title: Report Writing
paras: The many functions of the report - an orderly and objective communication of factual information which serves some specific purpose - are taught. Students will receive practice in research, in organization and in writing many kinds of reports.
Prereq: Second-year standing or above

courses.label: ENGL 240R
courses.title: Form and Function 1
paras: The uses of literacy and the functions of language as acquired in ENGL, 140F/141R. These will be applied to the more advanced form of the literary and critical assignment essay, involving comparison, evaluation and exposition.
GROUP TWO
Courses in this group carry degree credit and may be counted as fulfilling the minimum requirements for a General or Honours pragram in English.

ENGL 102 AJB: .. The Major Forma of Literature Different kinds of literature will be explored to discover how the shape of a literary work contributes to its meaning. Students will read novels, poetry, short stories and drama.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 102A
paras: The Major Forms of Literature: Short Stories and Drama A study of short stories and drama to determine how the shape of a literary work contributes to its meaning.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 102B
paras: The Major Forms of Literature: Noveis and Poetry A study of novels and poetry to determine how the shape of a literary work contributes to its meaning.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 108A
courses.title: The Nature and Structure of the
paras: English Language : Introduction to the study of the English language. Topics to be discussed include the nature and origin of language, the structure of English and its development, and the relations between language and reality.

courses.label: ENGL 108B
courses.title: Varieties of English
paras: Introduction to the study of varieties of
the English language - regional, social.
temporal, functional, and stylistic. The
relations of languages and literature and
of speech and writing will be discussed. Prereq: ENGL 103A or consent of
instructor
ENGL 105A/B A close examination of a representative selection of works by major British, Canadian, American and other authors writing in English.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 105A
courses.title: 20th Century Literature in English
paras: 1900-30 A close examination of a representative selection of works by major authors writing in English such as W.B. Yeats, Virginia Woolf, D.H. Lawrence, T.S. Eliot, and Ernest Hemingway.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 105B
courses.title: 20th Century Literature in English, |
paras: 1930-80 A continuation of ENGL 105A. A close examination of a representative selection of works by major authors writing in English such as William Faulkner, Dylan Thomas and Margaret Laurence. Prereq: ENGL 105A or consent of instructor Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 108
courses.title: Themes of Literature
paras: An exploration of the great variety of literature through thematic perspectives.

courses.label: ENGL 108A
courses.title: The Hero
paras: A study of human excellence in thought and action embodied in representative men and women, as seen through works of literature.

courses.label: ENGL 108E
courses.title: Women in Literature
paras: A study of the nature and role of women in British, Canadian and American literature. Works by both men and women will be studied in which women are seen in such forms as mothers, saints, sex objects and witches.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.
English

courses.label: ENGL 108F
courses.title: The Rebel
paras: A study of various works of literature in which the protagonist is a rébel against existing norms. The course will examine a number of rebel types and concepts, moral implications and final outcomes either is successful realization or in tragic defeat.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 108H
courses.title: Isolation and Alienation
paras: The study of a variety of works centering on the theme of man in crisis, the stress being on the individual at variance with his inner self, his fellow man or his world. The course will discuss the process in which wisdom and maturity are gained as the ultimate products of suffering.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 190
courses.title: Shakespeare
paras: Designed for students in ali faculties, the course examines some of Shakespeare’s comedies, history plays and tragedies. Shakespeare's variety and flexibility in developing characters and dramatic structures are stressed, as are significant themes.
No previous work in Shakespeare is required.
ENGL 200A/B Survey of British Literature An historical survey of major figures, types and trends in British literature from the Middle Ages to the present.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 200A
courses.title: Survey of British Literature 1
paras: An historical survey of major figures, types and trends in British literature from the Middle Ages to the late 18th century.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 200B
courses.title: Survey of British Literature 2
paras: An historical survey of major figures.
types and trends in British literature from
the late 18th century to the present. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 201
courses.title: The Short Story
paras: This course deals with the.history and techniques of the short story, with emphasis upon works by such British, American and Canadian writers as Henry James, James Joyce, D.H. Lawrence, Ernest Hemingway and Alice Munro. .
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.
Engileh
ENGL 2024/8
The Bible and Literature
The study of major themes, stories, myths and characters of the Old and New Testaments of the King James Bible, and their influence on other English literature.

courses.label: ENGL 202A
courses.title: The Bibie and Literature 1
paras: Selections from Hebrew Scripture will be Studied in relation to English literature.

courses.label: ENGL 202B
courses.title: The Bible and Literature 2
paras: The course will continue the study of the Bible, emphasizing the Christian gospels and epistles in relation to English literature.
Prereq: ENGL 202A or consent of instructor

courses.label: ENGL 203
courses.title: Introduction to Folklore 1
paras: An introduction to the scope and aims of folklore, together with a survey of the major types of folklore in the English tradition from nations of the Englishspeaking world. Topics such as oral literature, myth, legend, tale and marchen will be discussed.

courses.label: ENGL 204
courses.title: Introduction to Folkiore 2
paras: Similar to 203 but dealing with folkdrama, ballads, songs, medicines, tiddies, chants, proverbs and charms.

courses.label: ENGL 206R
courses.title: The Canadian Short Story
paras: Exploration of the Canadian short story, from its beginnings - in the bush, in the north, on the land, in the small towns - through the struggles of an urbanizing society to the present. Students will be expected to work in some depth with individual authors.

courses.label: ENGL 208A
courses.title: Forms of Fantasy
paras: This course will deal with the history and forms of fantasy written for adults. In considering the genre, related forms like the romance, the fairy tale, the fable and the gothic horror story will be discussed. Authors such as Morris, C.S. Lewis, Tolkien, Williams and White will be studied.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 208B
courses.title: Science Fiction
paras: Various examples drawn, for instance, from Utopian and anti-Utopian science ~ fiction, social science fiction, “gadget” science fiction, parapsychology, and altermate worlds and beings will be considered. Some attention will be given to the historical development of the genre.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 208C
courses.title: Studies in Children’s Literature
paras: This course will deal with classic works. of children’s literature, including fantasy written primarily for children. Selections from such authors as Kipling, Woolf, C.S. Lewis, George MacDonald, Kenneth Grahame and Thurber will be studied.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.
Modern Satire

The mode of satire in the fiction, drama, poetry and discourse of the 20th century. Particular attention to the literary works of Waugh, Huxfey, Orwell, Parker, Heller, Hiebélt and a dramatist of the absurd, but also attention to satiric cartoons and nightclub satire.

courses.label: ENGL 208E
courses.title: Women Writers of the 20th Century
paras: A study of such major 20th-century writers as Woolf, Hellman, Murdoch, McCarthy, Lessing, Laurence, Plath and Atwood. Emphasis will be on’ the concerns of these writers with the roles of women, the writer’s search for new Meanings and their innovations in literary forms.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 206H
courses.title: Arthurian Legend
paras: The story of Arthur and his knights of the Round Table will be discussed as it is treated at various times in various works and genres. Such matters will be considered as the character of Arthur, the concept of Camelot and the Fellowship of the Round Tabie.

courses.label: ENGL 208K
courses.title: Detective Fiction
paras: The history and characteristics of the "detective novel,” the "novel of crime” and the “thriller.” Attention will also be given to the novel of intrigue and espicnage. Such authors as Poe, Collins, Doyle, Chesterton, Hammett, Buchan, Greene, Deighton and Le Carre will be discussed. The course includes the examination of critical approaches to the form of detective fiction.
ENGL 2080 0.5 ; Ordered Chaos: The Apocatyptic Vision in Literature

A study of dehumanized worlds in fiction that can be called “apocalyptic.” Works by such writers as St. John the Divine, Shakespeare, Mary Shelley, Aldous Huxley, Mordecai Richler and Kurt Vonnegut will be studied.

courses.label: ENGL 209
courses.title: Writing Strategies
paras: Students practise effective writing along with the study of established models. The goal is to develop language competence to meet a variety of academic, business, and professional situations.
Prereq: Second-year standing or above .
Counts as an English Major credit as of Fall 1984.

ENGL 211/212 . The Novel The novel, by its nature, constitutes an attempt to formulate and to interpret the bewildering human experience. This course undertakes an exploration of the forms that attempt can take. British, . Canadian and American novels will be studied. The 2 haives' of the course may be taken independently.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 211
courses.title: The Nove! 1
paras: The study of the novel in English from
its beginnings to the late 19th century. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 212
courses.title: The Novel 2
paras: The study of the novel in English from
the late 19th century to the present. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 214
courses.title: Themes in Canadian Literature
paras: The course will survey a theme which is significant to the understanding of the Canadian literary mind. Topics will vary from section to section.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 232
courses.title: The Development of Drama to 1660
paras: A study of the origins and development of English drama, with special concentration on 16th-century non- Shakespearean drama.
Students may receive credit for only one of ENGL 232 or DRAMA 252.

courses.label: ENGL 233

A study of the principal playwrights.
plays, and movements in dramatic
history from the re-opening of the thea-
tres in 1660 to the present day. Students may receive crdit for only
one of ENGL 233 or DRAMA 253.

Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.title: The Practice and Theory of Criticism 1

courses.label: ENGL 305A
courses.title: Old English 1
paras: An introduction to the English language in its earliest form and to English prose in pre-Conquest England, examining Old English prose style, its principal practitioners and their world view.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 305B
courses.title: Old English 2
paras: An introduction to Old English poetry, noting in representative Old English poems those things about its purpose, style and its audience which make it unique but which also. provide the beginnings of the English poetic. tradition.
Prereq: ENGL 305A

(formerly ENGL 375A)

Prereq: ENGL 306A
(formerly ENGL 375B)

courses.title: Historical Linguistics
paras: Introduction to historical reconstruction and comparative analysis. Basic phonological, morphological, syntactic changes as they manifest themselves in language will be examined.
Prereq: ENGL 306A
(formerly ENGL 373A)

courses.label: ENGL 306D
courses.title: The History of English
paras: Introduction to the linguistic history of English from earliest documents to the present, with some consideration of various modern dialects. , Prereq: ENGL 306A (formerly ENGL 373B)

Introductory Note

There are a number of courses offered in the Faculty of Environmental Studies of an integrative nature which extend across the academic interests of the 4 units, School of Architecture, Department of Geography, Department of MarrEnvironment Studies, and School of Urban and Regional Planning. The courses are of a general interest and are open to ail students in the Univer sity. There is not an actual Department of Environmental Studies. Students interested in this area are urged to consult the course offerings of the 4 individual units mentioned above. These four departments/schools offer a variety of related courses allowing in-depth studies of topics covered in the Envi ronmental Studies courses.

courses.label: ENVS 195
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Studies
paras: Theories, methods and concepts in study of the environment. Emphasis on
‘natural and built environment and rela-
tionships between elements of the environment. Environmental planning, management, and design discussed.

courses.label: ENVS 200
courses.title: Fleid Ecology
paras: Introduces the main concepts and principles of ecology, the cycling of elements; energetics and structural organization of major ecological systems; population dynamics; impact of natural resource management practices and urban and industriat development
_ on the environment; incorporating envi-
ronmental quality considerations into development activities. There are weekly field trips to study natural and disturbed ecosystems, urban and applied ecology.
Prereq: Second, third and fourth year students only

courses.label: ENVS 201
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Planning Law
paras: Introduction to legal concepts generally and to environmental and planning law concepts in particular. Designed both. for students who do not pian to take further in-depth legal courses and as a prerequisite for senior legal courses - ENV S 401 and ENV S 402. Topics to be covered include Sources of Law, Nature of Legal Remedies, Common Law, Judicial Review, Administrative Agencies and the law relating to them, Planning Act, Environmental Protection and Assessment Acts, and Federal
Fisheries Act.

courses.label: ENVS 202
courses.title: Social Sclence Approaches to Environmental Problems
paras: Research strategies for understanding and addressing environmental problem/ opportunity situations based on concepts and methods derived from the social and behavioural sciences. Particular attention is given to determining the appropriate mix of research strategies for a range of situations in terms of data validity and reliability, time and financial constraints, and ethical considerations. Prereq: Second year students or consent of instructor.

courses.label: ENVS 252
courses.title: Media Tools for Environmental Studies
paras: Instruction in basic black and white photography relating to photography’s role as a media tool; basic darkroom functions, camera operation, composition, photographic theory, and photo essay production. Much of the course work and projects will be done outside the classroom in field situations of envifonmental concern using initiative in project development. Students are expected to supply their own cameras. A limited number of cameras will be available on a rental basis.
Prereq: ENV S students; others with consent of instructor

ENV S 2683 W 3C 05 Media Tools for Environmental Studies - Advanced Level Builds on work performed in the basic course. Photographic colour theory and practice, basic audio recording, editing and production, and presentation formats are investigated in workshop situations. A major project is developed using pre-research material assigned by the instructor. Students work in small groups to produce a slide-sound program of environmental concern. Prereq: ENV S 252

courses.label: ENVS 271
courses.title: Introduction to Quantitative Research Methods —
paras: An introduction to scientific method; descriptive and inferential statistics, sampling design. The course emphasizes the methodological and interpretative problems involved in using selected quantitative methods to investigate selected environmental topics.
Prereq: Only for students in Envirorr mental Studies
Students may receive credit for only one of ENV S 271 and PSYCH 292, STAT 202, 204, 205, 210, 220

courses.title: Computer Programming in Environmental Studies
paras: The course emphasizes programming
skills and applications in the context of environmental problems. Prereq: ENV S 271 \

Students will carry out a number of empirical exercises and Projects on various aspects of environmental perception and behaviour. Prereq: Second, third or fourth year students only

courses.title: Environmental Law
paras: An advanced, in-depth version of ENV S 201, providing an opportunity for detailed analysis of institutional factors regulating the natural environment and resources development in Ontario and Canada. How satisfactory present statutes, court systems and boards are for improving environmental quatity as well as alternatives to these legal-institutional approaches will be discussed.
Prereq: ENV S 201

Prereq: ENV S 201 .

Scrutiny of current “concepts” of future environments, including distillation of works of Bell, Clarke, Commoner, de Chardin, de Jouvenal, Dror, Doxiadis, Ehrlich, Forrester, Fuller, Kahn, Mead, Meadows, McHale, Michael, Polak, Theobald, Thompson, Toynbee and Ward.

courses.title: Ethics and The Engineering Profession
paras: An application of philosophical analysis and theories of ethics to issues of moral conduct in the engineering profession. Not open to Year 1 students.
