Course Descriptions
Courses not offered in the current academic year are listed at the end of this section.

courses.label: GEOG 101
courses.title: Introduction to Human Geography
paras: An introduction to human geography through a survey of some of the concepts, methods, techniques and applications of geographic analysis to man’s cultural environment. Directed towards the man-land theme and the location analysis theme.

courses.label: GEOG 102
courses.title: Introduction to Physical Geography
paras: Emphasis on the natural environment as an integrated system. Selected aspects of weather-climate, water, soils, biota, landforms along with flows of energy, water and matter and their effects on the subsystems of the natural environment.

courses.label: GEOG 110
courses.title: Introduction to the Field of Geography
paras: An introduction for first year geogra-° phers to: Geography as a profession, different approaches to solving geographical problems, research report writing, and to the Geography program at the University of Waterloo.
Prereq: First year Geography Majors only or 1st year Arts students intending to major in Geography or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 125A
courses.title: " Introduction to the Third World
paras: A study of the Third World under topics such as: population issues, planning and practices; education and health in the social development process; urbanization and industrialization; planning for rural and urban development in Asia, Africa and Latin America.

courses.label: GEOG 127
courses.title: Regional Problems of Europe
paras: An introduction to the Geography of Europe which examines agricultural, industrial and urban problems. Lectures, discussions and visual presentations based on field experience of instructors.

courses.label: GEOG 160
courses.title: Introduction to Cartography and Map Analysis
paras: Basic concepts involved in the analysis and use of existing types of cartographic products. Background theory of the production and reproduction of topographic and thematic maps, including historical development, collection of data and symbolization.
Lab fee $15-$25.

courses.label: GEOG 201A
courses.title: Geomorphology and Soils
paras: The roles of geomorphological and soit forming processes in creating and modifying landscapes. The utility of geomorphological information in our everyday lives.
Prereq: GEOG 102

courses.label: GEOG 201B
courses.title: Climatology
paras: Study of the atmospheric regime. The
general circulation model of the atmos-
phere together with processes involved.
climatic classification; effect of climate
on human activities and on the distribu-
tion of natural vegetation and soils. Prereq: GEOG 102

courses.label: GEOG 202
courses.title: Economic and Urban Geography
paras: An analysis of the locational structure of economic activities in the context of regional development, with the use of case studies. Basic concepts and tools are used to analyse the location structure of primary, secondary and tertiary activities.
Prereq: A 1st year human geography course

courses.label: GEOG 203
courses.title: Cultural and Regional Geography
paras: The approach of the regional geographer is illustrated by reference to one or more world regions. Political, social and historical processes are studied as they affect man’s perceptions of his environment and the identification of culture regions.
Prereq: A 1st year human geography course.

courses.label: GEOG 204
courses.title: Soviet Union
paras: Introduction to the geography of the Soviet Union, with a focus on selected problems in urbanization, industrialization, resource use and regional. economic development in a planned economy.
ood

courses.label: GEOG 205
courses.title: Africa
paras: The geography of modern Africa south of the Sahara in the context of changing attitudes to the continent on the part of the “developed” countries. Attention will focus on problems of the physical, social and economic environments.

courses.label: GEOG 220A
courses.title: World Regional Geography
paras: Study in depth of selected areas of the world’s climatic regions, emphasizing characteristic problems as well as their physical, cultural and economic interrelationships: resource use, population pressure, urban and rural land use, human impact on the earth.

courses.label: GEOG 220B
courses.title: World Regional Geography
paras: A continuation of GEOG 220A. Prereq: GEOG 220A

courses.label: GEOG 221
courses.title: The United States
paras: Focuses on population shifts, environmental issues, and regional economic development in the context of the nation and selected regions.

courses.label: GEOG 225R
courses.title: Urbanization in the Third World
paras: An analysis of the factors behind the rapid urbanization of selected areas in Asia, Africa and Latin America, with an examination of related problems of urban planning and development control policies.
Prereq: Any Faculty of Environmental Studies course.

courses.label: GEOG 232
courses.title: Geography of Population
paras: Population geography and its relationship to demography and human ecology. Analysis of the growth, diffusion, and distribution of human popula-
_ tions throughout the world.

courses.label: GEOG 251
courses.title: Cities in Canada |
paras: An introduction to some basic concepts
in urban studies emphasizing a system-
atic approach to processes and prob-
lems of urban development in Canada. Field trip fee $5-$10.

courses.label: GEOG 275
courses.title: Introductory Air Photo Analysis and Remote Sensing
paras: Basic characteristics of various remote sensing techniques and their application in the broad field of geographic and environmental studies. Emphasis on the analysis and interpretation of air photos in 3 dimensions.
Lab fee $20.
Course Deecriptians Geography

courses.label: GEOG 300
courses.title: Geomorphology and the Southem
paras: Ontario Environment ; Emphasizes field work and field trips in exploring the evolution of S. Ontario landforms. The identification of landforms, landform assemblages and their relationships. The meaning and utility of this information in terms of the contemporary and future environment will be stressed.
Prereq: Third and fourth year students only with GEOG 201A or consent of instructor
Lab fee $10-$15.

courses.label: GEOG 303
courses.title: Geographical Hydrology
paras: Study of the land based hydrological cycle and water balance with Canadian emphasis. Focus on snowcover, glacier ice, ground ice, streams and lakes and their physical, ecological and socioeconomic significance.
Prereq: GEOG 201A and B or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 307
courses.title: Social Survey Techniques
paras: Social research and the planning « * process, interview and self administered surveys; questionnaire design; profile data; sampling; data processing; nonsurvey data collection techniques; practical applications.
Prereq: Second or third year students with ENV S 271 or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as PLAN 307.
Students may receive credit for only one of GEOG 307 and PLAN 307.

courses.label: GEOG 311
courses.title: Regional Industrial Development
paras: Manufacturing and transportation in the context of economic development at regional and urban scales. Empirical focus on Canada and the U.K.
Prereq: GEOG 202 or consent of instructor ‘

courses.label: GEOG 315
courses.title: Agricultural Geography
paras: The geographical dimensions of agricultural systems. Diffusion of innovations, regional evolution of agricultural structure and vertical integration. Comparative study of programs of government intervention in agriculture in Canada and Europe. Some field trips.
Prereq: GEOG 202 or consent of instructor
Geography

courses.label: GEOG 316
courses.title: Multivariate Statistics
paras: The theory and application of multivariate statistics, with particular emphasis upon the use of the computer.
Prereq: ENV § 271 or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as PLAN 316.
Students may receive credit for only one of GEOG 316 and PLAN 316.

courses.label: GEOG 318
courses.title: Spatial Analysis
paras: Advanced quantitative analysis and sampling in a spatial context. A selection of techniques from gravity models, linear programming, nearest neighbour analysis, Markov chain analysis, graph theory, simulations, and trend surface analysis.
Prereq: ENV S 271 or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as PLAN 318.
Students may receive credit for only one of GEOG 318 and PLAN 318

courses.label: GEOG 319
courses.title: Economic and Social Techniques tor Regional Planning ’
paras: Critical appraisal of a selection of
descriptive and evaluative regional anal

ysis techniques. Economic considerations of regional development. Reliability and applicability of data; input-output analysis; cost-benefit analysis; planning, programming and budgeting systems; and social area analysis.
Prereq: ECON 101, 102 or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as PLAN 319.
Students may receive credit for only one of GEOG 319 and PLAN 319

courses.label: GEOG 322
courses.title: Geographical Study of Canada Geographical basis of Canada and
paras: Canadian issues. Selected problems relating to nationalism, regionalism, environmental quality, urbanization, regional disparities and resource davelopment.

courses.label: GEOG 323
courses.title: Comparative Regional Problems
paras: A geographical analysis of selected regions and current problems. The theme chosen in any given year will vary.

courses.label: GEOG 325R
courses.title: Special Topics in Development of the Third World
paras: Specific themes related to environmental, social and economic development problems of tropical Africa, South and South-East Asia, Caribbean and Latin America will be selected for seminars and discussions.
Prereq: First or second year courses related to Third World studies or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 330
courses.title: Cultural Geography
paras: The Geography of culture and the role of cultural factors in environmental relationships.

courses.label: GEOG 331
courses.title: Special Topics in Cultural Geography
paras: A detailed investigation of selected issues in man’s relations with the natural environment. Given as a seminar, issues will be partially selected on the basis of the interests of participants.
Prereq: GEOG 330 or consent of instructor.
“GEOG 332 W 3C 05

Topics in Population Geography: Health and Disease Population geography concepts and issues in studying health related problems. Areal variations and associations of diseases and environment. Topics include: morbidity, mortality patterns, “population at risk”, malnutrition, poverty, access to modern health care, and alternative health care systems. Regional case studies from the developing countries.
Prereq: 2nd year students or higher

courses.label: GEOG 341
courses.title: Historial Geography of Canada 1
paras: The changing geographics of settlement and resource use from the Discoveries to the early nineteenth century.
Prereq: A second year human geography course or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 342
courses.title: Historical Geography of Canada 2
paras: The changing geographies of settlement and resource use in the nineteenth and
_early twentieth centuries.
Prereq: A second year human geography course or consent of instructor.

GEOG M45 F 3XC 05 Political Geography A study of differences from place to place in political phenomena. Subjects covered include the interrelationships of states and nations, centripetal and centrifugal “forces” within states, electoral geography, boundary and frontier problems, the location of capital cities, internal organization of states, external relations, and geopolitics.
Prereq: A second year human geography course or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 349
courses.title: The City as a System
paras: Theories, models, and research procedures in the study of internal urban structure. Focuses on city-wide processes, urban land use, spatial economics, interaction systems, decision-making, urban growth, and the processes of development and redevelopment.
Prereq: GEOG 202 or 251 or consent of instructor
Field trip fee $5-$10

courses.label: GEOG 360
courses.title: Regional Urban Systems
paras: Theories, models and research procedures dealing with the growth and support of urban centres and city systems and their role in regional development. -
Prereq: GEOG 202 or GEOG 251 or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 362
courses.title: The Rural-Urban Fringe
paras: Comparative study of the natural, economic and cultural environments of / the rural-urban fringe-in the Westem World. Emphasis on the use, ownership, development and management of land and the interrelationships between the resource base and urban demands on it.
Prereq: GEOG 202

courses.label: GEOG 356
courses.title: Resources Management
paras: Reviews selected theories, methods, and terminology related to economic, behavioural, institutional and decisionmaking aspects of resources and envi ronmental problems.
Prereq: ENV § 271 or consent of instructor
Field Trip fee $10-$15

courses.label: GEOG 357
courses.title: Conservation and Resource Management
paras: History of the conservation movement; ecological principles of conservation and resource management. Analysis, use and planning of recreational resources.
Prereq: ENV S 200
Cross-listed as PLAN 357.
Lab fee $10-$15
Students may receive credit for only one of GEOG 367 and PLAN 357

courses.label: GEOG 358
paras: Water Planning and Management: Strategies and Experiences Benchmark theory and principies of comprehensive water planning and integrated river basin management. Selected international to local scale case studies.
Prereq: GEOG 356 or consent of instructor
Lab fee $10-$15.

courses.label: GEOG 359
courses.title: Geography of Energy
paras: Issues related to energy resources. The course examines both Canadian energy management problems and international issues such as cartels and relationships between energy and economic development.
Prereq: GEOG 202 or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 360
courses.title: Preparation of Maps and Illustrations
paras: Equipment, materials and techniques involved in the practical construction of maps and cartographic illustrations. Conventional drafting and plotting procedures, symbolization of data and map editing for reproduction.
Prereq: GEOG 160
Lab fee $15-25.

courses.label: GEOG 375
courses.title: Air Photo Interpretation
paras: The principles of air photo interpretation utilizing specific criteria visible in the conventional air photo. Examples from local and foreign environments. Prereq: GEOG 275 and either GEOG 201A or EARTH 121-122 or SCI 100 Lab fee $20

courses.label: GEOG 376
courses.title: Environmental Remote Sensing
paras: Theoretical and practical aspects of remote sensing (RS). Interaction between electromagnetic radiation, environmental media and sensors. Analysis of non-photographic systems like RADAR and LANDSAT. Methods of RS data processing and analysis and studies of physical and human environments. .
Prereq: GEOG 275
Lab fee $10-$15

courses.label: GEOG 381
courses.title: The Nature of Geography
paras: The roots and evolution of geographic ‘
thought, conceptual approaches and
pathways. Past traditions, current issues.
and future trends. The politics and soci-
ology of geography as an art, science.
and profession. . Prereq: Any 3 GEOG term courses or
consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 390
courses.title: Senior Honours Thesis Proposal
paras: The development of a research proposal under the supervision of an appropriate faculty member. Normally taken in the third year.
Prereq: Honours Geography students only

courses.label: GEOG 391
courses.title: Field Research
paras: One week field camp in which a
specific area will be analysed from a
geographic point of view. individual or
group analysis of specific field prob-
lems. Four Year General students may
take this course only in fourth year. Estimated cost to student: $125-$150.

courses.label: GEOG 400
courses.title: Climatic and Periglacial Morphology
paras: Characteristics of the main principles of climatic and climatogenetic geomorphology. Examination of processes and forms related to the periglacial environment.
Prereq: One of GEOG 300, GEOG 302 or EARTH 342 or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 401
courses.title: Glacial Geomorphology and Some Contemporary Applications
paras: Glacial and fiuvioglacial erosion and deposition and their effects on landscapes. Focus on the environmental influences of glaciation and on practical applications of glacial geomorphdtogists’ techniques and information. . Prereq: One of GEOG 300 or EARTH 342
Course Descriptions

courses.label: GEOG 403
courses.title: Advanced Cartography 1
paras: Advanced study of numerical map anal-
ysis and computer mapping techniques. Prereq: GEOG 160 and ENV S 271

courses.label: GEOG 404
courses.title: Advanced Cartography 2
paras: Advanced study of techniques of map production and design. Technical aspects include photo mechanics, scribing, process photography, typography, proofing and printing processes. Theoretical topics include the map as a communications system, advanced map design and principles of information selection and generalization.
Prereq: GEOG 360
Lab fee $35

courses.label: GEOG 407
courses.title: Field and Lab Techniques in Geomorphology
paras: An analysis of the range of techniques used by geomorphologists. This course will involve intensive field surveying, mapping and laboratory work. Prereq: GEOG 300, EARTH 342 or consent of instructor . . Field-trip expenses: $15 per student.

courses.label: GEOG 408
courses.title: Atmospheric Resource Management
paras: Advanced study of the atmosphere as a natural resource system. Emphasis on weather modification and economic, social and political aspects of climate.
Prereq: GEOG 338 (WLU) or equivelent

courses.label: GEOG 409
courses.title: Energy Balance Climatology
paras: A field and lecture course including the radiation and energy balances of various surfaces, the principles of turbulent energy exchange, and the biotic response to the energy environment. These concepts will be illustrated through the collection and examination of field data.
Prereq: GEOG 2014/8

courses.label: GEOG 410
courses.title: Recreation Geography
paras: The environmental implications of existing and potential recreational demands. Recreational travel, site capability, economic and ecological impact models will be considered as well as the behavioural aspects of amenity resources.
Prereq: GEOG 356
Geography

courses.label: GEOG 412
courses.title: Geography of Manufacturing Firms
paras: and industries A companion course to GEOG 311, Emphasis on decision-making, multinational corporations, technological change, and analysis of the locational patterns of specific industries.
Prereq: GEOG 311

courses.label: GEOG 414
courses.title: Energy Resources Management
paras: Energy management emphasizing ecological and economic approaches. Issues related to managing conventional energy resources and development of alternatives. Techniques for studying energy issues are also presented. Prereq: GEOG 359 and either GEOG 311 or GEOG 356 or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 421A
courses.title: Europe and the Mediterranean
paras: Detailed study of physical, cultural, economic and political geography, including the development of cities, problems of agriculture, changing industrial patterns, distribution of trade, regional disparities, and planning on the city, regional and national levels.

courses.label: GEOG 421B
courses.title: Europe and the Mediterranean
paras: Continuation of GEOG 421A. Preraq: GEOG 421A

courses.label: GEOG 422
courses.title: Canada
paras: Seminar on geographical regional “synthesis as applied to Canada. Study of regions at different scales. Issues of continuing Canadian concern.
Prereq: GEOG 322

courses.label: GEOG 450
courses.title: City and Regional Systems
paras: A continuation of Geography 349 and 350 with an emphasis on student projects.
Prereq: GEOG 350 and GEOG 349 or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 451
courses.title: Soils Geography
paras: An analysis of factors affecting soil
development and classification. Tech-
niques of soil survey and land classifi-
cation. Emphasis on fieldwork. Prereq: GEOG 201A

courses.label: GEOG 452
courses.title: Problems of Rural Land Use
paras: The nature of rural land problems and a critical evaluation of the methods of rural land use planning, in both metropolitan areas and underdeveloped or depressed rural regions.
Prereq: GEOG 315 and/or GEOG 352

courses.label: GEOG 471
courses.title: Advanced Remote Sensing
paras: Principles of earth resource analysis using remotely sensed imagery and digital data with emphasis upon satellite platform sources. The coordination of supplemental imagery and ground truth missions with satellite data in a multistrategy perspective.
Prereq: GEOG 376
Lab fee $10-$15.

courses.label: GEOG 481
courses.title: Frontiers in Geography
paras: Current philosophical and methodological trends in geographical thought. New and resurgent developments in various sub-fields and issues in related disciplines including professional plan-- ning, architecture, future studies, environmental psychology and public administration.
Prereq: GEOG 381 or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 482
courses.title: Geography and Education
paras: Organizational concepts in geography for instructional purposes. Conceptual frameworks for teaching environmental studies. Educational principles, theory and practice related to geography. Prereq: Environmental Studies students in third or fourth year, or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOE 126
courses.title: Geological Engineering Concepts
paras: An introduction to physical geology and earth processes. Geological time, introduction to earth, air and water processes including vulcanism, sedimentation, weathering, lithification, continental drift, radioactive dating, hydrogeology, pedology, resources, mass wasting, erosion. |

courses.label: GEOE 401
courses.title: Geological Engineering Project li
paras: These 2 courses are designed to serve the role of an undergraduate thesis. Specifically, the student is expected to work with a staff member in Civil Engr neering, Earth Sciences, or other appropriate department in identifying and carrying out a suitable short design or research project. The final product will be presented in thesis form and carefully scrutinized by two independent referees chosen for their familiarity with the topic. The subject may be laboratory based, analytic, numerical, or field oriented. The thesis format must follow accepted engineering practice and be of professional quality. Under special circumstances, 2 suitable courses may be substituted for GEO E 400 and 401.
All other courses in the Geological Engi neering program are listed under the course Gescriptions in Earth Sciences or Civil Engineering.

courses.label: HLTH 140
courses.title: Introduction to Health Sciences 1
paras: An expioration of the biological basis of health and disease and strategies for prevention and treatment of disease. Topics inelude human reproduction, (conception, pregnancy and childbirth, sexual development and expression).
human heredity (chromosomal disorders, _
genetic disease. birth defects), and acute disease states (infectious diseases, cancer, immune deficiencies).

courses.label: HLTH 141
courses.title: Introduction to Health Sciences 2
paras: An exploration of the biological basis of health and disease, strategies for prevention and treatment of disease, and the moral, social and psychological impact of innovations in heaith care on Canadian society. Topics include the human nervous system (neurological disorders, mental illness, brain dysfunctions, drug abuse), and lifestyles and health (heart disease, obesity, exercise, smoking).

courses.label: HLTH 210
courses.title: Growth, Development and Aging
paras: The physiology of human growth, development and aging is examined, with special reference to the influence of
diet, environment, exercise and disease ’
on the normal processes. Prereq: BIOL 230, 233 Cross-listed as KIN 210.

courses.label: HLTH 220
courses.title: Health and the Family
paras: The course familiarizes students with the issues involved in understanding how people five and develop within the context of families, and the family interaction with the farger social community. Special emphasis will be placed on health related concerns and the ways in which the family and health care institutions of the society contribute to the physical and emotional health of its members. ; Preraq: HLTH 140 and 141

courses.label: HLTH 245
courses.title: Community Health
paras: This course examines health care delivery systems by considering organizational principles, manpower issues, health resources and economics, service utilization and altematives to the institutional model. There is a'focus on societal and political issues which affect the health of the society through the delivery system.
Prereq: Health Studies students only or permission of instructor

courses.label: HLTH 302
courses.title: Introduction to Blomathematics 1
paras: Biometry is a biological discipline requiring both a knowledge of mathematics and some basic understanding of specific biological phenomena. The course material has been selected from genetics and gerontology to provide examples of where both mathematics and biology have contributed to the advancement of knowledge in interdisciplinary areas. -
Prereq: KIN 116 or first year Chenr istry or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as MTHEL 302A.

courses.label: HLTH 303
courses.title: Introduction to Biomathematics 2
paras: A continuation of Biomathematics 1. Topics considered are first order reaction kinetics in biological systems including a discussion of radioisotope and C™ dating, higher order kinetics including statistical considerations in enzyme kinetics, models for and the measurement of evolution from a knowl edge of genetics and protein structure and assessing the relative importance of environmental factors as evolutionary determinants. . Prereq: HLTH 302 . Cross-listed as MTHEL 302B.

courses.label: HLTH 340
courses.title: Environmental Health
paras: An examination of the effects of environmental pollutants and occupational hazards on human heaith. Emphasis will be placed on the biological mechanisms by which environmental toxicants cause human disease and disability.
Prereq: KIN 317 or equivalent

courses.label: HLTH 341
courses.title: Disease Process
paras: An introduction to the study of factors
governing the occurrence of disease in
human populations, using selected
diseases to illustrate disease mecha-
nisms and identification of risk factors. Prereq: BIO! 230, 233, KIN 317 or
equivalent

courses.label: HLTH 344
courses.title: Program Evaiuation
paras: A comprehensive and systematic introduction to the kéy concepts, methodologies, and issues related to program evaluation in general and their application to health programs in particular. Administrative and policy implications as well as the technical/methodological evaluation issues that face individuals involved in administering, planning, implementing, and evaluating health programs will be discussed.
Prereq: Basic courses in Statistics and in Research Design

courses.label: HLTH 346
courses.title: Nutrition
paras: An elementary course in nutrition with
special emphasis on diet for sport and
certain physiological conditions. Cross-listed as KIN 346.

courses.label: HLTH 448
courses.title: Social Psychology of Health Behaviour
paras: The study and application of basic social psychological processes in relation to selected health-related behaviours (e.g. family planning, overeating, smoking, non-medical drug use, cardiovascular risk factors, patient compliance, medical care utilization).
Prereq: PSYCH 101 or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as KIN 348.

courses.label: HLTH 349
courses.title: Principles of Behaviour Modification
paras: A course providing a general overview of behaviour modification principles and procedures. Basic principles of reinforcement, punishment, modelling and desensitization are examined as they relate to health behaviour.
Prereq: PSYCH 101 or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as KIN 349.

courses.label: HLTH 350
courses.title: Occupational Health
paras: A descriptive analysis of health problems commonly encountered in the workplace and surrounding environment (e.g. pollution). The health effects of chemical toxicants on human organ systems are described, based on the current toxicologic research literature. Methods for detection and control of workplace hazards (especially carcinogens) are also presented.
Prereq: HLTH 340

courses.label: HLTH 407
courses.title: Physiology of Coronary Heart Disease
paras: An examination of the pathology, risk factors and rehabilitation programs related to coronary heart disease. Major emphasis is placed on the cardiorespiratory implications of exercise in the rehabilitation process.
Prereq: KIN 300. or permission of instructor
Cross-listed as KIN 407.

courses.label: HLTH 431
courses.title: Research Project
paras: An independent research project on an approved topic, supervised by a faculty member. Includes an approved proposal and.completion of the first 3 chapters of the thesis - Introduction, Review of Literature, and Methods.
Recommended for students planning graduate studies

courses.label: HLTH 432
courses.title: Research Project
paras: An independent research project on an approved topic, supervised by a faculty member. Includes data collection, data analysis and presentation of results in thesis form. Prereq: Completion of HLTH 431 Recommended for students planning graduate studies

courses.label: HLTH 433
courses.title: Advanced Research Project
paras: A course designed to familiarize students with the skills requisite for the formulation, execution and written presentation of an empirical research Project. After a general discussion of the pertinent issues, students will be asked to analyse independently a data set related to a topic of interest to Health Studies students and to present this in a thesis format. Prereq: KIN 222, 330 and CS 316 Students must be enrolled in either 4th year regular or 3B Co-op of the Health Studies program.

courses.label: HLTH 442
courses.title: Epidemiology of Chronic Diseases
paras: An investigation of the epidemiology of selected non-communicable diseases. The course emphasizes understanding of epidemiologic methods and identification of risk factors. Specific diseases examined will vary from year to year. Prereg: HLTH 241 and an introductory statistics course or consent of instructor

courses.label: HLTH 443
courses.title: Behaviour and Chronic Disease
paras: A critical analysis of various behavioural strategies for the prevention of coronary heart disease, hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and lung
_ cancer. The role of behaviour in the
pathogenesis of disease and the feas-
iblity of behavioural change for preven-
tion of disease will be discussed. Prereq: HLTH 344, 348, 349

courses.label: HLTH 445
courses.title: Seminar in Health Promotion
paras: A study of current issues pertaining to health promotion, health behaviour, or biomedical research. Topics may include pertinent research that is significant to the health of individuals, families and groups, or the community. Prereq: Health Studies students only Normaily only 4th year students will be admitted.

courses.title: Independent Study
paras: For the student who desires to pursue a particular topic in depth through guided independent research and/or reading. A faculty member must approve a student's project prior to registration. May be repeated in subsequent terms. Depending on student demand and availability of teaching resources, special topics may be presented to smail groups in a lecture format. Such topics
* include Pharmacology, and Aging, Heath
and Immunity. Prereq: Consult with Department

Introductory Notes

courses.label: HIST 100
courses.title: Landmarks in World History
paras: A thematic introduction to the development of the world’s major civilizations. This year’s theme is “Community and Social Order", examining the dynamic relationship between individuals and their social structures, and their state.

courses.label: HIST 102A
paras: The American identity 1607-1980

A consideration of the shaping of American characteristics under the headings of: The Frontier; Religious Denominationalism; Libertarian Revolution: Black Slavery; New Immigrations; Mass Production; the Great Depression; War and Global Americanism.

courses.label: HIST 102C
courses.title: The Origins of Wars in the Twentieth Century
paras: An analysis of the diplomatic, political, economic, ideological, social and cultural explanations of the causes of the major wars of this century with special emphasis on Canada.

HIST 1020 W 05 From Nationalism to Totalitarianism The growth of nationalism and nation states since the French Revolution with attention ta the Industrial: Revolution, the World Wars, Fascism, Naziism and Stalinism.
Offered at Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: HIST 102E
courses.title: Canadian History
paras: Selected major themes from pioneer life to Canadian involvement in 20th century wars.
Offered at St. Jerome's College in the Winter term.

courses.label: HIST 102F
courses.title: An Introduction to Western intellectual History Since the Renaissance '
paras: An exploration of some of the questions and answers posed by thinkers on the human predicament from Renaissance and Reformation times to the modem period. Readings range from Luther to J.P. Sarte, Shakespeare to Marx and Freud.

courses.label: HIST 102H
courses.title: Early Modern Europe
paras: This course will survey the chief features of early modern European society. Topics will include the Renaissance and Reformation, Olid Regime society, the scientific revolution, the Enlightenment and the French Revolution.
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: HIST 102K
courses.title: Conflict in the Caribbean and Central America
paras: A study of the historical origins and nature of contemporary problems in the Caribbean and central America, from colonial times down to the U.S. intervention in Grenada.

courses.label: HIST 102M
courses.title: Law and Society in the Middle Ages
paras: 500-1000 A study of the laws and legal procedures of the Early Middle Ages. Anglo- Saxon and Germanic law will be examined along with legal procedures and institutions of that era.
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: HIST 102U
courses.title: Asian History
paras: This course aims to help the student develop a framework for understanding the histories and cultures of India, China, Japan, and Southeast Asia. Two themes given extensive study are the related issues of imperialism and modernization, the latter here defined as profound changes in the following areas: economic, social, cultural and potitical.

courses.label: HIST 130
courses.title: The Modern World in Historical Perspective
paras: This course will introduce students, through interrelationships and interaction of selected themes, to the contemporary history of Europe, North America, and the Far East. Its format includes 2 interpretive lectures per week plus major films on 20th century crises and discussion groups.

courses.label: HIST 200
courses.title: Twentieth Century History as Documented by Flims
paras: A history of the 20th century. through films. The First World War, Europe between the Wars, the Second World War, North American ‘society in the 20th century and other political, moral and social themes will be explored.

courses.label: HIST 201X
courses.title: Canadian Urban History
paras: An historical examination of the urbanization process, the social, political and economic factors that shaped the Canadian city and the relationship between selected metropolitan and hinterland areas.

courses.label: HIST 203X
courses.title: Modern Quebec
paras: The course will discuss the problem of Quebec in contemporary Canada by analyzing the historical background of key issues like separatism, the survival of the French language, French- Canadian nationalism and the Quiet Revolution.

courses.label: HIST 204X
courses.title: Life on the Ontario Frontier
paras: The course examines the cultural, moral, social and economic adaptations of European settlers to the Upper Canadian frontier environment.

courses.label: HIST 205X
courses.title: Canadian Business History
paras: A study of the development of business in Canada at both the general economic and the individual enterprise level.

courses.label: HIST 206X
courses.title: History of Canadian Minorities
paras: An introduction to the history of selected racial and regional minorities in Canada. The course examines the emergence of minority communities, and their position in modern Canadian society.

courses.label: HIST 208
courses.title: The Cold War: American-Russian Relations Since November, 1917
paras: Traditional and radical historians examine the Cold War: American- Russian rivalry, 19th century; Wilson vs. Lenin; F.D.R., Truman and Stalin; containment, coexistence, and the politics of crisis from 1945 to the present.

courses.label: HIST 210X
courses.title: History of Law
paras: An historical introduction to law in the
Ancient world. Babylonian, Assyrian.
Hittite and Roman law and tegal prac-
tices and concepts will be examined. Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: HIST 211
courses.title: British History to 1603
paras: A survey of the main stages in the transition of Britain from a remote province of the Roman Empire to a prominent state of post-Reformation Europe. Within the chronological framework, political and constitutional as well as ecclesiastical and social dévelopments will be examined.

courses.label: HIST 212
courses.title: British History since 1603
paras: A survey of the shaping of British society and the British experience from the time of Shakespeare to the present: constitutional conflict and compromise, tise and fall of empire, industrial and urban revolution, world wars and welfare state.

courses.label: HIST 213X
courses.title: Modern Western Popular Culture
paras: This course examines historically the formation of a distinct modern western popular culture, looking primarily at Britain, France, Canada and the United States from around 1850 to the present, and emphasizing such aspects as: industrialism and leisure, the family and sexual attitudes, religion and popular belief, education and literacy, drinking habits, organized sport and mass entertainment.

courses.label: HIST 214X
courses.title: Empires and Missionaries
paras: A survey of the role of missionaries in imperiat history since 1500. Native responses to evangelicization will be studied. Some comparisons will be made with indigenous response to Christianity in pre-modern times.

courses.label: HIST 216
courses.title: Irish History: Achievement, Unification, Revolt
paras: Political, social and religious history of Ireland from the beginning of the golden age of Irish medieval civilization to the Act of Union, c.400 to 1800.

courses.label: HIST 217
courses.title: Irish History: The Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries
paras: Polifical, social and religious history of lreland emphasizing social change, the © struggle for Home Rule and the Republic, 1800 to present.

courses.label: HIST 218
courses.title: German History 1740-1945
paras: The development of Germany from the Austrian-Prussian rivalry of 1740 through the end of World War il.
Offered at Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: HIST 222
courses.title: History of Modern Revolutions
paras: An introduction to historical explanations
of revolutions with special focus on
social change and revolutionary theories.
The French, Russian and Chinése Revo-
lutions will be used as case studies. Offered at Conrad Grebel College.
Course Descriptions History

courses.label: HIST 224
courses.title: Canadian Culture and Society in the Twentieth Century
paras: An approach to modern Canadian development as the people have wrestled with such phenomena as war, depression, internal and external tensions, urban growth, the "post industrial” society.

courses.label: HIST 226
courses.title: The Middle East Conflict
paras: A survey of regional, religious and impe-
rial rivalries from ancient to modern
times, with emphasis on the 20th
century and the Arab-\sraeli conflict. Offered at Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: HIST 229
paras: The Catholic Church in Canada: From the French Regime to Confederation An examination of the Catholic Church in Canada from the time of Brebeuf and the missionaries through the French and British regimes up to and including Confederation.
Offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: HIST 230
courses.title: Church and State in Modern Latin America
paras: A study of the relationship between the church and the governments of several Latin American countries in the 19th and 20th centuries.

courses.label: HIST 232
courses.title: Revolutions in Latin America
paras: An evaluation of the causes and effects of revolutions in Latin America with special emphasis on Nicaragua.

courses.label: HIST 234
courses.title: The Catholic Church in Canada Since Confederation An examination of the Catholic Church
paras: in Canada since Confederation, with an emphasis on social and political influences.
Offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: HIST 235
courses.title: History of Christianity
paras: The development of Christianity in its Roman Catholic, Eastern Orthodox and Protestant traditions from the time of Christ to the present. Offered at Conrad Grebel College. Cross-listed as R S 230.
History

courses.label: HIST 237
courses.title: Ancient Civilization 1
paras: A study of the civilizations of the
Ancient Near East focussing: on Meso-
potamia (Sumer and Akkad, the Babylo-
nian Dynasty and the Third Dynasty of
Ur), Hatti, Assyria, Egypt and Persia. Offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: HIST 238
courses.title: Ancient Civilization 2
paras: An introduction to the social, political
and cultural history of Rome in its
development from a Republic to an
Empire. Special attention will be placed
on the sources of political power. Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: HIST 245
courses.title: Religious and Cultural Minorities in
paras: Canada

A comparative study of the cultural and’ political conflicts with society and state: of such ethnic and religious minorities as Doukhobors, Hutterites, Jehovah's ‘ Witnesses, Jews, and Mennonites (including the Amish). Emphasis on 20th century.
Offered at Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: HIST 247
courses.title: Mennonite History: A Survey
paras: This course covers Mennonite origins, teachings, migrations, settlement patterns, divisions, leaders, institutions, and religious and social practices, indeed all facets of Mennonite history in various national settings.
- Offered at Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: HIST 248
courses.title: History of Canadian-American Relations to 1914
paras: An examination of the history of relations between the two countries until 1914. Topics of a political, economic, social and cultural nature will be studied.

courses.label: HIST 249
courses.title: History of Canadian-American Relations Since 1914
paras: An examination of the history of relations between the two countries since 1914. Topics of a political, economic, social and cultural nature will be studied.

courses.label: HIST 251X
courses.title: History of Medieval Europe 814-1303
paras: The political, cultural, economic and
ecclesiastical development of Europe
from Charlemagne to Philip IV of France. Offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: HIST 252X
courses.title: Europe in the Nineteenth Century
paras: European social and cultural history, 1815-1914. This course will consider the inter-relations between ideas and institutions during a period of industrialization, urbanization and mass education.

courses.label: HIST 253X
courses.title: Canadian History: The British Period
paras: The evolution of Canadian society in the face of dominant British and American influences..
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: HIST 254X
courses.title: Canadian History: The National
paras: Period
This course studies the development of
Modern Canada. Themes of the course
include immigration, industrialization.
feminism, labour unrest, and regionalism. Also offered at St. Jerome's College
in Winter term.

courses.label: HIST 255
courses.title: The Expansion of England
paras: The history of the British Empire down to the American War of independence,’ telling the story of the Tudor seadogs, of the plantation of ireland, the settlement of the North American mainland, the establishment of slave plantations in the Caribbean, and the earliest British enterprises in Africa, Asia and the Pacific.

courses.label: HIST 256
courses.title: The British Empire and Commonwealth
paras: The history of British imperialism between the loss of the American colonies and the Falklands Islands War of 1982, tracing the rise of the settlement colonies to dominion status, the huge expansion of the dependent empire during the age of the New imperialism, the imperial apogee after World War |, and the rapid change from Empire to New Commonwealth after World War Il.

courses.label: HIST 257
courses.title: History of the United States until
paras: The settlement of Engtish North America, British colonial society, the American Revolution, politics and culture in the American Republic, the Civil War. A special emphasis on religious and political culture.

courses.label: HIST 258
courses.title: History of the United States since
paras: A survey of American society, politics and thought and of the relations of the United States with the outside world from 1865 to the present.

courses.label: HIST 300
paras: The idea of History

The course is an introduction to the Philosophy of History and to the art of historical writing. tt deals with the great theoretical issues influencing historical analysis and with the classics of historical literature. It is equally concemed with the practical problems of historical research.

courses.label: HIST 305
courses.title: The English Reformation
paras: A history of the English reformation, expansively considered from the beginnings of the European Reformation to the establishment of the Anglican: church in the Revolutionary and Restoration periods in the 17th century.

courses.label: HIST 307
courses.title: British History 1760-1867
paras: A study of people, power, thought and culture in the world's first industrializing society.

courses.label: HIST 308
courses.title: Britain Since 1867
paras: A study of the British experience and of Britain's part in world history from the 1860's to the 1980's

courses.label: HIST 320
courses.title: The History of Modern Quebec
paras: The course will treat the history of Quebec from 1867 to the present. Nationalism, separatism, language and cultural problems, economic and social issues are all examined in their historical context.

courses.label: HIST 323
courses.title: The United States in World Affairs
paras: A study of the emergence of the United States as a world power in its international and domestic context, with particular emphasis on the 20th century.

courses.label: HIST 325
courses.title: History of Canadian indians to
paras: "From Freedom to Conquest”. The history of Indian-white contact and its effect on the life and culture of the native Canadians.

courses.label: HIST 326
courses.title: History of Canadian Indians since
paras: 1870's ’ “Life under coercion” and the "New Indian”. The history of Indians on reserves and under government administration. Contemporary themes and issues of concern to native people are examined.

- HIST 329 W O05 History of Anglo-American Law The emphasis will be on the early development of the common law in England and the formulation of constitutional law in the United States. Offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: HIST 339
courses.title: The History of France in the Nineteenth Century
paras: A study of French society and the four revolutions that influenced it with particular attention to social and institutional forces. _

courses.label: HIST 345
courses.title: Minorities in International Perspective
paras: An examination of the minorities phenomenon in the context of national, regional, and international power struggles and the resulting discriminations, refugee movements, international dispersions, arid conflicts in new settings. Emphasis on 20th century. Offered at Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: HIST 346
courses.title: Mennonite History: Canadian Issues
paras: Special issues examined in historical context include church/state conflicts in education, conscription and social policies, and such phenomena as nonconformity, internal divisions, organizational proliferation, theological shifts, changing forms of leadership, and issues of identity. .
Offered at Conrad Grebe! College.

courses.label: HIST 348
courses.title: The Radical Reformation
paras: A study of 16th century Anabaptism-a
retigious Reformation movement .
dissenting from both Protestantism and
Roman Catholicism-its origins, its social
political and theological content, and its
relationship to such independent
dissenters as Sebastian Franck. Offered at Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: HIST 350
courses.title: West Indian History
paras: A study of the Caribbean region from aboriginal times, including European imperialism, the history of plantations, slavery and siave society, independence movements, and the problems posed by modernization, underdevelopment and neo-colonialism.

courses.label: HIST 356
courses.title: Russian History since 1825
paras: The course will focus on selected themes in Russia’s development in the 19th and 20th centuries, including the Soviet period.

courses.label: HIST 377
courses.title: The Historian and the Computer
paras: This course will introduce students to quantitative analysis of historical data. After a brief introduction to basic SPSS Statistical programs, students will develop a research scheme and analyze machine-readable historical data.

courses.label: HIST 379
courses.title: Reformation History
paras: An analysis of the economic changes, the rise of “new monarchs,” the nature of and effect of the "religious reformation,” the expansion of Europe to the *new world” with their implications for 16th century Europe.
Offered at Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: HIST 385
courses.title: Canada: From Macdonald to Laurier
paras: An analytical and historical examination of the development of the Canadian nation from Confederation to the First World War.

courses.label: HIST 389
courses.title: Canada in World Affairs: From
paras: Laurier to Trudeau .

An analytical-and_ historical examination of Canadian foreign policy in the international system. Domestic sources of Canadian foreign policy and international sources of Canadian foreign policy are examined in detail.

courses.label: HIST 393
courses.title: Seven Faces of Evil
paras: A study of some of the major visions of evil in the West and their consequences in politics, economics, science and religion.

courses.label: HIST 396
courses.title: The History of the American South
paras: This course traces the main eras and issues in Southern history from the 16th century to the mid-20th century. Topics examined will include pre-revolutionary and antebellum South, the Trial of Tears, the Civil War and reconstruction, the New South, the “lost cause”, the era of Jim Crow, and the search for the central theme.

courses.label: KIN 102
courses.title: Biophysical Basis of Kinesiology
paras: Human physical movement is discussed from mechanical, anatomical and physiological viewpoints. The course provides a general orientation to the study of Kinesiology.

courses.label: KIN 103
courses.title: Psycho-Social Basis of Kinesiology
paras: An introduction to the study of human physical activity from psychological, sociological, anthropological and historical perspectives.

courses.label: KIN 116
courses.title: General and Organic Chemistry
paras: An introduction to the chemical concepts of importance in kinesiology and health studies.

courses.label: KIN 200
courses.title: Human Anatomy of the Limbs and Trunk
paras: Functionally-oriented study of the limbs and trunk by regions using predissected cadavers. A brief introduction to Neuroanatomy is included.
Prereq: Kinesiology, Health Studies and Dance students or consent of instructor
No Year 1 students are admitted.

courses.label: KIN 201
courses.title: Human Anatomy of the Brain, Head and Neck
paras: The anatomical structure and function of the brain, cranial nerves and sense organs of the head are emphasized. Included is an introduction to the histology of the nervous system. An opportunity for some dissection of the head and neck is provided.
Prereq: KIN 200 or consent of instructor

courses.label: KIN 210
courses.title: Growth and Development, and Aging
paras: The physiology of human growth, development and aging is examined with
_ special reference to the influence of
diet, environment, exercise and disease on the normal processes. Prereq: KIN 200, BIOL 230 and 233 Cross-listed as HLTH 210..
Course Descriptions Kinesiolégy

courses.label: KIN 222
courses.title: Statistical Techniques Applied to
paras: Kinealology
An introduction to descriptive and infer-
ential statistics and the interpretation of
data. A major consideration of the
course is the use of statistics. in the
solution of problems in Kinesiology. Prereq: KIN students only

courses.label: KIN 242
courses.title: Introduction to Movement Disorders
paras: An introduction to selected movement disorders and their implications for physical activity. The movement disorders examined include those which accompany neuromuscular and perceptual-motor impairment, mental retardation, cardio-vascular and respiratory disease.
Prereq: KIN 102 and 103

courses.label: KIN 252
courses.title: Introduction to the Sociology of Sport
paras: An introduction to the characteristics, processes and problems of sport as a social system. In addition, the social psychological aspects of sport involvement are considered. Prereq: KIN 103 and SOC 101 Cross-listed as REC 203 and SOC 348.

courses.label: KIN 255
courses.title: Introduction to Psychomotor Behaviour
paras: An information processing approach is used to introduce the principles of learning and performing fine and gross motor skills. In addition, social psychological variables are studied as they relate to the facilitation or decrement in learning and performance.
Prereq: KIN 103 and PSYCH 101

courses.label: KIN 300
courses.title: Physiology of Physical Activity
paras: A study of the effects of physical activity on the muscular, circulatory and respiratory systems and the mechanisms through which the body adapts to activity and environment.
Prereq: BIOL 230 and 233

courses.label: KIN 317
courses.title: Human Biochemistry
paras: An elementary course in human biochemistry including the metabolism and function of proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, and hormones. Emphasis is placed on the application of biochemical principles to human movement.
Prereq: KIN 116 or equivalent
Kinesiology

courses.label: KIN 321
courses.title: Introduction to the Biomechanics of Human Movement
paras: Anatomical, neural and mechanical considerations in the qualitative and quantitative analysis of human movement are examined. Concepts related to the biostatics and biodynamics of linked segment models of human motion are introduced.
Prereq: PHYS 103, KIN 200 and 222

courses.label: KIN 330
courses.title: Research Design
paras: An introduction to the basic principles of
scientific inquiry in Kinesiology. A
systematic treatment of the logic and
practice of methods and techniques
employed in research related to physical
activity with an examination of design.
sampling, data gathering and analysis. - Prereq: KIN 222

courses.label: KIN 335
courses.title: Evaluation of Human Motor Performance ,
paras: The nature and methodology of assessment is reviewed from theoretical and empirical perspectives. Taxonomies of motor performance are examined and principles developed for the measurement of specific constructs in field and laboratory situations.
Prereq: KIN 222

courses.label: KIN 340
courses.title: Introduction to Sports Medicine
paras: An introductory course to the area of sports medicine, including the prevention, care and rehabilitation of common sports injuries. Considerable attention is directed towards the mechanisms of traumatic injuries as well as the management in the acute, intermediate and advanced stages of injury care. Prereq: KIN 200, 3rd.and 4th year students only

courses.label: KIN 341
courses.title: Select Topics in Sports Medicine
paras: A course for those students wishing additional study in the area of sports medicine. Topics to be presented include trauma to the head and vertebral column, internal injuries, heat problems and the medical and non-medical use of drugs in sport.
Prereq: KIN 340

courses.label: KIN 346
courses.title: Nutrition
paras: An elementary course in nutrition with
special emphasis on diet for sport and
certain physiological conditions. Cross-listed. as HLTH 346.

KIN 48 WS 3C 05 Social Psychology of Health Behaviour The study and application of basic social psychological processes in relation to selected health-related behaviours (e.g. family planning, overeating, smoking, non-medica! drug use, cardiovascular risk factors, patient compliance, medical care utilization).
Prereq: PSYCH 101 or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as HLTH 348.

courses.label: KIN 349
courses.title: Principles of Behaviour Modification
paras: A course providing a general overview of behaviour modification principles and procedures. Basic principles of reinforcement, punishment, modelling and desensitization are examined as they relate to health behaviour.
Prereq: PSYCH 101 or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as HLTH 349.

courses.label: KIN 352
courses.title: Sociology of Aging
paras: An introduction to individual and population aging. Topics discussed include: aging from an historical and comparative perspective; aging in subcultures; aging and the social structure; aging and social processes, aging and the environment; work and retirement, and aging and leisure patterns.
Prereq: SOC 101 and one other SOC course
Cross-listed as SOC 344.

courses.label: KIN 354
courses.title: Social Psychology and Physical Activity
paras: An examination of sport and other forms of physical activity as social situations. Topics such as social facilitation, modelling, person perception, expectancies, group structure, unity, motivation, leadership, conformity, and intergroup relations are introduced in relation to motor performance.
Prereq: PSYCH 101
Cross-listed as REC 307.

courses.label: KIN 356
courses.title: Information Processing in Human Perceptual Motor Performance |
paras: An information processing model of perceptual-motor behaviour is presented. Human performance theory is used to study processes mediating input and output information. Specifically, the subprocesses of storage of information in memory, perception, retrieval of information from memory and execution of movement are examined. Prereq: KIN 222, 255

courses.label: KIN 357
courses.title: Motor Learning
paras: A course focused on the bases and applications of theories of motor learning. Included are selected psychological and neurophysiclogical processes as they relate to these theories.
Prereq: KIN 222, 255

courses.label: KIN 401
courses.title: Physiological Adaptations to Physical Activity
paras: An analysis of the physiologic adaptations that occur in response to protracted physical activity and the influence of such adaptations on the response to work in a variety of environmental conditions. Special emphasis is given to the changes occurring in skeletal and cardiac muscles and the neuro-endocrine mechanisms involved. Prereq: KIN 300 and 317

courses.label: KIN 402
courses.title: Hydrospace, Altitude and Aerospace Physiology
paras: An examination of man’s cardiorespiratory responses at rest and during work to selected stresses of hyperbaric and hypobaric environments.
Prereq: KIN 300

courses.label: KIN 405
courses.title: Exercise Management
paras: An examination of the rationale and procedures used in the development of exercise programs for normally healthy individuals.
Prereq: KIN 300 and 321

courses.label: KIN 407
courses.title: The Physiology of Coronary Heart Disease
paras: An examination of the pathology, risk factors and rehabilitation programs related to coronary heart disease. Major emphasis is placed on the cardiorespiratory implications of exercise in the rehabilitation process. Prereq: KIN 300 or equivalent Cross-listed as HLTH 407.

courses.label: KIN 416
paras: Neuromuscular integration An examination of the neural processes involved in the maintenance of posture and the control of movement.
Prereq: KIN 201 or PSYCH 261 or consent of instructor

courses.label: KIN 420
courses.title: Kineslological Considerations in Equipment Evaluation
paras: The principles of analysis and assessment of equipment for human use (e.g. helmets, backpacks, shoes) and selected tasks (e.g. manual materials handling) are studied from a kinesiological perspective. The use of biomechanicel analytical techniques is emphasized. Preraq: KIN 321, 3B and 4th year students only or consent of instructor KIN 425 is advisable and may be taken concurrently.

courses.label: KIN 425
courses.title: Biomechanics of Human Movement
paras: The quantitative measurement and analysis of the movement of the human musculo skeletal system. Multisegment dynamic movements will be studied using existing computer programs, with emphasis on kinematics, kinetics and energetics, as well as the use of EMG in the assessment of the control of the movement. Examples are presented from pathological, normal and athletic movement.
Prereq: KIN 321

courses.label: KIN 426
courses.title: Biophysical Signal Processing and Control Systems
paras: Basic electricity and electronics required for the understanding of bicelectric recording and electrophysiology. Appiication of signal processing to biophysical signals encountered in kinesiology. Mathematical modelling of passive and active systems and the control systems (cardiac, respiratory, neuromuscular) associated with human movement. Prereq: KIN 321, KIN 300, KIN 357 or consent of instructor

courses.label: KIN 431
courses.title: Research Proposai
paras: An independent paper in the form of a research proposal on an approved topic, supervised by a faculty member (see KIN 432 for range of topics). The proposal shall consist of 3 chapters which include: (1) an introduction or statement of the problem, (2) a review of the literature, (3) methods and procedures.
Prereq: 4ih year Honours Kinesiology

courses.label: KIN 432
courses.title: Research Project
paras: An independent research project on an approved topic, supervised by a faculty member. (The first three chapters are completed as KIN 431.) The project may include survey, experimental or theoretical research, program evaluation, mathematical modelling, fitness appraisal, etc.
Prereq: KIN 431
It is strongly recommended that students planning graduate studies take KIN 431 and KIN 432.

courses.label: KIN 433
courses.title: Senior Essay
paras: An extensive critical review of the literature on an approved topic. The topics will be broader in scope than those associated with specific research proposais.
Prereq: 4th year Honours Kinesiology

courses.label: KIN 452
courses.title: Sport in Society
paras: An advanced course in the sociology of sport with a particular focus on sport in Canadian society. Topics include the structure and processes of Canadian sport and its place in Canadian social structure and culture.
Prereq: KIN 252 or REC 203 or SOC 348

courses.label: KIN 453
courses.title: The Psychology of Sport and Physical Activity
paras: An introduction to specific psychological topics as they relate.to the social psychological behaviour of the individual in motor performance situations. Topics usually examined are personality, anxiety, motivation, attribution.
Prereq: KIN 354

courses.label: KIN 456
courses.title: Cognitive Dysfunction and Motor
paras: Skill : An examination of issues related to understanding the cerebral organization of motor skill. Discussion of how certain movement disorders are a reflection of disturbances at different stages in the sequence of information processing. Prereq: One of PSYCH 206, 207, or KIN 356.

courses.label: KIN 470
courses.title: Seminar in Kinesiology
paras: An examination of current major issues
and trends in Kinesiology. Students
select areas of major interest from a
series of faculty introduced topics. Prereq: 4th year Honours KIN
Students
Couree Descriptions Kinesiology

courses.label: KIN 472
courses.title: Directed Study in Special Topics
paras: For the student who desires to pursue a particular topic in depth through guided independent research and/or reading. A faculty member must approve a student’s project prior to registration. May be repeated in subsequent terms. Prereq: Consent of department

courses.label: KIN 480
courses.title: Coaching Foundations
paras: A study of the basic principles and philosophies of coaching today. Emphasis is placed upon the application of kinesiological principles of performance as well as social, organizational and resource probiems pertinent to each of several sport sections.

The specific sections offered are: KIN 481T - Volleyball, KIN 482T - Basketbali, KIN 483T - Gymnastics, KIN 484T - Racquets, KIN 485T - Football, KIN 486T - Ice Hockey, KIN 487T - Field Hockey, KIN 488T - Aquatics, KIN 489T - Track and Field. Students must complete a minimum of three (3) sport sections before credit is given.
Prereq: Students must complete 1 Physical Activity course in order to enrol in that particular 480 section

courses.label: KIN 491
courses.title: Clinical Kinesiology - Sports Injuries Assessment
paras: Practical experience in the examination, diagnosis, and treatment of sports inju-
ries under the supervision of a physician and an athletic therapist.
Prereq: KIN students only. Must have at least A- in KIN 200 and 340, first aid and athletic injury experience, and: consent of instructor

courses.label: KIN 492A
courses.title: Clinical Kinesiology - Cardiac Rehabilitation Practicum
paras: Practical experience with cardiac patients in a rehabilitation setting; major emphasis is placed on the cardiorespiratory implications of exercise and behaviour modification.
Prereq: KIN 300, 407, 349, and experience with high risk patients, plus consent of instructor
Courses may be taken concurrently.
Course Descriptions — Kinesiology.

courses.label: KIN 489A
courses.title: Ski School, W PHYSICAL ACTIVITY COURSES
paras: All physical activity courses are elective and non-credit and available only to students enrolled in Kinesiology. Students should consult with a faculty advisor concerning the applicability of these courses for entry into careers such as teaching.
In an attempt to satisfy those students who are keenly interested in
teaching, the Sport Proficiency Certifica-

tion Program is available. The contents of this program are tied to the requirements of the Colleges of Education and help to produce a more marketable graduate in this field. A small fee may be charged to cover the costs of printed materials, additional instruction, etc. Further information regarding this program can be found in the Kine- : siology Undergraduate Student Handbook.
The following activity courses are offered if there are sufficient requests.

Course Descriptions
Courses not offered in the current academic year are listed at the end of this section.

courses.label: MENV 100
courses.title: Issue Analysis and Problem Soiving for Environmental Studies 1
paras: Designed to complement the introductory overview of ENV S 195 and the introduction to methods and techniques (M ENV 150/151). Selected themes and case examples are analyzed within a framework of concepts and theories from the natural and social sciences. Students undertake practical exercises to develop analytic and probiem-solving skills.
Prereq: Honours Man-Environment Studies

courses.label: MENV 101
courses.title: Issue Analysis and Problem Solving for Environmental Studies 2
paras: Continuation of M ENV 100.
Prereq: Honours Man-Environment Studies

courses.label: MENV 150
courses.title: Environmental Issues: Methods and Techniques
paras: Course will teach basic research skills to complement the problem-solving skills taught in M ENV 100/101. Concentration on the “systems approach” and its use in problem solving, with attention to information gathering and organization, quantitative data analysis techniques, and presentation skills. Microcomputers will be used for report generation, information organization and basic data analysis. .
Prereq: Honours Man-Environment Studies or consent of instructor

courses.label: MENV 151
courses.title: Environmental issues: Methods and Techniques Continuation of M ENV 150
paras: Prereq: M ENV 150

courses.label: MENV 218
courses.title: Introduction to Canadian Energy Issues
paras: Emphasis on physical concepts, terminology, units, current policy, supply and demand noting technical and economic aspects, and alternative energy strategies.

courses.label: MENV 220
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Economics
paras: Introduction to the history of economic thought and the various schools of economic thought as these relate to environmental cases, issues and analysis.
Students may receive credit for only one of M ENV 220 and ECON 101, 102.

courses.label: MENV 241
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Social impact Assessment
paras: An introduction to means of assessing proposed approaches to environmentally and socially significant problems and opportunities. Special emphasis on the Nature and limitations of conventional . means of assessing the impacts, and overall desirability of technologies, Projects, plans and policies. Close examination of case examples.

courses.label: MENV 260
courses.title: Visual Perception and Communication
paras: An exploration of the nature of perception and its relationship to communication with special reference to visual phenomena.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: MENV 275
courses.title: Special Readings
paras: Background reading and study in
consultation with Faculty. Typically
utilized when a student must study a
topic in connection with other work, but
no course offering that topic is available. Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: MENV 290
courses.title: Seminar-Workshop
paras: Individual or small group project emphasizing multidisciplinary treatment of environmental problems. Work encouraged on situations of interest to community organizations, government agencies or other groups.
Prereq: Man-Environment Studies
A letter grade for M ENV 290 will be submitted only after the completion of M ENV 291

courses.label: MENV 291
courses.title: Seminar-Workshop
paras: Continuation of project begun in M ENV 290
Prereq: M ENV 290

courses.label: MENV 205
courses.title: Development of Environmental Thought 1
paras: Examination of conflicting positions on how we do and should view the natural world and ourselves, beginning with review of the history of attitudes to the environment and our place in it. Emphasis on evolution of attitudes to human nature and the environment in industrial society, critiques of these attitudes and implications for approaches to modern environmental issues. Prereq: Man-Environment Studies or consent of instructor .

courses.label: MENV 296
courses.title: Development of Environmental Thought 2
paras: Examination of twentieth century concems about industrial progress and treatment of people and the environment. Focus on problems and promises of efforts to dominate nature through scientific and technological advance.
alternative views on the nature of scien-
tific knowledge and human well-being, and the rise of modern environmentalism. Assessment of alternative futures.
Prereq: M ENV 295

courses.label: MENV 318
courses.title: Soft Energy Paths in Canada
paras: Analysis and evaluation of energy strategies based on energy conservation and renewable energy systems. Technical, economic, ecological, and social aspects will be examined.
Prereq: M ENV 218 or consent of instructor

courses.label: MENV 320
courses.title: Environmental Economics
paras: Evaluation of various economic approaches to the environment. Introduction to various models used to analyse environmental quality and used in the design of environmental policy and management initiatives.
Prereq: M ENV 220 or consent of instructor

courses.label: MENV 337
courses.title: Environmental impact Assessment
paras: Major problems and issues in the management of environmental impacts stemming from development projects. Synthesis of ecological, economic and institutional aspects . Integrating environmental management with social and economic development policies and programs.
Prereq: M ENV 241 or consent of instructor
Course Descriptions Men-Environment Studies

courses.label: MENV 338
courses.title: Social impact Assessment
paras: Introduction to the background, theory and methodology of social impact assessment (SIA). SIA as a type of social science research and as a key element in achieving more informed and responsible decision-making in society. Experience in SIA design for environmentally-relevant cases.
Prereq: M ENV 241 or consent of instructor

courses.label: MENV 350
courses.title: Community Action on Environmental Problems
paras: The citizen’s role in the solution of environmental problems. The work of various: community groups is examined and evaluated. Students select topics of particular interest to them for in-depth
study.

courses.label: MENV 360
courses.title: Man and Nature
paras: An exploration of Man’s position in Nature as viewed in science and arts and in different cultures. Course materials will be drawn from many sources including philosophy, psychology, religions, biology and literature.
Prereq: Third and fourth year students and consent of instructor

courses.label: MENV 375
courses.title: Special Readings or Seminars on Selected Topics
paras: Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: MENV 385
courses.title: Technology/Lifestyles for a Conserver Society What is a Conserver Society? What
paras: must we do to make our society into a Conserver Society? How do we evaluate the appropriatenéss of a lifestyle or technology for a Conserver Society? Is a Conserver Society realistic? This course will explore these questions, with emphasis on student participation in discussion and in seminar presentations. Lectures will focus on the basics of various technologies and lifestyles, and on quantitative techniques for comparing these.
Prereq: Second year or above
Man-Environment Studies

courses.label: MENV 390A
courses.title: Seminar-Workshop
paras: Individual or smail group project emphasizing multidisciplinary treatment of environmental problems. Work encouraged on situations of interest to community organizations, government agencies or other groups.
Prereq: Man-Environment Studies
A letter grade for M ENV 390A will be submitted only after the completion of M ENV 390B

courses.label: MENV 390B
courses.title: Seminar-Workshop
paras: Same as M ENV 390A but with additional intensive investigation of the Project as warranted by the project and by student ability.
Prereq: Man-Environment Studies and consent. of faculty

courses.label: MENV 301A
courses.title: Seminar-Workshop
paras: Continuation of M ENV 390A Prereq: M ENV 390A

courses.label: MENV 391B
courses.title: Seminar-Workshop
paras: Continuation of M ENV 390B Prereq: M ENV 3908

courses.label: MENV 400A
courses.title: Senior Honours Seminar ‘
paras: Provides practice in applying skills that are useful to people working in different kinds of organizations. Readings, discussions and exercises emphasize: problem perceptions and diagnoses, actor system analyses, and planning management and evaluation activities as these are carried out by and within organizations. Special attention given to roles that persons having an environmental studies background may be particularly well prepared to develop and refine.
Prereq: Third or fourth year Man- — Environment Studies or consent of instructor
A letter grade for M ENV 400A will be submitted only after the completion of M ENV 4008

courses.label: MENV 400B
courses.title: Senior Honours Seminar
paras: Continuation of M ENV 400A Prereq: M ENV 400A

courses.label: MENV 418
courses.title: Energy Research Seminar
paras: Detailed examination of specific energy issues emphasizing research skills and policy context. Students will participate in a research project. General areas of research may include social and political analysis of specific soft energy options, environmental impacts of certain energy technologies.
Prereq: M ENV 318 or consent of instructor

courses.label: MENV 445
courses.title: Impact Assessment and Policy Analysis: Practicum
paras: Students will draw on knowledge and experience gained in the prerequisite theme courses to critique and/or design impact analyses of a variety of “realworld” activities; including policy initiatives, technological choices, environmentally-relevant proposals, economic strategies and others of special interest or significance.
Prereq: M ENV 241, 337 and 338, or consent of instructor
M ENV 4754,B F,W,S 2R 0.5 each Special Readings or Seminar on Selected Topics See course descriptions under M ENV 275 and 375.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: MENV 490A
courses.title: Senior Honours Assignment
paras: A project of sufficient scope to demonstrate mastery of problem-solving and communication skills on a selected problem or issue concerning manenvironment interrelationships. Credit weights for 490, 491 and 492 vary depending on the amount of work involved and the depth of the subject matter. Study beyond the 490 level requires faculty approval.
Prereq: Honours Man-Environment Studies
A letter grade for M ENV 490A will be submitted only after the completion of M ENY 490B

courses.label: MENV 490B
courses.title: Senior Honours Assignment
paras: Continuation of M ENV 490A Prereq: M ENV 490A

courses.label: MENV 491A
courses.title: Senior Honours Assignment
paras: See description for M ENV 490A. Prereq: Honours Man-Environment Studies A letter grade for M ENV 491A will be submitted only after completion of M ENV 4918

courses.label: MENV 491B
courses.title: Senior Honours Assignment
paras: Continuation of M ENV 491A. Prereq: M ENV 491A

courses.label: MENV 492A
courses.title: Senior Honours Assignment
paras: See description for M ENV 490A. Prereq: Honours Man-Environment Studies A letter grade for M ENV 492A will be submitted only after the completion of M ENV 4928

courses.label: MENV 492B
courses.title: Senior Honours Assignment
paras: Continuation of 492A.
Prereq: M ENV 492A
