Introductory Notes
1. Any full course or 2 half courses in Philosophy can be used to satisfy the Group A (i) requirements.
2. Special courses are offered in
response to student demand or

Special interests of the faculty. Each Spring, the Department will publish a list of these courses offered for the following academic year. This list will include descriptions of those courses whose content is not speci fied below and names of instructors for each course.
3. Courses suffixed with "J" are administered by St. Jerome's College.
PHIL 1005 FW 3C 05 Introduction to Philosophy

A broad selection of the main problems in philosophy will be considered. For example: How can we know whether anything is right or wrong? How can we know about things we cannot directly observe? Can we know whether there is a God? Is mind in any sense distinct from matter?

courses.label: PHIL 101X
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
paras: A generat introduction, designed to provide the student with an understanding of the major problems of clas-_ sical and contemporary philosophy.

courses.label: PHIL 102A
courses.title: Introduction: Knowledge and Reality
paras: Discussion of the nature of reality. Rival theories concerning mind, matter, freedom, the existence of God, and the place of experience and reason in human knowledge are considered.

courses.label: PHIL 102B
courses.title: Introduction to Social and Political Philosophy
paras: An introduction to basic concepts and principles in classic and contemporary social and political philosophy. Differing views on basic questions are examined, with applications to such issues as capital punishment, welfare provisions, taxation, natural resource ownership, and terrorism.

courses.label: PHIL 102C
courses.title: Philosophy of Life
paras: “Who am |?” “What can | hope for after death?” "How can | tell what to do?” “What can | know?” are questions that have led many to philosophize. The course will examine what lifestyles and attitudes major philosophers, stoics, skeptics, pleasure-seekers, mystics, pragmatists, etc. have promoted, and why.

courses.label: PHIL 120J
courses.title: Philosophy of Life and Death
paras: A study of what some of the great philosophers have said about the meaning of life and death and the transition from life to death. Students are urged to raise questions and help direct discussion.
PHIL 130) W 3C 05
Philosophy of Discontent

A study of what some of the great philosophers have said about the causes of discontent. Social disobedience and the extent to which ethical principles can be altered to accommodate changing conditions are possible topics for discussion.

courses.label: PHIL 140
courses.title: Introduction to Formal Logic
paras: Elementary sentence and predicate logic. Translation from English into formalism, decision methods and deductions. Application of Graphic Methods to Logic. This course is a preparation for courses in the foundations of mathematics, scientific methods, and more advanced logic courses.

courses.label: PHIL 145
courses.title: Critical Thinking
paras: An analysis of basic types of reasoning, Structure of arguments, critical assessment of information, common fallacies, problems of clarity and meaning.
Course Descriptions Philosophy
PHIL 200 A/B

Great Works of Western Philosophy An examination of some of the greatest writings in Western Philosophy. Students will be encouraged to come to a critical appreciation of such masterworks as Plato’s Republic, Descartes’ Discourse on Method, Hobbes’ Leviathan, Hume’s Enquiry, Kant’s Prolegomena, Nietzsche’s Zarathustra, and an outstanding work in contemporary
philosophy.

courses.label: PHIL 200A
paras: Great Works of Westem Philosophy: Part 1
Outstanding works from the ancient and medieval periods.

courses.label: PHIL 200B
paras: Great Works of Western Philosophy: Part 2
Outstanding works from the early modem and contemporary periods.
Either PHIL 200A or PHIL 2008 may be taken separately.
PHIL 200) F 3C 05
Intentional Logic

An introduction to the understanding of how words are used, the formation of propositions, the construction of arguments and the examination of fallacies to help the student argue with order, facility and without error.

courses.label: PHIL 201
courses.title: Love
paras: A philosophical analysis of different forms and functions of love. Among the topics to be considered: love and sexu: ality, religious love, love and knowledge. Classical and contemporary sources will be treated.

courses.label: PHIL 202
courses.title: Philosophy of Women
paras: A study of some philosophical issues concerning women; the sexes, gender, and androgyny; the position of women in the work force, public life and family; marriage and its alternatives; sexuality, childbearing.

courses.label: PHIL 203
courses.title: Philosophical Perspectives on Death
paras: This course critically examines how philosophers from the Pre-Socratics to Wittgenstein have analyzed the concept of death. The course is aiso concemed with topics like the concept of a person, personal identity, and survival after death.
Course Descriptions -
Philosophy

courses.label: PHIL 205
courses.title: Science Technology, and Society
paras: Alternative philosophical perspectives on problems raised by scientific and technological developments including moral issues (e.g. privacy and data-gathering, ‘clean’ vs. ‘dirty’ energy). Also an examination of the nature and scope of scientific and technical knowledge as it bears on the responsibilities of scientists and engineers.

courses.label: PHIL 205J
courses.title: Philosophy of Nature
paras: An examination of ancient and modern accounts of the natural world. Problems include whether matter alone can account for change, whether there is more than one cause, whether nature operates by purpose or chance.

courses.label: PHIL 210
courses.title: Philosophy in Literature
paras: Each term, philosophical themes (such as alienation, freedom and responsibility) will be explored through appropriate literary works (for example, works by Aeschylus, Dostoevsky, Kafka, and Twain).

courses.label: PHIL 210J
courses.title: Philosophy of Man
paras: What is Man? What is man’s place among other creatures? !s man an accident of evolution? What are the major views on man as a species? How are love and sex aspects of man’s life?

courses.label: PHIL 215
courses.title: Professional and Business Ethics
paras: Study of ethical and morai issues that typically arise in professional and business activity. What responsibilities to society at large do people in such business and professional activities as teaching, engineering, planning, architecture and accounting have? How far should professional autonomy extend?

courses.label: PHIL 216
courses.title: Rational Behaviour and Decision-Making
paras: An elementary introduction to the subject of ‘rational’ behaviour and decision-making for individuals and groups. Emphasis is on the definition and measurement of utility functions and various criteria employed in models of decision-making. This course is intended to help those whose work will involve them in making decisions in either the public or private sectors.

courses.label: PHIL 218J
courses.title: Ethical Theory
paras: A normative approach, employing several of the classic Western traditions of rational thought, to general ethics. The various schools of ethical thought will be discussed..

courses.label: PHIL 219J
courses.title: Practical Ethics
paras: This course will discuss the applications of general ethics to more specific areas of human endeavour. Among the topics discussed will be abortion, contraception, sex, obscenity, violence, drugs, egoism, dishonesty, and various forms of human exploitation. _

courses.label: PHIL 220
paras: Moral issues

The aim of this course is to improve the student's understanding of ethical ideas and principles by careful discussion of selected concrete moral issues, such as abortion, euthanasia, capital punishment, and violence. Choice of issues is partly determined by student interest.
PHIL 221, F 3C 0.5
Ethics 1

This course is intended to be both a history of and an introduction to moral philosophy. Views on the foundations of ethics of the great philosophers from classical antiquity to about 1900 are systematically examined. Writers studied include: Plato, Aristotle, Aquinas, Kant, Mill and Nietzsche.

courses.label: PHIL 224
courses.title: Mankind and Nature
paras: A philosophical study of the relationship between mankind and nature: historical and current philosophies of the natural world, including the place and responsibilities of human beings; problems of ecological imbalance and collapse.

courses.label: PHIL 225
paras: Social and Political Philosophy: Canadian Problems Basic ideological perspectivesconservative, socialist, and liberaton Canadian problems-such as native rights, nationalism, separatism, and regionalism-are philosophically presented and assessed.
Prereq: PHIL 102B or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 226
courses.title: Ethics and the Life Sciences
paras: An investigation of some critical ethical issues in human research and therapy. Includes discussions of the right to live and the right to die, behaviour control (e.g. psychosurgery, behaviour modification and psychotherapy), human experimentation (including "informed consent” and fetal research) and genetic engineering.

courses.label: PHIL 230J
courses.title: God and Philosophy
paras: An investigation of several aspects concerning the meaning and existence of God. Is God-talk possible? Can faith and reason be reconciled? |s religious experience a meaningful argument? A wide range of different views will be considered..

courses.label: PHIL 236
courses.title: Magic, Mysticism, and the Occult
paras: A critical philosophical discussion of reports of several kinds of extraordinary experiences, such as magic, extrasensory perception, mysticism, and divination will lead us to discussion of such concepts as insanity, irrationality, the supernatural, and the miraculous.

courses.label: PHIL 237
courses.title: Introduction to the Philosophy of Religion
paras: A critical discussion of basic religious concepts. Among the topics covered will be faith, miracles, religious experience, immortality, and arguments for the existence of God.

courses.label: PHIL 237J
courses.title: Ethics and Society
paras: This course examines the nature and purpose of community living as weil as such traditionally controversial issues as
. private and public morality, the individual
good and the common good, personal freedom and group responsibility.

courses.label: PHIL 240A
courses.title: Logic
paras: A systematic development of the

paras: Elementary Logic : The classical logic introduced in PHIL 140 will be extended to form systems of modal logic, including logics of obligation, belief and knowledge, necessity, and temporal order. Essentialism, future contingencies, proofs for the existence of God will be discussed.
Prereq: PHIL 140 or consent of the instructor.

courses.title: Conftict, Contract and Choice

courses.title: Introduction to the Philosophy of
paras: Science.

A discussion of the fundamental concepts on which science is based. Consideration is given to such topics as scientific theories, the nature of lawlikeness, the grounds for scientific confirmation, and the debate between rationalism and empiricism in science.

courses.title: The Existentialiat Experience

PHIL 3010 W 3C 05 The Western Philosophical Tradition (1600 to present) Descartes to Existentialism. Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: PHIL 300X
courses.title: Sources of Twentieth-Century Thought
paras: An examination of major writings that have shaped present-day consciousness. Works by such thinkers as Marx, Darwin, Freud, Nietzsche and Mill will be included.

courses.title: Modern Feminism
paras: An examination of contemporary feminist
thought, de Beauvoir through to the
present. Positions taken on various
issues will be compared and critically

courses.label: PHIL 311
courses.title: Philosophy of Education 1
paras: A philosophical analysis of classical and contemporary theories of education, with a view to formulating a clear workable concept of education, its aims and methods.
Prereq: At least second year standing or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHIL 312
courses.title: Philosophy of Education 2
paras: An introduction to current work in the field. issues to be considered may include: the desirability and content of a core curriculum, methods of moral development, the problem of indoctrination, gender and education, computers and education, and peace education.

courses.label: PHIL 315
courses.title: Ethics and the Engineering Protession
paras: An analysis from the standpoint of philosophical ethics of moral issues arising in professional engineering practice. Issues include’ the social responsibility of engineers, conflict of interest and obligation, morally acceptable levels of risk, and moral implications of technology.

courses.label: PHIL 318
courses.title: Philosophy of the Family

family, its foundation, its purpose, its
importance in personal growth and its

or consent of instructor

Prereq: PHIL 221 recommended

law and legal reasoning forms the core
of this course. Law’s relations to
morality, social practice, and politics are
considered. Authors to be studied
include Aquinas, Kant, Austin and Hart. This is a required course for the
Legal Studies Option.

courses.label: PHIL 327B
courses.title: Philosophy of Law: Part 2

Prereq: PHIL 327A or consent of the instructor

courses.title: War, Peace and Justice
paras: An intensive study of the moral issues involved in war and armed revolution. Critical evaluation of “just war" theories and international rules of warfare is pursued as well as the moral argurnents for and against pacifism and conscientious objection.
Prereq: PHIL 102B or 322 or consent of instructor

Prereq: One full or two half courses in Philosophy, or consent of instructor

courses.title: Contemporary Philosophical Problems in Art
paras: An examination of some of the many philosophical problems, especially in music, painting, and poetry, which confront today’s artist as well as his audience. Traditional aesthetic categories are re-evaluated and contemporary philosophies of art considered.
Prereq: One other philosophy course, or consent of instructor

courses.label: PHYS 352
courses.title: Analogue Electronics
paras: DC and AC circuit theory, p and n materials, pn diodes, junction and FET transistors. Transistor amplifiers and their equivalent circuits. Operational ampiifiers. Feedback, oscillators and power supplies.
Prereq: Knowledge of determinants, elementary caiculus and elementary electricity
Coreq: 3521

courses.label: PHYS 352L
courses.title: Analogue Electronics Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 352
Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 353
courses.title: Digital Electronics
paras: Logic gates, flip-flops and shift registers. Binary numbers and Boolean algebra. An introduction to microprocessors is discussed based on the 6800. This will include arithmetic logic units, parallel input/output ports, assembly language and a number of examples.
Prereq: PHYS 122
Coreq: PHYS 353L

courses.label: PHYS 353L
courses.title: Digital Electronics Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 353 Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 354
courses.title: Atomic Molecular Physics
paras: The Schrédinger equation applied to simple one- and three-dimension potentials, hydrogen atoms, angular momentum and spin, molecular vibrations and rotations, many electron atoms, radiation processes. Prereq: PHYS 263, MATH 213a-213b Antireq: CHEM 355

courses.label: PHYS 358
courses.title: Thermodynamics
paras: Thermodynamic systems, equation of state, the laws of thermodynamics with applications. Change of phase.
Prereq: PHYS 254, MATH 213a-213b and 216

courses.label: PHYS 369
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
paras: Basic theory. ideal classical and quantum gas. Occupation numbers. Effects of statistics. Applications to metals, perfect crystals, radiation and dense fluids.
Prereq: PHYS 358

courses.label: PHYS 360A
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Selected experiments in mechanics, atomic physics, solid state physics, optics and electronics. Prereq: PHYS 263, MATH 213a-213b 18 hours of experiments
PHYS 3605 W 3L 0.25 Intermediate Laboratory Continuation of 360a. Prereq: PHYS 263, MATH 213a-213b 18 hours of experiments

courses.label: PHYS 363
courses.title: Classical Mechanics
paras: Application of the methods of classical mechanics to central force motion, rigid body rotation, coupled oscillations and motion in non-inertial frames; survey of Hamiltonian dynamics.
Prereq: PHYS 263, second year calculus
Primarily intended for Honours Physics students.

courses.label: PHYS 364
courses.title: Mathematical Physics 1
paras: Vector analysis and applications. Vector operators using curvilinear coordinates. Cartesian tensors. inertia tensor; stress, strain and rate of strain tensors. Applications to elasticity, fluids, electromagnetism and relativity. Prereg: MATH 213a-213b and 216 Primarily intended for Honours Physics students.

courses.label: PHYS 365
courses.title: Mathematical Physics 2
paras: Fourier series, integral and transform with applications. Use of the Laplace transform in physics. Partial differential equations of mathematical physics. Separation of variables. Bessel and Legendre functions with applications. Sturm-Liouville theory. Other special functions.
Prereq: MATH 213a-213b and 216
Primarily intended for Honours Physics students.

courses.label: PHYS 368
courses.title: Geophysics 4
paras: Introductory topics on the physics of the earth. Seismology and the earth’s interior. Thermat history of the earth, gravity and ‘scstasy. Origin of the continents and continental drift.
Prereq: First year physics and calculus
Cross-listed as EARTH 368.

courses.label: PHYS 369
courses.title: Geophysics 2
paras: The geology of the ocean basins. Topics in physical oceanography. Physical properties of ocean water, heat budget of the world oceans. Oceanic circulations. Coriolis effects. Some idealized current regimes.
Prereq: First year physics and calculus
Cross-listed as EARTH 369.

courses.label: PHYS 371A
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Further experiments in atomic, nuclear and solid state physics, optics and electronics. For honours students who are taking PHYS 360a.
18 hours experiments.

courses.label: PHYS 371B
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Continuation of 371A.
For honours students who are taking PHYS 360b.
18 hours experiments.

courses.label: PHYS 371C
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Microprocessor Interface Course. A Project laboratory course in which the student will interface some common microcomputers (e.g. PET, VIC20, Apple) to a variety of parallel and serial devices (e.g. terminal, D.V.M.).
Prereq: PHYS 353

courses.label: PHYS 380
courses.title: Molecular Blophysics
paras: Macromolecular structure and function, weak interactions, DNA replication, protein synthesis, energy production, photosynthesis, control of intracellular processes, structure of viruses, physical techniques.

courses.label: PHYS 381
courses.title: Cell Biophysics
paras: Structure and function of cellular membranes and organelles, membrane potentials and ion transport, nerve conduction, muscle contraction, vision and interaction of light with cells intercellular communication, growth control.
Course Descriptions Physics

courses.label: PHYS 432
courses.title: Physics of Solid State Devices
paras: The theories of solid state physics are applied to explain the operation and use of several modern electronic devices, including the p-n junction, transistors, thyristors, tunnel! diodes, field effect devices, optical devices, etc.
Prereq: PHYS 435

courses.label: PHYS 433A
courses.title: Experimental Research Project
paras: An experimental research project. This course is designed for students in the Honours Physics program and in the Co-operative Applied Physics program.
Students in the regular Hons Physics program must take either PHYS 433 or PHYS 437.
Although students in the Co-operative Applied Physics (Hons) program are advised to take 1 of these courses, enrolment may be limited. -
No credit or grade is given for the first-term course unless the two-term sequence, PHYS 4334/8, is completed.

courses.label: PHYS 434
courses.title: Introductory Quantum Mechanics
paras: Origins and necessity for quantum mechanics and its concepts and formulation. The Hamiltonian operator and Schrédinger’s equation, the harmonic oscillator (Schrédinger’s treatment). The uncertainty principle. Momentum representation. One dimensional potential problems. Angular momentum. The hydrogen atom.
Prereq: PHYS 354, 364, and 365

courses.label: PHYS 435
courses.title: Solid State Physics
paras: Introductory concepts in crystal diffraction and the reciprocal lattice. Crystal bonding. Lattice vibrations, thermal properties of insulators, free-electron theory of metals, band theory. Semiconductors.
Prereq: Completion of Year 3 Honours. Physics

courses.label: PHYS 437A
courses.title: Theoretical Physics Project
paras: Selected subjects for advanced study by theoretically inclined students, topics in relativistic, quantum, and statistical physics. Fall term enrolment will be limited.
Students in the regular Hons Physic program must take either PHYS 437a or PHYS 433.
Although students in the Co-operative Applied Physics (Hons) program are encouraged to take 1 of these courses, enrolment may be limited.
PHYS 4387b W -3R 0.5
Continued Theoretical Physics Project

A continuation and extension of the project initiated in PHYS 437a. Available only to those students who have satisfdctorily completed that portion of the Project contained in PHYS 437a in the immediately preceding term.
Students intending to take both PHYS 437a and 437b must register for both courses, and have their registration approved by the Theoretical Physics Project co-ordinator, at the start of the Fall term.

courses.label: PHYS 441A
courses.title: Electromagnetic Theory
paras: A generalized treatment of the basic laws of electricity and magnetism, mathematical techniques for the problems of electrostatics, solution of Maxwell's equations in free space and the study of plan waves, theory of waveguides and introduction to radiation.
Prereq: PHYS 253, PHYS 364-365
No credit or grade is given for the first-term course unless the two-term sequence, PHYS 441A/8, is completed.

courses.label: PHYS 442
courses.title: Structure of Solids
paras: A survey with emphasis on the physical properties and behaviour of metals and alloys. Elastic and plastic deformations of crystais. Solidification, structure of alloys, free energy of alloy systems, equilibrium diagrams, diffusion, solid state phase transformation
Prereq: PHYS 435

courses.label: PHYS 443
courses.title: Continuum Mechanics
paras: General description of continuum behaviour: stress, strain, rate of strain, constitutive relations, equations of motion, affect of symmetry; thermodynamics, Elastic media: Hooke’s law, simple problems, elastic waves. Fluids: classification, perfect fluids, Newtonian fluids, boundary layers, turbulence, Viscoelasticity, plastoelasticity. Applications to various system.
Prereq: PHYS 364-365

courses.label: PHYS 444
courses.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
paras: Theory of deuteron. Nucleon-nucleon scattering. Nuclear models. Basic concepts in particle physics. Conservation laws and invariance principles, SU (3) model. The quark model.
Prereq: PHYS 455, and PHYS 434

courses.label: PHYS 445
courses.title: Modern Optics
paras: Basic electromagnetic wave theory. Polarization reflection, refraction and dispersion. Fibre optics and communica-
tions. Temporal coherence and spectra.
Spatial coherence and diffraction. Phase contrast microscopy. Basics of Holography. Crystal optics and nonlinear effects. Lasers, modes, pulses and propagation of beams.
Prereq: PHYS 256 and PHYS 354

courses.label: PHYS 449
courses.title: Radio Astronomy
paras: Radio telescopes. Radio sources including the sun. H {l regions, H | regions. The galactic centre, pulsars, quasars, other extragalactic sources, cosmological implications.
Prereq: PHYS 253 and PHYS 250-251 or consent of instructor
Offered in even calendar years.

courses.label: PHYS 450
courses.title: Astrophysics 3
paras: Solar system astrophysics (excluding the sun). The physical nature of planetary (and satellite) surfaces, atmospheres and interiors. Asteroids, meteorites and comets. The interplanetary medium (solar wind). Solar interactions with the interplanetary medium and earth’s magnetosphere.
Prereq: PHYS 250 or consent of instructor
Familiarity with the contents of PHYS 250-251, however, will be assumed.

courses.label: PHYS 451
courses.title: Astrophysics 4
paras: The structure of stellar interiors, nuclear reactions and energy sources in the stars of the main sequence, early evolution of stars from the main sequence. Lifetimes of the stars
Prereq: PHYS 251 or consent of instructor .
Familiarity with the contents of PHYS 250-251, however, will be assumed.
Offered in even calendar years.
PHYS 449, PHYS 451 are also open to third and fourth year students. PHYS 350 alternates with PHYS 451 and PHYS 351 alternates with PHYS 449.

courses.label: PHYS 463B
courses.title: Advanced Analogue Electronics
paras: A variety of topics in the operation of systems. Transistors, modern circuit techniques, noise, stability under feedback, information theory, and possible student motivated topics. Includes laboratory demonstrations.
Prereq: PHYS 352-353

courses.label: PHYS 454
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
paras: The matrix formulation of quantum mechanics. The harmonic oscillator (Heisenberg’s treatment). The matrices for angular momentum. Time- | independent and time-dependent perturbation theory. The interaction of atomic systems with radiation. Multiparticle systems, identical particles. Pauli exclusion principle. Tha helium atom. Prereq: PHYS 434. ‘ PHYS 454 is strongly recommended for students intending to do graduate work.

courses.label: PHYS 455
courses.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
paras: Nuclear structure, interactions of nuclear radiations with matter, radioactive decay, nuclear reactions, nuclear force, elementary particles.
Prereq: PHYS 354.

courses.label: PHYS 464
courses.title: Mathematical Physics 3
paras: Applications to Physics of the theory of
functions of a complex variable. Prereq: PHYS 364-365

courses.label: PHYS 465
courses.title: Mathematical Physics 4
paras: Theory and applications of integral
transforms, integral equations and
Green's functions. Asymptotic analysis. Prereq: PHYS 464

courses.label: PHYS 480
courses.title: Radiation Biophysics
paras: The effect of radiation of various kinds on calls and tissues, exposure calculations, mechanism of damage, repair theories, genetic effect, target theory, isotopic tracers in biophysical research.

courses.label: PHYS 481
courses.title: Biophysics of Organ Systems
paras: Physics of hemeostasis, interactions with the environment, circulation of blood, temperature regulation, respiration, transport problems and special organ systems.
PHYS 487 and 482 are offered in alter. nate years.

courses.label: PHYS 482
courses.title: Biophysics of Nervous Systems
paras: Neurons; nerve conduction, sensory transducers; coding, processing and storage of information; control of muscles and other effector organs. Recommended for third or fourth year students in Math, Eng, Sci or HKLS.

Course Descriptions

introductory Note
Extensive descriptions of the content of Political Science courses are available in the Department at the time of preregistration.

courses.label: PSCI 101A
courses.title: Introduction to Politics 1
paras: An introduction to the nature of politics and to the conflict of political ideas
within the setting of a liberal democracy.
The purpose is a clearer understanding of conservatism, liberalism and socialism.

courses.label: PSCI 101M
courses.title: Introduction to Public Policy
paras: This course is an introduction to the process of policy making. Students will be given an opportunity to examine, in the context of several examples, the factors affecting choices among policy alternatives. In addition, questions about the range of alternatives and the implementation of policies will be addressed.
P SCI 102 consists of a series of courses dealing with different aspects of politics. Students should select the course which most closely corresponds to their interest.
First-year winter term courses will be drawn from the following list.

courses.label: PSCI 102D
courses.title: The Political Process in the Modern Democracies °
paras: A study of power and influence in the modern democracies, based on.an examination of 3 contending models in the political process - the liberal democratic or popular rule model, the pluralist model, and the elitist model.

courses.label: PSCI 102E
courses.title: Political Rights and Obligations
paras: An introductory examination of the idea of individual rights as a limitation on legitimate governmental authority, the possible grounds for such claimed rights, and their relationships to political obligations (duties).

courses.label: PSCI 102
courses.title: Mass Political Violence |
paras: A distinctive social feature of our century is the amount of. political violence. Man-made deaths number approximately one hundred million. This course will describe and evaluate various theories of political violence.
Course Descriptions Political Science

courses.label: PSCI 102M
courses.title: Contemporary issues in Canadian
paras: Public Policy.
An evaluation of various public policy responses to some contemporary Canadian social, cultural, economic, environmental, and political problems, as well as thé process of policy-making.

courses.label: PSCI 214
courses.title: Quantitative Analysis
paras: An introduction to the use of quantita: tive methods in Political Science. Only a rudimentary understanding of mathematics is required. Prereq: Second year standing Students who have taken or are taking a course of similar content in another discipline should check with their Undergraduate Officer or the Arts Registrars Office to determine if credit will be granted for both courses.

courses.label: PSCI 225
courses.title: The History of Political Theory 1
paras: A survey of the principal ideas of-
Western political theorists fram the
earliest times to the 17th century. Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: PSCI 226
courses.title: The History of Political Theory 2
paras: A survey of the principal ideas of Western political theorists since the 17th century.
Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: PSCI 231
courses.title: Government and Business in
paras: Canada
An examination of the political environ-
ment in which business functions in
Canada with particular emphasis on the
constraints and opportunities condi-
tioned by government intervention in
and interaction with the private sector. Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: PSCI 255
courses.title: The Politics of Western Industrial Nations
paras: A systematic introduction to the political processes of industrial countries. The central focus will be on Western Europe and North America. Some attention, however, will be devoted to the Antipodes, the Mediterranean countries, South Africa and Japan.
Prereq: Second year standing
Course Descriptions. . Political Science —

courses.label: PSCI 256B
courses.title: The Politics of Western Industrial Nations Il
paras: This course will examine a number of ways by which developed countries have tried to overcome the contempofary “crisis”. Topics to be discussed include economic planning and participation, wage controls, corporatism, decentralization and authoritarianism. Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: PSCI 260A
courses.title: Canadian Government and Politica 1
paras: An analysis of the political environment in which the Canadian political system operates, including discussion of the Canadian political culture, federalism, the constitution, federal-provincial relations, and the role of the Governor General.
No prereq for students in the second year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 260B
courses.title: Canadian Government and Politics 2
paras: An analysis of the decision-making machinery of the Canadian political system, including discussion of cabinet " government, the role of the House of Commons, interest groups, the electoral system, the party system and voting behaviour.
Prereq: P SCI 260A or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 264
courses.title: American Government and Politics
paras: The theory and practice of the American political system as revealed by the institutions and operations of American national government.
No prereq for students in the second year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 268
courses.title: British Government and Politics
paras: An examination of the uniquely British characteristics of the British political system.
No prereq for students in the second year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 271
courses.title: Political Behaviour 1
paras: Empirical approaches to the study of
politics are examined in light of their
assumptions, aspirations, and critics. No prereq for students in the second
year and above.
sf

courses.label: PSCI 281
courses.title: International Politics
paras: This course studies the transformation of the international system stressing East-West, Rich-Poor, and North-South perspectives and interactions.
No prereq for students in the second year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 282
courses.title: Foreign Policy
paras: This course studies the roots of foreign policy behaviour of selected western and non-western (particularly Asian) states.
Prereq: P SCI 281 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 291
courses.title: The Canadian Legal Process
paras: An analysis of the manner in which the Common Law functions, together with an examination of the structure and jurisdiction of the Canadian court systems. Taught by a member of the legal profession.
Prereq: Open to all students in the second year and above

courses.label: PSCI 292
courses.title: Issues in Canadian Criminal Law
paras: Rational principles and concepts appli-

cable to current emotional criminal issues are analyzed by a practising crown attorney, for example, abortion, euthanasia, pornography, seat belts, homosexuality, marijuana, policy power, civil rights, criminal trials, jury, capital punishment, prisons, etc.
Prereq: Open to all students in the second year and above

courses.label: PSCI 295
courses.title: Public Sector Management
paras: This course examines the functions of management with major emphasis placed on employee relations, values, communication, motivation and leadership.
Prereq: Second-year or consent of instructor
This course is specifically designed for Co-op and Administrative Studies students .

courses.label: PSCI 315
courses.title: Research Design in Political Science
paras: Introduction to the logic and limitations of experimental and non-experimental research designs. Selected studies of politics are examined to demonstrate how plausible threats to validity are made less plausible with appropriate design and data analysis.
Prereq: P SCI 214 or consent of instructor
P SC! 321 F 2S 05 Marxist Theory A basic introduction to the political and social thought of Karl Marx from the early writings to capital.
Prereq: None

courses.label: PSCI 322
courses.title: Marxism and Revolution after Marx
paras: A selective study.of developments in Marxist theory and political. movements after Marx.
Prereq: P SCI 321

courses.label: PSCI 323
courses.title: Ancient Political Philosophy
paras: A Selective examination of political philosophy during the classica! period in Greece.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 324
courses.title: Modern Political Philosophy
paras: A selective examination of political
philosophy in the modern period. Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 331
courses.title: Public Administration 1
paras: An introduction to the principles of public administration illustrated by the study of Canadian institutions largely at the federal level, but including provincial and municipal examples.
Prereq: P SCI 260A and 260B or consent of instructor
PSCI3392 WS 28 05 Public Administration 2 Analysis of problems and issues in the field applying the knowledge gained in P SCI 331.
Prereq: P SCI 331 or consent of instructor .

courses.label: PSCI 333
courses.title: Administrative Law
paras: A study of Canadian administrative law including the delegation of political power to various administrative agencies which play a prominent role in controlling contemporary social and economic life. The supervisory role of the courts will also be examined.
Prereq: P SCI 331 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 342
courses.title: Politics in Quebec
paras: A seminar dealing with the political and social development of Quebec. The emphasis will be on the problems and
- issues of contemporary Quebec.
Prereq: P SCI 260A and 260B or 341 or consent: of instructor
PSCIM3 F 2C O05
Canadian Municipal Government
A study of the assumptions, structures
and performance of municipal govern-
ment in Canada with reference to
metropolitan and regional structural
innovations (particularly in Ontario). Open to students in the third year
and above with at least 1 previous
course in Political science.

courses.label: PSCI 344
courses.title: The Politics of Local Government
paras: A study of the political process in selected Canadian cities focusing on citizen participation, internal decisionmaking, leadership, and the allocation of power.
Prereq: P SCI 343 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 350A
courses.title: The Politics of the Developing Areas 1
paras: An introduction to the politics of Asia, Africa and Latin America focusing upon the political roots of poverty in the developing areas. Topics include the impact of world trade, colonization, multinationals and foreign aid.
No prereq for students in the third year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 350B
courses.title: The Politics of the Developing Areas 2
paras: An examination of the politics of the developing areas with emphasis on the political behaviour of peasants, the urban poor, organized labour, and the military.
No prereq for students in the third year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 351
courses.title: Comparative Federal Systems
paras: A comparative examination of federal systems, with an emphasis on the problems and processes of integration and disintegration.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 383
courses.title: Comparative Communist Systems
paras: This course, which will focus on the Soviet Union, China and Cuba (with reference to Yugoslavia), will familiarize students with the differences and similarities that exist among communist countries..
Prereq: Third year standing and” consent of instructor

P SCI 363: -F OS Canadian Constitutional Law An introduction to the nature and basic Principles of constitutional law. This course will deal especially with the distribution of powers in the Canadian federation, and its evolution, notably by judicial decision. Leading cases will be examined.
Prereq: P SCI 260A and 260B or 260A and consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 366
courses.title: Chinese Politics
paras: An analysis of the historical develop-
ment, contemporary politics and future
directions of the People’s Republic of
China emphasizing the role of ideology.
political institutions, citizen participation
and policy-making in selected areas. Prereq: Third year standing and
consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 375
courses.title: The Politics of Self-Management
paras: An examination of the participation of citizens in decision making, both at work and in politics. The self-management system of Yugoslavia will be studied in detail.
Prereq: Second year standing or above

courses.label: PSCI 380A
courses.title: World Politics 1
paras: An examination of the structure of the world capitalist system concentrating upon warfare between core states during 1815-1945 and assessing the impact of the nuclear revolution. A number of classic theories of imperialism are considered.
Open only to students in the third year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 380B
courses.title: World Politics 2
paras: An examination of the allocation of misery in the world capitalist system. The focus is on core/periphery relations and a number of theories of imperialism are considered.
Prereq: Open only to students in the third year and above
Special Studies
From time to time courses of special study may be added to the program at the third year level. Students wishing to take such courses should consuit the Department's Undergraduate Officer.

courses.title: Selected Subjects in Political Philosophy
paras: A selective treatment of basic themes in political philosophy in the modern and pre-moderm times.
Prereq: For third year Political Science students, but open to others with prereq of P SCI 225, 226, 323, or 324, or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 427
courses.title: Special Topics in Political
paras: Philosophy
A selective examination of basic prob-
lems in political philosophy in the
modern and pre-modem periods. Prereq: P SCI 225, 226, 323, or 324

courses.label: PSCI 428
courses.title: State and Economic Life
paras: An analytical and comparative study of
the. growth of government intervention in
the economic process, and of the
development of the welfare state. Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 431
courses.title: Canadian Public Policy
paras: An examination of the way that policy making processes and institutions have responded to the problems of governing, especially at the federal level in Canada.
Prereq: P SCI 260A and 260B and consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 433
courses.title: Public Policy and Underdevelopment in the Third World
paras: An examination of industrial strategies, agricultural programs and energy policies of selected Third World countries focussing upon the political obstacles, both domestic and foreign, to the achievement of the long term integrated planning required for the alleviation of poverty in-the Third World.
Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of instructor

P SCI 4385 W 28 05 The Politics of Canadian Resource Development A seminar focusing on the strategies of resource development policies, with an emphasis on the economic, political, environmental and cultural implications of oil, natural gas, and mineral exploitation.
Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of instructor
Political Science

courses.label: PSCI 436
courses.title: Comparative Public Policy: The Politics of Food
paras: P SCI 436 will introduce the actors and
the framework of norms, rules and prac-
tices that control the global food regime. The course will then proceed to deal with selected problems in the politics of food.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor *

courses.label: PSCI 437
courses.title: The Politics of International Resources
paras: AN examination of the politics of international resources. Attention will be given to the set of issues relating to minerals, water, oceanic fisheries, oil energy, timber and labour. Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 442
courses.title: Politics in Ontario
paras: A critical examination of the distinct elements of government and politics in the Province of Ontario
Prereq: P SCI 260A and 260B or 341 or consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 443
courses.title: Politics in Western Canada
paras: A critical examination of the distinctive elements of government and politics in the provinces of Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta and British Columbia. Prereq: P SCI 260 or 341 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 453
courses.title: Comparative Politics of Latin America
paras: The course examines the politics of Latin America focussing upon the inter- ‘play between external ties and internal processes. Topics include comparative studies of class alliances, the establishment of bureaucratic authoritarian regimes and revolutionary movements. Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of instructor ‘

courses.label: PSCI 454
courses.title: Comparative Politics
paras: Selected topics in the politics of the Third World. Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 461
courses.title: Problems in Canadian Politics 1
paras: Selected aspects of Canadian nationat politics.
Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 462
courses.title: Problems in Canadian Politics 2
paras: Selected aspects of Canadian provincial politics.
Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 471
courses.title: Public Opinion and Propaganda
paras: A detailed study of the nature of public opinion and the attempt to control it through propaganda.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor
P.SCI 473 2S 05
Voting Behaviour
A comparative study of the motivations
underlying electoral choice in Canada.
Great Britain and the United States. Prereq: P SCI 214, 373 or consent of
instructor

courses.label: PSCI 475
courses.title: Political Socialization
paras: A study of the processes and agents of political socialization and their effects on political stability or change in liberaldemocratic societies..
Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 476
courses.title: Research Seminar in Political Behaviour
paras: A research-oriented seminar on selected theoretical works in political behaviour, with an emphasis on the development of research projects dealing with Canadian topics.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 479
courses.title: Senior Research Seminar: Violence in the Political Process
paras: Politics can be brutal. This seminar deals with violence in the political process. The focus on the relationships between the society and the coercive apparatus of the state.
Prereq: Third or fourth year standing

courses.label: PSCI 481
courses.title: Research Seminar on World Politics
paras: An examination of research on the causes and consequences of interstate warfare.
Prereq: P SCI 380 or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 483
courses.title: Power Politics and World Order Studies
paras: This theory course examines the evolution of the international system; the capacity of the system of states to cope with the demands on it; meanings of international and regional power and order.
Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of the instructor

courses.label: PSCI 484
courses.title: Contemporary Strategies: Theories and Policies
paras: The course examines strategic studies and their premises, the evolution of Strategic thinking, the role of national policies of military power. Strategic concepts are studied with specific reference to military policies of regional powers.
Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of instructor

courses.label: PSCI 486
courses.title: Middle Powers and World Politics
paras: The course studies the literature on middle powers (including Canada). Particular ernphasis is on the study of self-images, views of power, of power politics, and the sources of influence of these powers.
Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of the instructor

powers, and the search for peace. Prereq: Fourth year standing or

courses.label: PSYCH 101
courses.title: Introductory Psychology
paras: A general survey course designed to provide the student with an understanding of the basic concepts and techniques of modern psychology as a behavioural science. Students may receive credit for only one of PSYCH 101 or PSYCH 120R Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

PSYCH 102 ; Introductory Psychology Special Topics An in-depth study of selected broad issues and problems introduced in PSYCH 101. Students may receive credit for only one of PSYCH 102 or PSYCH 121R Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 102A
courses.title: Applied Psychology
paras: Applications of Psychological research to contemporary problems: man and environment, human factors engineering, management and organizations, crime and violence, and public health.

courses.label: PSYCH 102B
courses.title: Nature, Nurture and Human
paras: Behaviour .
The role of heredity and environment in the development of intelligence, person-, ality and personality disorders, and conflict and aggression.

courses.label: PSYCH 102C
courses.title: Culture’s Influence on Behaviour
paras: The role of culture on the development of Petception, Cognition, Learning and, - Memory, cultural influences on personality and personality disorders, and on conflict and aggression.

courses.label: PSYCH 102D
courses.title: Paychology of Consciousness
paras: Modes of thinking, emotion, creativity, anu altered states of consciousness.

courses.label: PSYCH 102E
courses.title: Psychological Intervention Applications of Psychology to human
paras: coping problems and growth with emphasis on analyzing critically current treatment methods.
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 102F
courses.title: Persona! Adjustment
paras: Focus on research which investigates the everyday task of coping with ourselves, our environment, and the peopie we encounter. Topics will focus on the themes of knowing the self, interpersonal relationships, and of the way in which our social and physical environment affects our behaviour.

courses.label: PSYCH 102G
courses.title: Introduction to Neuroscience
paras: The relation between brain as a substrate and mind as a process is an important scientific and philosophical problem. In this course, those biological aspects of brain function will be discussed which are directly related to the functioning of the human mind.

courses.label: PSYCH 200
courses.title: Measurement in Psychology
paras: The logic of measurement in Psychology. Descriptive procedures for collecting and handling data. Making inferences from test scores. The use of correlational procedures in measuring intelligence, achievement, aptitudes, interests and personality.

courses.label: PSYCH 203
courses.title: Learning and Motivation
paras: This course is designed to introduce the
student to theories in Learning and
Motivation and to provide the student
with an understanding of the experi-
mental techniques in these areas. Prereq: PSYCH 101

courses.label: PSYCH 206
courses.title: Perceptual Processes
paras: An examination of data and theory concerning perceptual processes. Topics will include the perception of form and space; perceptual learning and a consideration of the effect of personality variables in perception.
Prereq: PSYCH 101

courses.label: PSYCH 207
courses.title: Cognitive Processes
paras: An examination and evaluation of selected topics dealing with human learning, thinking, concept formation, memory and language.
Prereq: PSYCH 101

courses.label: PSYCH 211
courses.title: Developmental Psychology
paras: An examination of the process and_. factors of human development. Prereq: PSYCH 101 Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 212
courses.title: Educational Psychology
paras: A consideration of the main variables affecting leaming in the classroom with special focus upon the conditions essential to efficient learning.
Prereq: PSYCH 101
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 213
courses.title: Exceptional Children
paras: Educational problems associated with mental retardation, emotional disturbances, sensory and physical impairments and intellectual giftedness.

courses.label: PSYCH 214
courses.title: Psychology of Adolescence
paras: A’study of the psychological processes in the second decade of human development. Consideration is given to such areas as intellectual, emotional and social growth, and identity formation. Current concepts, issues, and research are stressed.
Prereq: PSYCH 214
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 217
courses.title: Aging and Basic Psychological Processes
paras: What processes change as adults age? ls the idea of age-related decline in functioning a myth? The course deals with processes such as memory, perception, intelligence, and problemsolving. it also outlines the problems in interpreting developmental research. Prereq: PSYCH 101

courses.label: PSYCH 218
courses.title: Aging, Dying and Death
paras: An examination of the psychological _ aspects of aging and the traditional and recent literature relating to various views on the reality of death in the life of man. Therapy with dying individuals is reviewed and evaluated.
Prereq: PSYCH 101
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 231
courses.title: Psychology of Religious Experience
paras: Approaches of traditional psychological theories and especially of a modern psychology of consciousness toward phenomena of religious experience, mysticism and meditation are examined. The transcendent phenomena are compared with other altered states of consciousness.
Prereq: PSYCH 101
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 235
courses.title: Paychological Perspectives on Gender and Sex
paras: The course focuses on the existence of and bases for sex and gender differences with emphasis on biological, psychological and cultural issues.

courses.label: PSYCH 236
courses.title: A Psychological Analysis of Human
paras: Sexuality. . . This course will examine psychological and social psychological theories and empirical investigations of human sexuality. Prereq: PSYCH 101 or permission of instructor . Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 263
courses.title: Social Psychology
paras: An introduction to the scientific, study of social behaviour and social influences on behaviour. Theories and research on such topics as attitude change and persuasion, stereotypes and prejudice, conformity and obedience to authority, altruism, conflict, attraction and ®ve will be introduced. Students may receive credit for only one of PSYCH 253 or PSYCH 220R Prereq: PSYCH 101

courses.label: PSYCH 264
courses.title: Interpersonal Relations
paras: A psychological analysis of social inter-
action, The development of interpersonal
attraction from first impressions to long-
term relationships. The roots of hostility.
conflict and communication problems. Students may receive credit for only
one of PSYCH 254 or PSYCH 221R Prereq: PSYCH 253

courses.label: PSYCH 258
courses.title: Principles and Evolution of Psychoanalytic Thought
paras: This course expresses the fundamental psychoanalytic vision as articulated by Sigmund Freud, and its relevance to the humanities. The theme is to understand the potentially liberating spirit which is at the root of psychoanalysis.
Prereq: PSYCH 101
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 261
courses.title: Physiological Psychology
paras: Introduction to brain, basic physiological processes, and their roles in behaviour. Course covers sensing and perceiving; neural bases of action; motivation; learning and memory; and consciousness. Both experimental and clinical data are considered.
Prereq: PSYCH 101 or permission of instructor

courses.label: PSYCH 271
courses.title: Animal Behaviour
paras: Survey of mechanisms, development, adaptive value and evaluation of behaviour in non-human animals. Covers ethology, sociobiology and experimental comparative psychology. Emphasis on principles of research with laboratory and wild animals as well as methods of observing behaviour. : Prereq: PSYCH 101 or permission of instructor

courses.label: PSYCH 291
courses.title: Basic Research Methods
paras: An introduction to the methods used in psychological research. Methods for observing behaviour and the procedures used to summarize these observations are emphasized.
Prereq: PSYCH 101 and second year Honours standing in Psychology

courses.label: PSYCH 202
courses.title: Basic Data Analysis
paras: An introduction ta the logic and methods of inferential statistics with emphasis on application in Psychology. Also included is a more detailed treatment of the methods and projects introduced in PSYCH 291.
Prereq: PSYCH 291 and second year Honours standing in Psychology
See overlapping content note (Grading Systems, Item 6) on page 8.7.

courses.title: Sensory Processes
paras: A consideration of data and theory
concerning sensory processess. Topics
will include psychophysical methodology.
sensory mechanisms, and the neurop-
sychological basis of perceptions. Prereq: PSYCH 206

courses.label: PSYCH 307
courses.title: Cognitive Neurology
paras: An introduction to current human experimental neuropsychology. The course will review evidence for brain-behaviour interactions obtained from studies of human brain damage and from investigations of the normal brain. Topics such as the representation of language, hemispheric specialization, memory, spatial ability, dyslexia, movement disorders and affective disorders will be considered.
Prereq: One of PSYCH 206, 207, 261, or KIN 356

courses.label: PSYCH 311
courses.title: Behaviour and Development of Human Infants
paras: The purposes of this course are to study the behaviour and development of human infants, to gain direct experience with infants, and to examine community attitudes and resources available for infant care.
Prereq: PSYCH 211 or permission of instructor

courses.label: PSYCH 312
courses.title: Learning Disabilities
paras: A critical examination of the concept of learning disability and of current issues in the assessment and remediation of learning problems. Prereq: PSYCH 211, 212, or 213 Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 316
courses.title: Moral Development
paras: A consideration of psychological theory and research dealing with the nature and origin of morat development, developmental differences in moral judgement, and various approaches to teaching moral behaviour with its consequent effects on the individual. Prereq: PSYCH 211 Also offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: PSYCH 317
courses.title: The Emotionally Disturbed Child
paras: An examination of children’s psychological disorders from several major perspectives with an emphasis on current research findings. Theoretical and clinical issues are considered. Prereg: PSYCH 211 Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 322A
courses.title: Principles and Practice in Early Childhood Education 1
paras: Current principles of teaching preschoo!l-aged children. An emphasis is placed on those curricula which aim to foster social and cognitive development. Topics inciude: characteristics and needs of children in group-care settings; classroom management; curriculum planning.
Prereq: Acceptance into the Early Childhood Education and Care Option

produce important changes in the way people think, feel and behave including psychoanalysis, behaviour therapy, brainwashing, cult conversions, deprogramming, hypnosis, biofeedback and meditation.
Prereq: PSYCH 101

courses.label: PSYCH 339
courses.title: Personnel Psychology
paras: An examination of the following | major topics in personnel psychology: employment planning, selection and. recruitment, selection techniques, career development, performance appraisal, training programs, labour relations, compensations systems.
Prereq: PSYCH 333

courses.label: PSYCH 340
courses.title: Community Psychology
paras: Theory and practice are integrated in an attempt to identify and to understand the social factors which inhibit or facilitate healthy development of the individual. The adequacy of existing social structures and institutions in the treatment of various personal problems is assessed..
Prereq: PSYCH 253
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 120R
courses.title: Introductory Psychology
paras: Basic concepts and techniques of modern psychology as a behavioural science, with special emphasis on social aspects of behaviour. Topics may include the nervous system, perception, learning, memory, cognition, motivation, emotion, development, personality, social influences, psychopathology and psychotherapy. . Students may receive credit for only one of PSYCH 120R or PSYCH 101

courses.label: PSYCH 121R
courses.title: Introductory Psychology (Special Topics)
paras: A continuation of PSYCH 120R with in-depth study of some selected topics. Prereq: PSYCH 120R Students may receive credit for only one of PSYCH 121R or PSYCH 102

courses.label: PSYCH 220R
courses.title: Social Psychology
paras: Examination of psychological principles involved in individual-society interaction. Topics may include research methods, self, sexual attitudes and behaviour, person perception, attitudes, affiliation, aggression, altruism, groups, environment and behaviour, ioneliness, social psychology and legal process.
Prereq: An introductory Psychology course
Students may receive credit for only one of PSYCH 220R or PSYCH 253

courses.label: PSYCH 221R
paras: Interpersonal interaction A consideration of selected theories of interpersonal interaction. Topics include E. Goffman, non-verbal communication, H.S. Sullivan, transactional analysis, the double-bind theory, R.D. Laing, the basic dimensions of interpersonal behaviour, and social exchange. Prereq: PSYCH 220R or PSYCH 253 Students may receive credit for only one of PSYCH 221R or PSYCH 254
PSYCH 32°R F 3C 05 Personality Theory An examination of the major theories of personality including consideration of the psychoanalytic, dispositional, humanistic, and behaviouristic models.
Prereq: An introductory Psychology mise Students may receive credit for only ere of PSYCH 322R or PSYCH 355

courses.label: PSYCH 323R
courses.title: Abnormal Psychology
paras: * sivey of concepts, theory, and esearch dealing with the nature and etiology of behavioural abnormality. Topics include neurosis, schizophrenia, depression, psychophysiological and behavioural disorders.
Prereq: An introductory Psychology Course
Students may receive credit for only one of PSYCH 323R or PSYCH 357

courses.label: PSYCH 334
courses.title: Theories of Individual Counselling Psychology
paras: An introduction to the methods, theories an problems in individual Counselling Psychology.
Prereq: An introductory Psychology course.

courses.title: Special! Topics in Psychology
paras: One cr more term courses will be offered from time to time as announced by the Social Development Studies Prag:am. Subjects will be dependent uocn special research and/or instructional interests of facuity.

courses.label: PSYCH 398R
courses.title: Independent Study
paras: 4 independent in-depth study of a selected area of concern to the student within the discipline of Psychology. Available to individuals or small groups of third or fourth year Social Development Studies majors and arranged with one of the faculty members from the program.
Prereq Permission of Undergraduate Officer

courses.label: REC 100
courses.title: Introduction to the Study of Leisure and Recreation and Leisure Services
paras: An overview of the field of recreation emphasizing the understanding of leisure phenomena as well as an introduction to various leisure service agencies and their programs provided.

courses.label: REC 200
courses.title: Theories of Play
paras: A critical analysis of definitions, concepts and assumptions of classical, recent and modern theories of play with implications for research strategies, programming and planning for play.

courses.label: REC 201
courses.title: Leisure and the Social Sciences
paras: Examination of modern methodological and theoretical approaches to the study of leisure behaviour with emphasis upon the socio-cultural, socio-psychological and economic dimensions.

courses.label: REC 203
courses.title: An Introduction to the Sociology of
paras: Sport . An introduction to the characteristics, processes and probiems of sport as a social system. In addition, the social psychological aspects of sport involvement are considered.
Prereq: SOC 101
Cross-listed as KIN 252 and SOC 348.

courses.label: REC 204
courses.title: Leisure and Recreation in Historical Perspective
paras: Analysis of socio-cultural determinants which have influenced Canadian Leisure behaviour.
Prereq: REC 100 or consent of instructor

courses.label: REC 210
courses.title: Organization and Administration of Recreation Services
paras: The organization and administration of recreation on federal, provincial and municipal levels; jegislation, financing, budgeting, problem solving, public retations, administrative practices and departmental organization with particular emphasis on the municipal jevel.

courses.label: REC 220
courses.title: Program Management in Leisure Services
paras: A study of the scope of community recreation programs and the factors invoived in program leadership. Emphasis will be placed on the goals in recreation for the leader and participant. effective leadership of individuals and groups, individual and group creativity.

courses.label: REC 230
courses.title: Introduction to Outdoor Recreation
paras: A study of outdoor recreation in relation to contemporary lifestyles, natural and human resource systems. Includes the examination of outdoor settings as an integral part of an outdoor recreation continuum. Includes the role of selected governmental and non-governmental bodies.

courses.label: REC 241
courses.title: Administration of Camping and Outdoor Education
paras: The philosophy and objectives of camping and outdoor education; administration, organizing, planning, staff, relationships, feadership training, trends in camping and outdoor education. The emphasis in this course will be the place of the resident camp in education and recreation.
Prereq: REC 230

courses.label: REC 250
courses.title: Introduction to Recreation for Special Populations
paras: Examines the philosophical, theoretical and empirical frameworks of recreation as a therapeutic service and process to individuals with physical, emotional and intetlectua! disabilities.

courses.label: REC 270A
courses.title: Research Design Applicable to Leisure Studies
paras: An introduction the the methods and techniques of research as applied to leisure studies and services. General consideration will be given to the technical problems involved in various stages of research methodology with emphasis on the logic underlying the research process.
Course Descriptions Recreation and Leleure Studies

courses.label: REC 300
courses.title: Philosophy of Leisure
paras: Examination of major philosophical themes through the ages with reference ta contemporary viability and effect upon social behaviour.
Prereq: Consent of instructor; third year standing

courses.label: REC 301
courses.title: Sociology of Leisure
paras: Nature and extent of leisure phenomena in contemporary society. Examination of institutional and formal organizational aspects, social role, social research Strategies employed in the study of leisure. .
Prereq: Two item courses in Soci
ology Cross-listed as SOC 347.

courses.label: REC 302
courses.title: Travel and Tourism
paras: The scope and nature of travel and tourism as contemporary leisure experiences. Economic, political and social ramifications, research strategies employed, imptications for the future.

courses.label: REC 304
courses.title: Community and Cultural Development
paras: A study of major issues of Canadian cultural policy from a socio-historical, political and sociological perspective. Students will examine the role and organizational structure of the arts and major cultural agencies, and discuss social, economic and administrative aspects of professional, amateur, commercial and public art organizations and services. .
Prereq: REC 201 or consent of instructor

courses.label: REC 305
courses.title: Social Psychology of Leisure
paras: A study of the effects of personality and social factors in shaping how people perceive, experience and respond to discretionary time. Current theory and research focusing on the impact of leisure on the socio-psychological adjustment of the individual, and appiications to human problems associated
with leisure will be examined.
Prereq: PSYCH 101 and REC 201
Recreation and Leisure Studies

courses.label: REC 307
courses.title: Social Paychology and Physical Activity
paras: An examination of sport and other forms of physical activities as social situations. Topics such as social facititation, modelling, person perception, expectancies, group structure, unity, motivation, leadership, conformity, and intergroup relations are introduced in relation to motor performance.
Prereq: PSYCH 101
Cross-iisted as KIN 354.

courses.label: REC 310
courses.title: Commercial Recreation Business Development
paras: Students will develop an idea for a small recreation business and will then determine whether or not the idea is feasible. The course emphasizes marketing research, organizational structure, short and long range planning, financial analysis and promotions.
Prereq: REC 210 and BUS 121, or consent of instructor

courses.label: REC 311
courses.title: School Recreation
paras: An analysis of the relationship between recreation and education with particular emphasis on the sponsoring of community recreation programs by education authorities including leisure education and co-curriculurn activities.
Prereq: REC 210

courses.label: REC 312
courses.title: Recreation and Community Action
paras: The rale of the citizen in recreation systems with regard to social change. Students will examine models for social change which interact with recreation systems and power relationships between citizen’s groups and recreation systems.
Prereq. FEC 210

REC'316 F 3C,1L 05 Principles of Recreation Planning An exploration of alternative approaches to the planning of recreation opportunities. The demand for and supply of recreation opportunities; standards, - models and systems; recreation planning policies and agencies; and selected recreation planning issues. Prereq: PLAN 156 or @ full credit in Geography, or consent of instructor

courses.label: REC 317
courses.title: Introduction to Museum Management
paras: Overview of organization and structure of federat, provincial, and local Canadian heritage institutions, ie., museums, art galleries, historic sites, and parks, etc. Examination of staff-personnel functions with respect to policy and program, income and expenditure, microenvironmental issues, computerized information holdings, etc. Laboratory work and field trips.
Prereq: introductory management course, or consent of the instructor

courses.label: REC 320
courses.title: Evaluation of Recreational Programs
paras: Evaluation procedures and techniques applicable to recreation programs are examined in detail. Specification of objectives, development of, practical recording procedures and experimental analysis are stressed. Students conduct field evaluations in local community agencies.
Prereq: REC 270

courses.label: REC 321
courses.title: Selected Topics in Recreation and Leisure Studies

courses.label: REC 331
courses.title: Outdoor Education
paras: The present status of outdoor education in modern society; government functions and policies related to outdoor education services; the planning and administration of outdoor education activities. Current problems.
Prereq: REC 230

courses.label: REC 332
courses.title: Applied Methods in Outdoor
paras: * Recreation
Emphasis on methods and techniques for the selection, development, and implementation of programs and projects through the utilization of diverse and unique natural settings and environments.
Prereq: REC 230

courses.label: REC 334
courses.title: Park Management
paras: Basic administrative procedures in park - management. Operational techniques are examined together with general policies of acquisition, operation and | development. ‘ Prereq: REC 230 and REC 332 Cross-listed as ENV § 334.

courses.label: REC 352
courses.title: Recreation and Mental Retardation
paras: An analysis of the motoric and psychosocial behavioural dimensions specific to the retarded with direct and obvious applicability to the planning, implementing and evaluating of recreational programs.
Prereq: REC 250, PSYCH 312

REC 3583 WS 3C 05 Recreation and Physical Disabilities The psycho-social aspects of physical disabilities will be analysed, with special focus given to the’ planning, implementing and evaluating of leisure activites.

with particular reference to the Leisure
Service Industry. : Prereq: REC 301

courses.title: Statistical Techniques Applied to Leisure Studies
paras: An introduction to descriptive and inferential statistics and the interpretation of data. A major consideration of the course is the use of statistics in the solution of problems in recreation and leisure.

courses.label: REC 372
courses.title: Introduction to Statistical Problem Solving by Computer
paras: ” This is an applications oriented course which, prepares the nonmathematical student to use the computer as a research tool. Topics include aids for statistical analysis and the preparation of documents such as reports and theses. The course provides sufficient background for application to other problems specific to the individual's field.
Prereq: A 1 term statistics course and computer literacy (e.g. CS100 or high schoo! computing)

of market and non-market segmentation.
valuation, and related concepts to
recreation and leisure. Course content is
based on recent research methods and

courses.title: Comparative Recreational Systems
paras: A study of multi-national recreation systerns. Course meets on campus and in the field in other countries. Full term Study over a period of 6-8 weeks. Laboratory fee varies with field observation.

courses.title: Planning of Recreation Facilities
paras: A course to introduce the students to
the planning, design and layout of
recreation areas and facilities. Prereq: REC 210 or consent of
instructor

courses.title: Computer Applications In Leisure Services
paras: Theory and application in leisure service management and programming. Examination of computer impact on leisure service industry.

courses.title: Interpretation

Prereq: REC 332 or consent of instructor

Preraq: REC 334/ENV 334 Cross-listed as ENV S 433.

paras: Management
A study of policies, procedures, and
practices relative to the management of
Natural resources in parks. Emphasis is
placed on an ecological systems
approach to management as it relates
to parks at all levels of government. Prereq: REC 334/ENV S 334 Cross-listed as ENV S 434.

courses.label: REC 435
courses.title: Recreation Resource Policy
paras: A study of policies, policy development and policy gaps related to recreation resources in Canada. Based on a literature review and discussion of decisionmaking procedures, roles and tools used in the recreation field; students are required to research real and theoretical situations for seminar presentation. Prereq: REC 100 and REC 230 or consent of instructor

REC 470 includes an approved design and completion of the first segment of the paper.

paras: Chemistry: The nature of matter, atomic and nuclear reactions, chemical bonds and the formation of molecules.

6 Weeks. . Biology and Biophysics: Biological macromolecules, D.N.A. genetic code, protein synthesis, organic evolution. Photosynthesis, enzymes and A.T-P. Cells, Organelies, specialization, nerve and muscle cells.

courses.label: SCI 205
courses.title: Physics of High Fidelity Sound Reproduction
paras: Applies elementary physical principles to the study of the components of high fidelity systems. Prereq: At least 1 year of Secondary School Physics

paras: Retrieving information and imparting the information you have to others; the art of speaking and writing, modern aids to producing scientific papers, reports, letters, etc,; and common errors in writing.

cl 219 F 2C 05 Chemistry in Modern Society The impact of chemistry on modern society will be considered by discussion of a number of topics including: marijuana and other non-medical drugs; food additives; birth controls; cancer-causing chemicals; pesticides and other chemical methods to control insects; chemical warfare.
